translations.idiomatic: Hearing that his mother was ill, he returned home by a secret route.

sentences.zh: 明亡，益自韜晦。

translations.literal: When Ming fell, he withdrew still further into obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Ming, he withdrew still further into obscurity.

sentences.zh: 歸衡陽之石船山，築土室曰觀生居，晨夕杜門，學者稱船山先生。

translations.literal: He returned to Stone Boat Mountain in Hengyang, built an earthen chamber called the Dwelling for Contemplating Life, and morning and evening kept his doors shut; scholars called him Master Chuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Stone Boat Mountain in Hengyang, built an earthen chamber called the Dwelling for Contemplating Life, kept his doors shut morning and evening, and scholars called him Master Chuanshan.

sentences.zh: 所著書三百二十卷，其著錄於四庫者，曰周易稗疏、考異，尚書稗疏，詩稗疏、考異，春秋稗疏。

translations.literal: The books he wrote numbered three hundred and twenty juan; those recorded in the Siku are: Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Changes and Textual Investigation of Variants, Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Documents, Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Poetry and Textual Investigation of Variants, and Supplementary Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: The books he wrote numbered three hundred and twenty juan; those recorded in the Siku are Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Changes and Textual Investigation of Variants, Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Documents, Supplementary Commentary on the Book of Poetry and Textual Investigation of Variants, and Supplementary Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 存目者，曰尚書引義、春秋家說。

translations.literal: Those listed only in the catalogue are: Elucidation of the Book of Documents and Family Interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Those listed only in the catalogue are Elucidation of the Book of Documents and Family Interpretations of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 夫之論學，以漢儒為門戶，以宋五子為堂奧。

translations.literal: In Fuzhi's approach to learning, he took Han Confucians as the gateway and the Five Masters of Song as the inner sanctum.
translations.idiomatic: In his learning, Fuzhi took Han Confucians as the gateway and the Five Masters of Song as the inner sanctum.

sentences.zh: 其所作大學衍、中庸衍，皆力辟致良知之說，以羽翼朱子。

translations.literal: His works Expounding the Great Learning and Expounding the Doctrine of the Mean both forcefully refute the doctrine of realizing innate moral knowledge in order to support Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His works Expounding the Great Learning and Expounding the Doctrine of the Mean both forcefully refute the doctrine of realizing innate moral knowledge in order to support Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 於張子正蒙一書，尤有神契，謂張子之學，上承孔、孟，而以布衣貞隱，無鉅公資其羽翼；

translations.literal: Regarding Master Zhang's Correcting Obscure Learning, he had a special affinity and said that Master Zhang's learning descended from Confucius and Mencius, yet as a commoner who preserved integrity in reclusion he had no great minister to supply him wings;
translations.idiomatic: Regarding Master Zhang's Correcting Obscure Learning, he had a special affinity and said that Master Zhang's learning descended from Confucius and Mencius, yet as a commoner who preserved integrity in reclusion he had no great minister to supply him wings;

sentences.zh: 其道之行，曾不逮邵康節，是以不百年而異說興。

translations.literal: the spread of his Way did not even reach Shao Kangjie, and so within less than a century heterodox doctrines arose.
translations.idiomatic: the spread of his Way did not even reach Shao Kangjie, and so within less than a century heterodox doctrines arose.

sentences.zh: 夫之乃究觀天人之故，推本陰陽法像之原，就正蒙精繹而暢衍之，與自著思問錄二篇，皆本隱之顯，原始要終，炳然如揭日月。

translations.literal: Fuzhi then thoroughly examined the causes of Heaven and man, traced the origins of yin-yang and symbolic forms, refined and expanded Correcting Obscure Learning, and together with his own two juan of Records of Reflective Inquiry, all reveal the hidden from the manifest, trace beginnings to ends, and shine as clearly as the sun and moon laid bare.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi then examined the causes of Heaven and man, traced yin-yang and symbolic forms to their roots, refined and expanded Correcting Obscure Learning, and together with his own Records of Reflective Inquiry in two juan, all brought the hidden to light from the manifest and traced things from origin to end, shining as clearly as sun and moon unveiled.

sentences.zh: 至其扶樹道教，辨上蔡、象山、姚江之誤，或疑其言稍過，然議論精嚴，粹然皆軌於正也，

translations.literal: As for his upholding the Way of teaching, and his refutation of the errors of Shangcai, Xiangshan, and Yaojiang, some suspected his words went slightly too far, yet his arguments were precise and strict, pure and wholly aligned with the orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: As for his upholding the Way of teaching, and his refutation of the errors of Shangcai, Xiangshan, and Yaojiang, some suspected his words went slightly too far, yet his arguments were precise and strict, pure and wholly aligned with the orthodox.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，吳三桂僭號於衡州，有以勸進表相屬者，夫之曰：「亡國遺臣，所欠一死耳，今安用此不祥之人哉！」

translations.literal: In Kangxi year eighteen, Wu Sangui usurped the title at Hengzhou; when someone entrusted him with a memorial urging enthronement, Fuzhi said: "A remnant minister of a fallen state owes nothing but one death—what use have I now for this inauspicious man?"
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year eighteen, Wu Sangui usurped the title at Hengzhou; when someone entrusted him with a memorial urging enthronement, Fuzhi said: "A remnant minister of a fallen state owes nothing but one death—what use have I now for this inauspicious man?"

sentences.zh: 遂逃入深山，作祓禊賦以示意。

translations.literal: He then fled into the deep mountains and wrote the Purification Rhapsody to make his meaning clear.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled into the deep mountains and wrote the Purification Rhapsody to make his meaning clear.

sentences.zh: 三桂平，大吏聞而嘉之，囑郡守餽粟帛，請見，夫之以疾辭。

translations.literal: When Sangui was suppressed, high officials heard of this and praised it, instructing the prefect to send grain and silk and requesting an audience; Fuzhi declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui was suppressed, high officials heard of this and praised it, instructing the prefect to send grain and silk and requesting an audience; Fuzhi declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，葬大樂山之高節裡，自題墓碣曰「明遺臣王某之墓」。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was buried at Gaojie Village on Mount Dale; he inscribed his own tomb epitaph: "Tomb of Wang, remnant minister of Ming."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died and was buried at Gaojie Village on Mount Dale, inscribing his own tomb epitaph: "Tomb of Wang, remnant minister of Ming."

sentences.zh: 當是時，海內碩儒，推容城、盩厔、餘姚、崑山。

translations.literal: At that time the leading scholars within the seas were held to be those of Rongcheng, Zhouzhi, Yuyao, and Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the leading scholars under Heaven were held to be those of Rongcheng, Zhouzhi, Yuyao, and Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 夫之刻苦似二曲，貞晦過夏峰，多聞博學，志節皎然，不愧黃、顧兩君子。

translations.literal: Fuzhi's austerity resembled Erqu; his reclusive integrity surpassed Xiafeng; he was broadly learned and widely informed, his integrity and resolve bright and clear—he did not disgrace the two gentlemen Huang and Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi's austerity resembled Erqu, his reclusive integrity surpassed Xiafeng; broadly learned and resolute in integrity, he did not disgrace the two gentlemen Huang and Gu.

sentences.zh: 然諸人肥遯自甘，聲望益炳，雖薦辟皆以死拒，而公卿交口，天子動容，其著述易行於世。

translations.literal: Yet those men fattened themselves in lofty reclusion and grew ever more illustrious in reputation; though recommendations and summons were all refused unto death, officials spoke of them with one voice and the Son of Heaven was moved, and their writings spread easily in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those men fattened themselves in lofty reclusion and grew ever more illustrious in reputation; though recommendations and summons were all refused unto death, officials spoke of them with one voice and the Son of Heaven was moved, and their writings spread easily in the world.

sentences.zh: 惟夫之竄身瑤峒，聲影不出林莽，遂得完發以歿身。

translations.literal: Only Fuzhi hid himself in the Yao grottoes; his voice and shadow did not emerge from forest and thicket, and so he was able to die with his hair intact.
translations.idiomatic: Only Fuzhi hid in the Yao grottoes; his voice and shadow never left the forest, and so he died with his hair intact.

sentences.zh: 後四十年，其子敔抱遺書上之督學宜興潘宗洛，因緣得入四庫，上史館，立傳儒林，而其書仍不傳，

translations.literal: Forty years later, his son Yin brought the surviving books and presented them to educational intendant Pan Zongluo of Yixing; by this connection they entered the Siku, were sent to the History Bureau, and a Ru lin biography was established, yet his books still did not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years later, his son Yin brought the surviving books and presented them to educational intendant Pan Zongluo of Yixing; by this connection they entered the Siku, were sent to the History Bureau, and a Ru lin biography was established, yet his books still did not circulate.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，曾國荃刻於江南，海內學者始得見其全書焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi, Zeng Guoquan printed them in Jiangnan, and scholars throughout the realm at last obtained his complete works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi, Zeng Guoquan printed the works in Jiangnan, and scholars throughout the realm at last saw his complete writings.

sentences.zh: 兄介之，字石子。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jiezhi, courtesy name Shizi.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jiezhi, courtesy name Shizi.

sentences.zh: 國變，隱不出。

translations.literal: When the dynasty changed, he went into reclusion and did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty changed, he went into reclusion and did not emerge.

sentences.zh: 先夫之卒。

translations.literal: He died before Fuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He died before Fuzhi.

sentences.zh: 李顒，字中孚，盩厔人。

translations.literal: Li Yong, courtesy name Zhongfu, was a native of Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 又字二曲，二曲者，水曲曰盩，山曲曰厔也。

translations.literal: He also styled himself Erqu; Erqu means that where water bends is zhou and where mountains bend is zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also styled himself Erqu; Erqu means that where water bends is zhou and where mountains bend is zhi.

sentences.zh: 布衣安貧，以理學倡導關中，關中士子多宗之。

translations.literal: A commoner who was content in poverty, he took Neo-Confucian learning as his banner to lead Guanzhong, and many Guanzhong scholars looked to him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner content in poverty, he led Guanzhong through Neo-Confucian teaching, and many scholars there took him as their master.

sentences.zh: 父可從，為明材官，

translations.literal: His father Kecong was a Ming military officer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kecong was a Ming military officer.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年，張獻忠寇鄖西，巡撫汪喬年總督軍務，可從隨征討賊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong raided western Yun; Governor Wang Qiaonian directed military affairs, and Kecong followed the campaign to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong raided western Yun; Governor Wang Qiaonian directed military affairs, and Kecong followed the campaign to suppress the bandits.

sentences.zh: 臨行，抉一齒與顒母曰：「如不捷，吾當委骨沙場。

translations.literal: Before departing, he extracted a tooth and gave it to Yong's mother, saying: "If I am not victorious, I shall leave my bones on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing, he extracted a tooth and gave it to Yong's mother, saying: "If I am not victorious, I shall leave my bones on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 子善教吾兒矣。」

translations.literal: You will kindly teach my son."
translations.idiomatic: You will kindly teach my son."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He then set out.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，死之。

translations.literal: The army was defeated and he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated and he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 顒母葬其齒，曰「齒塚」。

translations.literal: Yong's mother buried the tooth and called the mound the Tooth Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's mother buried the tooth and called the mound the Tooth Tomb.

sentences.zh: 時顒年十六，母彭氏，日言忠孝節義以督之，顒亦事母孝。

translations.literal: At the time Yong was sixteen; his mother was the Lady Peng, who daily spoke of loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness to admonish him, and Yong also served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yong was sixteen; his mother was the Lady Peng, who daily spoke of loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and righteousness to admonish him, and Yong also served his mother filially.

sentences.zh: 飢寒清苦，無所憑藉，而自拔流俗，以昌明關學為己任。

translations.literal: Hungry, cold, and in bitter poverty, with nothing to rely upon, he yet lifted himself above the vulgar current and took reviving Guan learning as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Though hungry, cold, and without support, he lifted himself above the vulgar world and made reviving Guan learning his personal charge.

sentences.zh: 有餽遺者，雖十反不受。

translations.literal: When gifts were offered, even if sent ten times he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When gifts were offered, even if sent ten times he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「交道接禮，孟子不卻。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "In social intercourse one receives courtesy; Mencius did not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "In social intercourse one receives courtesy; Mencius did not refuse."

sentences.zh: 顒曰：「我輩百不能學孟子，即此一事不守孟子家法，正自無害。」

translations.literal: Yong said: "We are in a hundred ways unable to learn from Mencius; if in this one matter we do not keep to Mencius's household rule, that in itself does no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: "We are in a hundred ways unable to learn from Mencius; if in this one matter we do not keep to Mencius's household rule, that in itself does no harm."

sentences.zh: 先是顒聞父喪，欲之襄城求遺骸，以母老不可一日離，乃止。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yong heard of his father's death, he wished to go to Xiangcheng to seek the remains, but because his mother was old and could not be parted from even for a day, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yong heard of his father's death, he wished to go to Xiangcheng to seek the remains, but because his mother was old and could not be parted from even for a day, he stopped.

sentences.zh: 既丁母憂，廬墓三年，乃徒步之襄城，覓遺骸，不得，服斬衰晝夜哭。

translations.literal: After he completed mourning for his mother and dwelt at her tomb for three years, he went on foot to Xiangcheng to search for the remains; failing to find them, he wore the coarsest mourning and wept day and night.
translations.idiomatic: After he completed mourning for his mother and dwelt at her tomb for three years, he went on foot to Xiangcheng to search for the remains; failing to find them, he wore the coarsest mourning and wept day and night.

sentences.zh: 知縣張允中為其父立祠，且造塚於戰場，名之曰「義林」。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhang Yunzhong built a shrine for his father and also made a tomb on the battlefield, naming it the Righteous Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhang Yunzhong built a shrine for his father and also made a tomb on the battlefield, naming it the Righteous Grove.

sentences.zh: 常州知府駱鍾麟嘗師事顒，謂祠未能旦夕竣，請南下謁道南書院，且講學以慰學者之望，顒赴之，凡講於無錫，於江陰，於靖江、宜興，所至學者雲集。

translations.literal: Changzhou prefect Luo Zhonglin had once studied under Yong; he said the shrine could not be finished overnight and asked Yong to go south to visit Daonan Academy and also lecture to satisfy the scholars' hopes; Yong went, lecturing at Wuxi, Jiangyin, Jingjiang, and Yixing, and wherever he went scholars gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Luo Zhonglin, who had studied under Yong, said the shrine could not be finished at once and asked Yong to go south to Daonan Academy and lecture to satisfy the scholars' hopes; Yong went, lecturing at Wuxi, Jiangyin, Jingjiang, and Yixing, and wherever he went scholars gathered in crowds.

sentences.zh: 既而幡悔曰：「不孝！

translations.literal: Then he suddenly repented and said: "Unfilial!
translations.idiomatic: Then he suddenly repented and said: "Unfilial!

sentences.zh: 汝此行何事，而喋喋於此？」

translations.literal: What business did you come on this journey for, yet you chatter on about this?"
translations.idiomatic: What business did you come on this journey for, yet you chatter on about this?"

sentences.zh: 即戒行赴襄城。

translations.literal: He immediately prepared to leave for Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately prepared to leave for Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 常州人士思慕之，為肖像於延陵書院。

translations.literal: The people of Changzhou admired him and had his portrait placed in Yanling Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Changzhou admired him and placed his portrait in Yanling Academy.

sentences.zh: 顒既至襄城，適祠成，乃哭祭招魂，取塚土西歸附諸墓，持服如初喪。

translations.literal: When Yong had arrived at Xiangcheng, the shrine happened to be completed; he then wept and performed a sacrifice to summon the soul, took earth from the tomb mound and returned west to place it beside the other graves, and wore mourning garments as at the first bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong reached Xiangcheng, the shrine had just been completed. He wept and performed a soul-summoning sacrifice, took soil from the battlefield tomb and carried it west to place beside the family graves, and wore mourning dress as though for a fresh bereavement.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，薦舉博學鴻儒，稱疾篤，舁床至省，水漿不入口，乃得予假。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi, when he was recommended for the Broad Learning and Eminent Confucian examination, he pleaded grave illness; he was carried on a bed to the provincial seat and took neither water nor gruel, and only then was granted leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi, when he was recommended for the Broad Learning and Eminent Confucian examination, he pleaded grave illness; he was carried on a bed to the provincial seat and took neither water nor gruel, and only then was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 自是閉關，晏息土室，惟崑山顧炎武至則款之。

translations.literal: From then on he shut his gate and rested quietly in an earthen chamber; only when Gu Yanwu of Kunshan came did he receive him warmly.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he shut his gate and rested quietly in an earthen chamber; only when Gu Yanwu of Kunshan came did he receive him warmly.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，聖祖西巡，召顒見，時顒已衰老，遣子慎言詣行在陳情，以所著四書反身錄、二曲集奏進。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when Shengzu made a western tour and summoned Yong to an audience, Yong was already old and weak, so he sent his son Shenyan to the traveling palace to explain his circumstances and submit his works Four Books Record of Self-Reflection and Erqu Collection.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, when Shengzu made a western tour and summoned Yong to an audience, Yong was already old and weak, so he sent his son Shenyan to the traveling palace to explain his circumstances and submit his works Four Books Record of Self-Reflection and Erqu Collection.

sentences.zh: 上特賜御書「操志高潔」以獎之。

translations.literal: The emperor specially bestowed the imperial inscription “Conduct and Aspiration Pure and Lofty” to commend him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor specially bestowed the imperial inscription “Conduct and Aspiration Pure and Lofty” to commend him.

sentences.zh: 顒謂：「孔、曾、思、孟，立言垂訓，以成四書，蓋欲學者體諸身，見諸行。

translations.literal: Yong said: “Confucius, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius established words and left teachings, making the Four Books, because they wished learners to embody them in themselves and show them in action.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said: “Confucius, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius established words and left teachings, making the Four Books, because they wished learners to embody them in themselves and show them in action.

sentences.zh: 充之為天德，達之為王道，有體有用，有補於世。

translations.literal: When fulfilled, they become heavenly virtue; when extended, they become the kingly way. They have substance and function, and they benefit the world.
translations.idiomatic: When fulfilled, they become heavenly virtue; when extended, they become the kingly way. They have substance and function, and they benefit the world.

sentences.zh: 否則假途幹進，於世無補，夫豈聖賢立言之初心，國家期望之本意耶？」

translations.literal: Otherwise one merely borrows the path to seek advancement and brings no benefit to the world. How could that be the original intention with which the sages and worthies set down their words, or the true purpose of the state’s expectations?”
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise one merely borrows the path to seek advancement and brings no benefit to the world. How could that be the original intention with which the sages and worthies set down their words, or the true purpose of the state’s expectations?”

sentences.zh: 居恆教人，一以反身實踐為事，門人錄之，為七卷。

translations.literal: In ordinary teaching he made self-reflection and practical enactment his sole concern; his disciples recorded this in seven juan.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary teaching he made self-reflection and practical enactment his sole concern; his disciples recorded this in seven juan.

sentences.zh: 是時容城孫奇逢之學盛於北，餘姚黃宗羲之學盛於南，與顒鼎足稱三大儒。

translations.literal: At this time Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng’s learning flourished in the north and Huang Zongxi of Yuyao’s learning flourished in the south; together with Yong they stood like the three legs of a tripod and were called the Three Great Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng’s learning flourished in the north and Huang Zongxi of Yuyao’s learning flourished in the south; together with Yong they stood like the three legs of a tripod and were called the Three Great Confucians.

sentences.zh: 晚年寓富平，關中儒者咸稱「三李」。

translations.literal: In his later years he lodged in Fuping, and the Confucians of Guanzhong all spoke of the “Three Lis.”
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he lodged in Fuping, and the Confucians of Guanzhong all spoke of the “Three Lis.”

sentences.zh: 三李者，顒及富平李因篤、郿李柏也。

translations.literal: The Three Lis were Yong, Li Yindu of Fuping, and Li Bai of Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Lis were Yong, Li Yindu of Fuping, and Li Bai of Mei.

sentences.zh: 李因篤，字天生，富平人。

translations.literal: Li Yindu, courtesy name Tiansheng, was a native of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yindu, styled Tiansheng, was from Fuping.

sentences.zh: 明庠生。

translations.literal: A Ming county-school student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a county-school student under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，貫串注疏。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a strong memory, he mastered commentaries and subcommentaries through and through.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and possessed of a formidable memory, he had mastered the commentarial tradition from end to end.

sentences.zh: 舉博學鴻儒，試授檢討。

translations.literal: Recommended as a Broad Learning and Eminent Confucian, he was appointed Examining Editor upon examination.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a Broad Learning and Eminent Confucian, he passed the examination and was appointed Examining Editor.

sentences.zh: 未踰月，以母老乞養，詔許之。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed, because his mother was old he requested leave to support her, and the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he petitioned to retire and care for his aged mother, and the throne granted his request.

sentences.zh: 母歿，仍不出。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he still did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, he still did not take office.

sentences.zh: 因篤深於經學，著詩說，顧炎武稱之曰：「毛、鄭有嗣音矣！」

translations.literal: Yindu was deeply versed in classical learning and wrote Expositions on the Odes; Gu Yanwu praised it, saying: "Mao and Zheng have a successor in sound!
translations.idiomatic: Yindu was deeply versed in classical learning and wrote Expositions on the Odes. Gu Yanwu praised it, saying: "Mao and Zheng have found a worthy successor!

sentences.zh: 又著春秋說，汪琬亦折服焉。

translations.literal: He also wrote Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals, and Wang Wan was likewise won over.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Expositions on the Spring and Autumn Annals, which likewise won over Wang Wan.

sentences.zh: 李柏，字雪木，郿縣人。

translations.literal: Li Bai, courtesy name Xuemu, was a native of Mei County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bai, styled Xuemu, was from Mei County.

sentences.zh: 九歲失怙，事母至孝。

translations.literal: At nine he lost his father and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at nine and served his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 稍長，讀小學，曰：「道在是矣！」

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older and read the Elementary Learning, he said: "The Way is here!
translations.idiomatic: When he was a little older he read the Elementary Learning and said: "Here is the Way!

sentences.zh: 遂盡焚帖括，而日誦古書。

translations.literal: He then burned all his examination essays and daily recited ancient books.
translations.idiomatic: He then burned all his examination essays and devoted himself to reciting the classics each day.

sentences.zh: 避荒居洋縣，入山屏跡讀書者數十年。

translations.literal: Fleeing famine he lived in Yang County, entering the mountains and hiding his traces to read books for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing famine, he settled in Yang County and spent decades in the mountains, living in seclusion and reading.

sentences.zh: 嘗一日兩粥，或半月食無鹽。

translations.literal: He sometimes had two bowls of gruel in a day, or went half a month without salt in his food.
translations.idiomatic: At times he ate only two bowls of gruel a day; at other times he went half a month without tasting salt.

sentences.zh: 時時忍飢默坐，間臨水把釣，夷然不屑也。

translations.literal: He would often endure hunger and sit in silence; occasionally he fished by the water, utterly indifferent and disdainful of the world.
translations.idiomatic: He often endured hunger in silent meditation; now and then he fished by the water, utterly detached and indifferent to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 昕夕謳吟，拾山中樹葉書之。

translations.literal: Morning and evening he chanted in song, writing his verses on tree leaves gathered in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he composed and sang poetry, writing his verses on oak leaves gathered in Qinshan.

sentences.zh: 門人都其集曰槲葉集。

translations.literal: His disciples collected his works and called the collection Oak Leaf Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples collected his writings under the title Oak Leaf Collection.

sentences.zh: 年六十六，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-six, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 王心敬，字爾緝，鄠縣人，

translations.literal: Wang Xinjing, courtesy name Erji, was a native of Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xinjing, styled Erji, was a native of Hu County.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was recommended as Xiaolian Fangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, of the Qianlong reign, he was recommended as Xiaolian Fangzheng.

sentences.zh: 心敬論學，以明、新、止至善為歸。

translations.literal: In discussing learning, Xinjing took illumination, renewal, and reaching utmost goodness as his goal.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching, Xinjing took illumination, renewal, and reaching utmost goodness as his guiding the Way.

sentences.zh: 謹嚴不逮其師，注經好為異論，而易說為篤實。

translations.literal: In strictness and rigor he did not match his teacher; in annotating the classics he liked to put forward unusual views, but his commentary on the Changes was solid and practical.
translations.idiomatic: He was less rigorous than his teacher; in annotating the classics he favored unconventional views, but his commentary on the Changes was solid and practical.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「學易可以無大過矣，是孔子論易，切於人身，即可知四聖之本旨。」

translations.literal: He said: "Study the Changes and you can avoid great faults—this is Confucius's discussion of the Changes, close to the person, and from it one can know the original intent of the Four Sages.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Study the Changes and you can avoid great faults—this is how Confucius spoke of the Changes, in terms close to human life, and from it one can grasp the original intent of the Four Sages.

sentences.zh: 著有豐川集、關學編、豐川易說。

translations.literal: He wrote Fengchuan Collection, Records of Guan Learning, and Fengchuan's Exposition on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Fengchuan Collection, Records of Guan Learning, and Fengchuan's Exposition on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 沈國模，字求如，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Shen Guomo, courtesy name Qiuru, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Guomo, styled Qiuru, was from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming county student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a county student under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 餘姚自王守仁講致良知之學，弟子遍天下。

translations.literal: Since Wang Shouren lectured on the learning of extending innate moral knowledge, Yuyao's disciples spread throughout the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Wang Shouren taught the doctrine of extending innate moral knowledge, disciples from Yuyao spread throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 同邑傳其學者，推徐愛、錢德洪、胡瀚、聞人詮，再傳而得國模。

translations.literal: Among those of the same county who transmitted his learning, Xu Ai, Qian Dehong, Hu Han, and Wenren Quan were foremost; through a second transmission Guomo received it.
translations.idiomatic: Among those of his county who transmitted the teaching, Xu Ai, Qian Dehong, Hu Han, and Wenren Quan were foremost; Guomo received it through a second generation of transmission.

sentences.zh: 少以明道為己任。

translations.literal: From youth he took making the Way manifest as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he made it his mission to bring the Way to light.

sentences.zh: 嘗預劉宗周證人講會，歸而辟姚江書院，與同里管宗聖、史孝咸輩，講明良知之說。

translations.literal: He once participated in Liu Zongzhou's Zhengren lecture assembly; returning, he established Yaojiang Academy and, with fellow townsman Guan Zongsheng, Shi Xiaoxian, and others, expounded the doctrine of innate moral knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He once joined Liu Zongzhou's Zhengren lecture assembly; on returning home he founded Yaojiang Academy and, with fellow townsman Guan Zongsheng, Shi Xiaoxian, and others, expounded the doctrine of innate moral knowledge.

sentences.zh: 其所學或以為近禪，而言行敦潔，較然不欺其志，故推純儒。

translations.literal: Some considered his learning close to Chan, but his words and conduct were earnest and pure, clearly not betraying his purpose; therefore he was acclaimed a pure Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Some considered his teaching close to Chan Buddhism, but his words and conduct were earnest and pure and clearly never betrayed his purpose, so he was acclaimed a pure Confucian.

sentences.zh: 山陰祁彪佳以御史按江東，一日，杖殺大憝數人，適國模至，欣然述之。

translations.literal: Qi Biaojia of Shanyin, as censor inspecting Jiangdong, one day had several great villains beaten to death; Guomo happened to arrive and Qi happily recounted it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Biaojia of Shanyin, while serving as censor inspecting Jiangdong, one day had several notorious criminals beaten to death; Guomo happened to arrive, and Qi happily recounted the affair.

sentences.zh: 國模瞠目字祁曰：「世培，爾亦曾聞曾子曰『如得其情，則哀矜而勿喜』乎？」

translations.literal: Guomo stared wide-eyed and addressed Qi by his given name, saying: "Shipei, have you ever heard Zengzi's words, 'If you obtain the facts of the case, show pity and do not rejoice'?
translations.idiomatic: Guomo stared at him in shock and addressed Qi by his given name: "Shipei, have you ever heard what Zengzi said—'If you obtain the facts of the case, show pity and do not rejoice'?

sentences.zh: 後彪佳嘗語人曰：「吾每慮囚，必念求如言。

translations.literal: Later Biaojia often told people: "Whenever I examine prisoners, I always recall Qiuru's words.
translations.idiomatic: Later Biaojia often told people: "Whenever I examine prisoners, I always recall what Qiuru said.

sentences.zh: 恐倉卒喜怒過差，負此良友也。」

translations.literal: I fear that in haste my joy or anger may exceed the mark and fail this good friend."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in haste my joy or anger may go too far and betray this good friend."

sentences.zh: 明亡，聞宗周死節，為位哭之痛，已而講學益勤，

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, hearing that Zongzhou had died maintaining his integrity, he set up a mourning seat and wept bitterly; thereafter he lectured with even greater diligence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, upon hearing that Zongzhou had died maintaining his integrity, he set up a mourning seat and wept bitterly; thereafter he lectured with even greater diligence.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, he died at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi, he died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 孝咸，字子虛。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian, courtesy name Zixu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiaoxian, styled Zixu.

sentences.zh: 繼國模主姚江書院。

translations.literal: He succeeded Guomo in presiding over Yaojiang Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Guomo as head of Yaojiang Academy.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「良知非致不真。」

translations.literal: He once said: "Innate moral knowledge, if not extended, is not true."
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Innate moral knowledge is not genuine unless it is extended into action."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「空談易，對境難。

translations.literal: He also said: "Empty talk is easy; facing real circumstances is hard.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Empty talk is easy; meeting real circumstances is hard.

sentences.zh: 於『居處恭，執事敬，與人忠』三語，精察而力行之，其庶幾乎！」

translations.literal: On the three phrases 'be respectful in dwelling, reverent in handling affairs, and loyal toward others,' examine them closely and put them forcefully into practice—perhaps one may come close!"
translations.idiomatic: If one closely examines and earnestly practices the three phrases 'be respectful in dwelling, reverent in handling affairs, and loyal toward others,' one may come close to the mark!"

sentences.zh: 家貧，日食一粥，泊如也，

translations.literal: His family was poor; he ate one bowl of gruel a day and was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he ate only one bowl of gruel a day and remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，卒，年七十有八。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, he died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 韓當，字仁父。

translations.literal: Han Dang, courtesy name Renfu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dang, styled Renfu.

sentences.zh: 國模弟子。

translations.literal: A disciple of Guomo.
translations.idiomatic: He was a disciple of Guomo.

sentences.zh: 自沈、史歿後，書院輟講垂十年，而當繼之。

translations.literal: After Shen and Shi died, the academy ceased lecturing for nearly ten years, and Dang succeeded them.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen and Shi died, the academy ceased lecturing for nearly ten years until Dang took it up again.

sentences.zh: 其學兼綜諸儒，以名教經世，嚴於儒、佛之辨。

translations.literal: His learning synthesized various Confucians, took name and teaching to order the world, and was strict in distinguishing Confucianism from Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: His learning synthesized various Confucian traditions, took moral teaching as the means to order the world, and was strict in distinguishing Confucianism from Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 家貧，未嘗向人稱貸。

translations.literal: His family was poor, yet he never borrowed from others.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor, he never borrowed money from others.

sentences.zh: 每言立身須自節用始。

translations.literal: He often said that establishing oneself must begin with self-restraint in expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He often said that establishing oneself must begin with frugality.

sentences.zh: 人有過，於講學時以危言動之，而不明言其過。

translations.literal: When someone had faults, at lecture he would stir them with stern words without explicitly naming the fault.
translations.idiomatic: When someone had faults, he would stir them with stern words during lectures without explicitly naming the fault.

sentences.zh: 聞者內愧沾汗，退而相語曰：「比從韓先生來，不覺自失。」

translations.literal: Those who heard felt inward shame and broke into sweat; withdrawing they said to one another: "Since coming from Master Han, one cannot help feeling oneself at fault."
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard felt inward shame and broke into a sweat; afterward they would say to one another: "Since coming from Master Han, one cannot help feeling oneself at fault."

sentences.zh: 疾亟，謂弟子曰：「吾於文成宗旨，覺有新得。

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, he told his disciples: "In Wencheng's essential teaching I feel I have gained something new.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical, he told his disciples: "In Wencheng's essential teaching I feel I have gained something new.

sentences.zh: 然檢點於心，終無受用，小子識之！」

translations.literal: Yet when I examine my heart, in the end there is nothing I can use—remember this, young men!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet when I examine my heart, in the end nothing has truly taken hold—remember this, young men!"

sentences.zh: 味其言，則知其學守仁之外，亦近朱子矣。

translations.literal: Savoring his words, one knows that beyond Shouren his learning also approached Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Reading between the lines of his words, one sees that beyond Shouren his teaching also drew close to Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 邵曾可，字子唯。

translations.literal: Shao Cengke, courtesy name Ziwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Cengke, styled Ziwei.

sentences.zh: 與韓當同時。

translations.literal: Contemporary with Han Dang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a contemporary of Han Dang.

sentences.zh: 性孝友愷悌。

translations.literal: By nature filial, friendly, and gentle.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was filial, friendly, and gentle.

sentences.zh: 少愛書畫，一日讀孟子「伯夷聖之清者也」句，忽有悟，悉棄去，壹志於學。

translations.literal: In youth he loved calligraphy and painting; one day reading in Mencius the line 'Boyi was the pure one among sages,' he suddenly had an awakening, cast them all aside, and devoted himself wholly to learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved calligraphy and painting; one day, reading in Mencius the line 'Boyi was the pure one among sages,' he suddenly awakened, cast them all aside, and devoted himself wholly to learning.

sentences.zh: 姚江書院初立時，人頗迂笑之。

translations.literal: When Yaojiang Academy was first established, people rather ridiculed it as pedantic.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaojiang Academy was first established, many ridiculed it as pedantic.

sentences.zh: 曾可厲色曰：「不如是，便虛度此生。」

translations.literal: Cengke said sternly: "If not thus, one simply wastes this life."
translations.idiomatic: Cengke said sternly: "Otherwise one simply wastes this life."

sentences.zh: 遂往學。

translations.literal: He then went to study there.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to study there.

sentences.zh: 其初以主敬為宗，自師孝咸之後，專守良知。

translations.literal: At first he took reverence as his principle; after taking Xiaoxian as his teacher, he devoted himself solely to innate moral knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: At first he took reverence as his principle; after becoming Xiaoxian's disciple, he devoted himself solely to innate moral knowledge.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「於今乃知知之不可以已。

translations.literal: He once said: "Only now do I know that knowing cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Only now do I understand that knowing cannot cease.

sentences.zh: 日月有明，容光必照。

translations.literal: The sun and moon have brightness; reflected light must shine.
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon have light; wherever light falls, it must shine.

sentences.zh: 不爾，日用跬步，鮮不貿貿者矣。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, in daily steps one is scarcely not confused and ignorant.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, in one's daily steps one is scarcely ever free of confusion and blindness.

sentences.zh: 孝咸病，晨走十餘里叩床下問疾，不食而返。

translations.literal: When Xiaoxian fell ill, each morning he walked more than ten li to kneel at the bedside and inquire after his illness, then returned without eating.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoxian fell ill, each morning he walked more than ten li to kneel at his bedside and inquire after him, then returned without eating.

sentences.zh: 如是月餘，亦病。

translations.literal: Thus for more than a month, he too fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month of this, he too fell ill.

sentences.zh: 同儕共推為篤行之士焉。

translations.literal: His peers together acclaimed him a man of earnest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His peers unanimously acclaimed him a man of earnest conduct.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十有一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 曾可子貞顯，貞顯子廷採，世其學。

translations.literal: Cengke's son was Zhenxian, and Zhenxian's son was Tingcai; they inherited his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Cengke's son was Zhenxian, and Zhenxian's son was Tingcai; they carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 廷採，字允斯，又字念魯。

translations.literal: Tingcai, courtesy name Yunci, also styled Nianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingcai, styled Yunci and also known as Nianlu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 從韓當受業，又問學於黃宗羲。

translations.literal: He studied under Han Dang and also sought learning from Huang Zongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Han Dang and also sought instruction from Huang Zongxi.

sentences.zh: 初讀傳習錄無所得，既讀劉宗周人譜，曰：「吾知王氏學所始事矣。」

translations.literal: At first reading Records of Practice and Inquiry he gained nothing; after reading Liu Zongzhou's Chart of Man, he said: "Now I know what Wang's learning begins with."
translations.idiomatic: At first he gained nothing from reading Records of Practice and Inquiry; after reading Liu Zongzhou's Chart of Man, he said: "Now I know what Wang's learning truly begins with."

sentences.zh: 蠡縣李塨貽廷採書，論明儒異同，兼問所學。

translations.literal: Li Gong of Li County sent Tingcai a letter-spacing tasking him with discussing the agreements and differences among Ming Confucians and also asking about his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong of Li County wrote to Tingcai, discussing the agreements and differences among Ming Confucians and also inquiring about his learning.

sentences.zh: 廷採曰：「致良知者主誠意，陽明而後，原學蕺山。」

translations.literal: Tingcai said: "Extending innate moral knowledge takes sincere intent as its master; after Yangming, one should trace the learning back to Jishan."
translations.idiomatic: Tingcai replied: "Extending innate moral knowledge takes sincere intent as its foundation; after Yangming, one should trace the learning back to Jishan."

sentences.zh: 又私念師友淵源，思託著述以自見。

translations.literal: He also privately reflected on the deep sources of teachers and friends and thought to entrust himself to writing to make himself known.
translations.idiomatic: He also privately reflected on the deep lineage of teachers and friends and resolved to make himself known through writing.

sentences.zh: 以為陽明扶世翼教，作王子傳；

translations.literal: Thinking that Yangming supported the age and aided instruction, he wrote a biography of the Prince;
translations.idiomatic: Believing that Yangming had supported the age and aided instruction, he wrote a biography of the Prince;

sentences.zh: 蕺山功主慎獨，作劉子傳；

translations.literal: Jishan's merit lay in emphasizing vigilance in solitude, so he wrote a biography of Master Liu;
translations.idiomatic: Since Jishan's merit lay in emphasizing vigilance in solitude, he wrote a biography of Master Liu;

sentences.zh: 王學盛行，務使合乎準則，作王門弟子傳；

translations.literal: Wang learning was widespread; to make it conform to standards, he wrote biographies of Wang's disciples;
translations.idiomatic: As Wang learning was widespread, he wrote biographies of Wang's disciples to bring it into line with proper standards;

sentences.zh: 金鉉、祁彪佳等能守師說，作劉門弟子傳，

translations.literal: Jin Xuan, Qi Biaojia, and others were able to preserve their teacher's doctrine, so he wrote biographies of Liu's disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xuan, Qi Biaojia, and others were able to preserve their teacher's doctrine, so he wrote biographies of Liu's disciples.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the 50 year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the 50 year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 王朝式，字金如，山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Chaoshi, courtesy name Jinru, was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chaoshi, styled Jinru, was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 亦國模弟子。

translations.literal: Also a disciple of Guomo.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a disciple of Guomo.

sentences.zh: 嘗入證人社，宗周主誠意，朝式守致知。

translations.literal: He once entered the Zhengren Society; Zongzhou upheld sincere intent, while Chaoshi upheld extending knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He once joined the Zhengren Society; Zongzhou upheld sincere intent, while Chaoshi upheld extending knowledge.

sentences.zh: 曰：「學不從良知入，必有誠非所誠之蔽。」

translations.literal: He said: "Learning that does not enter through innate moral knowledge must have the obscuring defect of sincerity that is not truly sincere."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Learning that does not begin with innate moral knowledge must suffer the defect of a sincerity that is not truly sincere."

sentences.zh: 亦篤論也。

translations.literal: This too was earnest doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: This too was sound and earnest doctrine.

sentences.zh: 順治初，卒，年三十有八。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi reign, he died at the age of thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shunzhi reign he died at the age of thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 謝文洊，字秋水，南豐人。

translations.literal: Xie Wenjian, courtesy name Qiushui, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wenjian, styled Qiushui, was from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming county student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a county student under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，入廣昌之香山，閱佛書，學禪。

translations.literal: At a little over twenty he entered Xiangshan in Guangchang, read Buddhist books, and studied Chan.
translations.idiomatic: At a little over twenty he went to Xiangshan in Guangchang, read Buddhist texts, and studied Chan.

sentences.zh: 既，讀龍溪王氏書，遂與友講陽明之學。

translations.literal: Thereafter, reading the writings of Longxi Wang, he then with friends lectured on Yangming's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after reading the writings of Wang Longxi, he and his friends began lecturing on Yangming's teaching.

sentences.zh: 年四十，會講於新城之神童峰。

translations.literal: At forty he held a joint lecture at the Divine Child Peak in Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he held a joint lecture at the Divine Child Peak in Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 有王聖瑞者，力攻陽明。

translations.literal: There was one Wang Shengrui who forcefully attacked Yangming.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Shengrui forcefully attacked Yangming's teaching.

sentences.zh: 文洊與爭辯累日，為所動，取羅欽順困知記讀之，始一意程、朱。

translations.literal: Wenjian debated with him for many days, was moved by him, took Luo Qinshun's Records of Knowledge Through Adversity to read, and then devoted himself solely to the Cheng and Zhu school.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjian debated with him for many days, was swayed by his arguments, read Luo Qinshun's Records of Knowledge Through Adversity, and then devoted himself solely to the Cheng and Zhu school.

sentences.zh: 辟程山學舍於城西，名其堂曰尊雒。

translations.literal: He established Chengnan Academy west of the city and named its hall Reverence for Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He established Chengnan Academy west of the city and named its hall Reverence for Luo.

sentences.zh: 著大學中庸切已錄，發明張子主敬之旨。

translations.literal: He wrote Records of Self-Application to the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, elucidating Master Zhang's principle of upholding reverence.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Self-Application to the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, elucidating Master Zhang's principle of upholding reverence.

sentences.zh: 以為為學之本，「畏天命」一言盡之，學者當以此為心法。

translations.literal: He held that the root of learning is fully expressed in the single phrase 'stand in awe of Heaven's decree,' and scholars should take this as the method of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the foundation of learning is fully captured in the phrase 'stand in awe of Heaven's decree,' and that scholars should take this as the method of the heart.

sentences.zh: 注目傾耳，一念之私，醒悔刻責，無犯帝天之怒。

translations.literal: Fix the eyes and incline the ears; if a single thought is selfish, awaken, repent, and reprove oneself severely, and do not incur the wrath of the August Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the eyes fixed and the ears attentive; at the slightest selfish thought, wake, repent, and reprove oneself sternly, lest one provoke the wrath of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其程山十則亦以躬行實踐為主。

translations.literal: His Ten Principles of Chengnan also took personal practice and earnest action as their main theme.
translations.idiomatic: His Ten Principles of Chengnan likewise emphasized personal practice and earnest action.

sentences.zh: 時寧都「易堂九子」，節行文章為海內所重，「髻山七子」，亦以節概名，而文洊獨反己闇修，務求自得。

translations.literal: At the time the Nine Masters of Yitang in Ningdu were esteemed throughout the realm for integrity and literary accomplishment, and the Seven Masters of Jishan were also famed for moral fortitude, yet Wenjian alone turned inward in secret cultivation, striving to attain understanding for himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Nine Masters of Yitang in Ningdu were esteemed throughout the realm for integrity and literary accomplishment, and the Seven Masters of Jishan were likewise famed for moral fortitude, yet Wenjian alone turned inward in secret cultivation, striving to attain understanding for himself.

sentences.zh: 髻山宋之盛過訪文洊，遂邀易堂魏禧、彭任會程山，講學旬餘。

translations.literal: Song Zhisheng of Jishan came to visit Wenjian and then invited Wei Xi and Peng Ren of Yitang to meet at Chengnan, where they lectured together for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhisheng of Jishan came to visit Wenjian and then invited Wei Xi and Peng Ren of Yitang to gather at Chengnan, where they lectured together for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 於是皆推程山，謂其篤躬行，識道本。

translations.literal: Thereupon all acclaimed Chengnan, saying that it was earnest in personal conduct and understood the root of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all acclaimed Chengnan, saying that it was earnest in personal conduct and understood the root of the Way.

sentences.zh: 甘京與文洊為友，後遂師之，

translations.literal: Gan Jing was Wenjian's friend and later became his disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Jing was Wenjian's friend and later became his disciple.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十年，卒，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 京，字健齋，南豐人。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Jianzhai, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Jing, styled Jianzhai, was from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 負氣慷慨，期有濟於世。

translations.literal: Spirited and generous, he hoped to be of use to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Spirited and generous, he hoped to be of use to the world.

sentences.zh: 慕陳同甫之為人，講求有用之學。

translations.literal: He admired Chen Tongfu's character and pursued learning of practical use.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Chen Tongfu's character and pursued learning of practical use.

sentences.zh: 與同邑封濬、曾曰都、危龍光、湯其仁、黃熙師事文洊，粹然有儒者氣象，時號「程山六君子」。

translations.literal: Together with fellow townsman Feng Jun, Zeng Yuedou, Wei Longguang, Tang Qiren, and Huang Xi, he studied under Wenjian as master; pure in bearing and possessed of a Confucian air, they were called at the time the Six Gentlemen of Chengnan.
translations.idiomatic: Together with fellow townsman Feng Jun, Zeng Yuedou, Wei Longguang, Tang Qiren, and Huang Xi, he studied under Wenjian; pure in bearing and possessed of a Confucian air, they were called the Six Gentlemen of Chengnan.

sentences.zh: 著軸園稿十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Shaoyuan Drafts in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Shaoyuan Drafts in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 熙，字維緝。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Weiji.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Xi, styled Weiji.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, he was a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 文洊長熙僅六歲，熙服弟子之事，常與及門之最幼者旅進退。

translations.literal: Wenjian was only six years older than Xi; Xi performed the duties of a disciple and often entered and withdrew together with the youngest of those at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjian was only six years older than Xi; Xi performed the duties of a disciple and often entered and withdrew together with the youngest of those at the gate.

sentences.zh: 朔望四拜，侍食起饋，唯諾步趨，進退維謹，不以為勞。

translations.literal: On the first and fifteenth of each month he bowed four times; he waited on meals, rose to serve food, answered with assent, walked and hastened with care, and was scrupulous in advancing and withdrawing, never considering it burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month he bowed four times; he waited on meals, rose to serve food, answered with assent, walked and hastened with care, and was scrupulous in advancing and withdrawing, never considering it burdensome.

sentences.zh: 彭士望比之朱子之事延平。

translations.literal: Peng Shiwang compared him to Zhu Xi's service to Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shiwang compared him to Zhu Xi's service to Yanping.

sentences.zh: 母喪未葬，鄰不戒於火，延燎將及。

translations.literal: When his mother died and had not yet been buried, a neighbor was careless with fire and the blaze spread and was about to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and had not yet been buried, a neighbor was careless with fire and the blaze spread and was about to reach them.

sentences.zh: 熙撫棺大慟，原以身同燼。

translations.literal: Xi embraced the coffin and wailed bitterly, willing to be burned together with it.
translations.idiomatic: Xi embraced the coffin and wailed bitterly, willing to be burned together with it.

sentences.zh: 俄而風返，人以為純孝所感。

translations.literal: Shortly the wind turned back, and people regarded it as moved by pure filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly the wind turned back, and people regarded it as moved by pure filial piety.

sentences.zh: 曰都，字姜公。

translations.literal: Yuedou, courtesy name Jianggong.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Yuedou, styled Jianggong.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 其學務實體諸己，因自號體齋。

translations.literal: His learning sought to embody reality in oneself; therefore he styled himself Tizhai.
translations.idiomatic: His learning sought to embody reality in oneself; therefore he styled himself Tizhai.

sentences.zh: 以學行為鄉里所矜式。

translations.literal: For learning and conduct he was admired and taken as a model in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: For learning and conduct he was admired and taken as a model in his home district.

sentences.zh: 龍光，字二為。

translations.literal: Longguang, courtesy name Erwei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Longguang, styled Erwei.

sentences.zh: 善事繼母，繼母遇之非理，委曲承順，久而愛之若親子焉。

translations.literal: He was good at serving his stepmother; though his stepmother treated him unreasonably, he yielded and submitted tactfully, and in time she loved him as her own child.
translations.idiomatic: He was good at serving his stepmother; though his stepmother treated him unreasonably, he yielded and submitted tactfully, and in time she loved him as her own child.

sentences.zh: 其仁，字長人。

translations.literal: Qiren, courtesy name Changren.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qiren, styled Changren.

sentences.zh: 著四書切問、省克堂集。

translations.literal: He wrote Close Questions on the Four Books and the Shenke Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Close Questions on the Four Books and the Shenke Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 與文洊同時者，有宋之盛、鄧元昌。

translations.literal: Contemporary with Wenjian were Song Zhisheng and Deng Yuanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary with Wenjian were Song Zhisheng and Deng Yuanchang.

sentences.zh: 之盛，字未有，星子人。

translations.literal: Zhisheng, courtesy name Weiyou, was a native of Xingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhisheng, styled Weiyou, was from Xingzi.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎己卯舉人。

translations.literal: A juren in the jimao year of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren in the jimao year of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 結廬髻山，足不入城巿，以講學為己任。

translations.literal: He built a hut on Jishan and never entered the city or market, taking lecturing and learning as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut on Jishan and never entered the city or market, taking lecturing and learning as his own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 其學以明道為宗，識仁為要，於二氏微言奧旨，皆能抉摘異同。

translations.literal: His learning took making the Way manifest as its principle and recognizing benevolence as its essential point; in the subtle words and profound meanings of the two schools he could always extract agreements and differences.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took making the Way manifest as its principle and recognizing benevolence as its essential point; in the subtle words and profound meanings of the two schools he could always extract agreements and differences.

sentences.zh: 與文洊交最篤。

translations.literal: His friendship with Wenjian was the closest.
translations.idiomatic: His friendship with Wenjian was the closest.

sentences.zh: 晚讀胡敬齋居易錄，持敬之功益密。

translations.literal: In his later years he read Hu Jingzhai's Records of Dwelling in the Ordinary, and the work of upholding reverence grew even more rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he read Hu Jingzhai's Records of Dwelling in the Ordinary, and the work of upholding reverence grew even more rigorous.

sentences.zh: 與甘京論祭立屍喪復之禮不可廢，魏禧亟稱之。

translations.literal: With Gan Jing he argued that the rites of establishing the corpse at sacrifice and reviving the dead at mourning must not be abandoned; Wei Xi greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: With Gan Jing he argued that the rites of establishing the corpse at sacrifice and reviving the dead at mourning must not be abandoned; Wei Xi greatly praised this.

sentences.zh: 元昌，字慕濂，贛縣人。

translations.literal: Yuanchang, courtesy name Mulian, was a native of Gan County.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanchang, styled Mulian, was from Gan County.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 年十七，得宋五子書，遂棄舉子業，致力於學。

translations.literal: At seventeen he obtained the books of the Five Masters of Song and then abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees, devoting himself wholly to learning.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he obtained the books of the Five Masters of Song and then abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees, devoting himself wholly to learning.

sentences.zh: 雩都宋昌圖以通家子謁之，元昌喜之曰：「吾小友也！」

translations.literal: Song Changtu of Yudu came to visit him as a son of a family connected by marriage; Yuanchang was pleased and said: "My young friend!
translations.idiomatic: Song Changtu of Yudu came to visit him as a son of a family connected by marriage; Yuanchang was pleased and said: "My young friend!

sentences.zh: 館之於家，昕夕論學為日程，言動必記之，互相考覈。

translations.literal: He lodged him in his home, made morning and evening discussion of learning the daily schedule, always recorded words and actions, and mutually examined one another.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged him in his home, made morning and evening discussion of learning the daily schedule, always recorded words and actions, and mutually examined one another.

sentences.zh: 一日，昌圖讀朱子大學或問首章，元昌過窗外駐聽之，謂昌圖曰：「子勉之！

translations.literal: One day Changtu was reading the first chapter of Zhu Xi's Questions on the Great Learning; Yuanchang passed outside the window and stopped to listen, then said to Changtu: "You must exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: One day Changtu was reading the first chapter of Zhu Xi's Questions on the Great Learning; Yuanchang passed outside the window and stopped to listen, then said to Changtu: "You must exert yourself!

sentences.zh: 毋蹈吾所悔，永為朱子罪人，偷息天地也。」

translations.literal: Do not follow what I regret, forever becoming a criminal against Zhu Xi, breathing idly beneath Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Do not follow what I regret, forever becoming a criminal against Zhu Xi, breathing idly beneath Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 其互相切劘如此。

translations.literal: Thus they mutually sharpened one another.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they mutually sharpened one another.

sentences.zh: 高愈，字紫超，無錫人，明高攀龍之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Gao Yu, courtesy name Zichao, was a native of Wuxi and the elder brother's grandson of the Ming figure Gao Panlong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu, styled Zichao, was from Wuxi and was the elder brother's grandson of the Ming figure Gao Panlong.

sentences.zh: 十歲，讀攀龍遺書，即有向學之志。

translations.literal: At ten he read Panlong's posthumous writings and immediately had the will to pursue learning.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he read Panlong's posthumous writings and immediately had the will to pursue learning.

sentences.zh: 既壯，補諸生。

translations.literal: When grown, he entered the county school as a student.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he entered the county school as a student.

sentences.zh: 日誦遺經及先儒語錄，謹言行，嚴取捨之辨，不尚議論。

translations.literal: Daily he recited the classics handed down and the recorded sayings of earlier Confucians; he was careful in words and conduct, strict in distinguishing what to accept and reject, and did not esteem disputation.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he recited the classics handed down and the recorded sayings of earlier Confucians; he was careful in words and conduct, strict in distinguishing what to accept and reject, and did not esteem disputation.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「士求自立，須自不忘溝壑始。」

translations.literal: He once said: "A scholar seeking to establish himself must begin with not forgetting the ditches and ravines.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "A scholar seeking to establish himself must begin with not forgetting the ditches and ravines.

sentences.zh: 事親孝，居喪，不飲酒食肉，不內寢。

translations.literal: He served his parents filially; in mourning he did not drink wine or eat meat and did not sleep indoors.
translations.idiomatic: He served his parents filially; in mourning he did not drink wine or eat meat and did not sleep indoors.

sentences.zh: 晚年窮困，餟粥七日矣，方挈其子登城眺望，充然樂也。

translations.literal: In his later years he was poor and distressed; he had eaten thin gruel for seven days, yet he took his son up to the city wall to gaze into the distance, perfectly content.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was poor and distressed; he had eaten thin gruel for seven days, yet he took his son up to the city wall to gaze into the distance, perfectly content.

sentences.zh: 儀封張伯行巡撫江蘇，延愈主東林書院講會，愈以疾辭。

translations.literal: Zhang Boxing of Yifeng, as governor of Jiangsu, invited Yu to preside over the lecture assembly at Donglin Academy; Yu declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boxing of Yifeng, as governor of Jiangsu, invited Yu to preside over the lecture assembly at Donglin Academy; Yu declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 平居體安氣和，有忿爭者，至愈前輒愧悔。

translations.literal: In ordinary life his body was at ease and his spirit harmonious; those engaged in angry disputes, upon coming before Yu, would immediately feel shame and regret.
translations.idiomatic: In ordinary life his body was at ease and his spirit harmonious; those engaged in angry disputes, upon coming before Yu, would immediately feel shame and regret.

sentences.zh: 鄉人素好以道學相詆諆，獨於愈，僉曰：「君子也。」

translations.literal: The people of his district were accustomed to slandering one another over Neo-Confucian learning, but toward Yu alone they all said: "A gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The people of his district were accustomed to slandering one another over Neo-Confucian learning, but toward Yu alone they all said: "A gentleman.

sentences.zh: 顧棟高嘗從愈遊，說經娓娓忘倦。

translations.literal: Gu Donggao once traveled with Yu; in expounding the classics he spoke at length without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Donggao once traveled with Yu; in expounding the classics he spoke at length without tiring.

sentences.zh: 年七十八，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy-eight, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 嘗撰朱子小學注，又所著有讀易偶存、春秋經傳日鈔、春秋類、春秋疑義、周禮疏義、儀禮喪服或問。

translations.literal: He once compiled a commentary on Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning, and his works also include Casual Notes on Reading the Changes, Daily Notes on the Spring and Autumn Classic and Commentary, Categories of the Spring and Autumn, Doubts on the Spring and Autumn, Exposition of the Rites of Zhou, and Questions on Mourning Garments in the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He once compiled a commentary on Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning, and his works also include Casual Notes on Reading the Changes, Daily Notes on the Spring and Autumn Classic and Commentary, Categories of the Spring and Autumn, Doubts on the Spring and Autumn, Exposition of the Rites of Zhou, and Questions on Mourning Garments in the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 東林顧、高子弟顧樞、高世泰等，鼎革後尚傳其學。

translations.literal: The disciples of Gu and Gao of Donglin—Gu Shu and Gao Shitai and others—after the dynastic change still transmitted their learning.
translations.idiomatic: The disciples of Gu and Gao of Donglin—Gu Shu and Gao Shitai and others—after the dynastic change still transmitted their learning.

sentences.zh: 初，世泰為攀龍從子，少侍講席，晚年以東林先緒為己任，葺道南祠、麗澤堂於梁谿，一時同志恪遵遺規。

translations.literal: At first Shitai was Panlong's grandnephew; from youth he attended the lecture seat, and in his later years took the earlier lineage of Donglin as his own responsibility, restoring the Daonan Shrine and Lizhe Hall at Liangxi; for a time like-minded men strictly observed the legacy rules.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shitai was Panlong's grandnephew; from youth he attended the lecture seat, and in his later years took the earlier lineage of Donglin as his own responsibility, restoring the Daonan Shrine and Lizhe Hall at Liangxi; for a time like-minded men strictly observed the legacy rules.

sentences.zh: 祁州刁包等相與論學。

translations.literal: Diao Bao of Qizhou and others discussed learning together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Bao of Qizhou and others discussed learning together with him.

sentences.zh: 學者有南梁、北祁之稱。

translations.literal: Scholars spoke of the Southern Liang and Northern Qi schools.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars spoke of the Southern Liang and Northern Qi schools.

sentences.zh: 大學士熊賜履講學出世泰門下，儀封張伯行、平湖陸隴其亦嘗至東林講學。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü lectured after coming from Shitai's gate; Zhang Boxing of Yifeng and Lu Longqi of Pinghu also once came to Donglin to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xiong Cilü lectured after coming from Shitai's gate; Zhang Boxing of Yifeng and Lu Longqi of Pinghu also once came to Donglin to lecture.

sentences.zh: 賜履、隴其自有傳。

translations.literal: Cilü and Longqi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Cilü and Longqi have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 顧培，字畇滋，無錫人。

translations.literal: Gu Pei, courtesy name Yunzi, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Pei, styled Yunzi, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 少從宜興湯之錡學，幡然悔曰：「道在人倫庶物而已。」

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Tang Zhiqi of Yixing and suddenly repented, saying: "The Way lies only in human relations and the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Tang Zhiqi of Yixing and suddenly repented, saying: "The Way lies only in human relations and the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 之錡歿，有弟子金敞。

translations.literal: When Zhiqi died, there was the disciple Jin Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhiqi died, there was the disciple Jin Chang.

sentences.zh: 培築共學山居以延敞，晨夕講會。

translations.literal: Pei built Gongxue Mountain Retreat to receive Chang, and morning and evening they held lecture assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Pei built Gongxue Mountain Retreat to receive Chang, and morning and evening they held lecture assemblies.

sentences.zh: 遵攀龍靜坐法，以整齊嚴肅為入德之方。

translations.literal: Following Panlong's method of quiet sitting, he took orderliness and solemnity as the way to enter virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Following Panlong's method of quiet sitting, he took orderliness and solemnity as the way to enter virtue.

sentences.zh: 默識未發之中，篤守性善之旨。

translations.literal: Silently recognizing the state before feelings are aroused, he steadfastly upheld the principle that nature is good.
translations.idiomatic: Silently recognizing the state before feelings are aroused, he steadfastly upheld the principle that nature is good.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，四方來學日眾。

translations.literal: In his later years students came from all directions in ever greater numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years students came from all directions in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 張伯行頗疑靜坐之說，培往復千言，暢高氏之旨。

translations.literal: Zhang Boxing rather doubted the doctrine of quiet sitting; Pei exchanged letters of a thousand words, expounding the intent of the Gao school.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Boxing rather doubted the doctrine of quiet sitting; Pei exchanged letters of a thousand words, expounding the intent of the Gao school.

sentences.zh: 彭定求，字勤止，又字南畇，長洲人。

translations.literal: Peng Dingqiu, courtesy name Qinzhi, also styled Nanyun, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Dingqiu, styled Qinzhi and also known as Nanyun, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父瓏授以梁谿高氏之學，又嘗師事湯斌。

translations.literal: His father Long transmitted to him the learning of the Gao school of Liangxi, and he also once studied under Tang Bin as master.
translations.idiomatic: His father Long transmitted to him the learning of the Gao school of Liangxi, and he also once studied under Tang Bin as master.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十五年一甲一名進士，授翰林院修撰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi, first-ranked jinshi, he was appointed Hanlin Academician and Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kangxi, first-ranked jinshi, he was appointed Hanlin Academician and Compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷官國子監司業、翰林院侍講，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting, and was appointed Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperors' Actions.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and Hanlin Academician Reader-in-Waiting, and was appointed Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperors' Actions.

sentences.zh: 前後在翰林才四年，即歸里不復出。

translations.literal: After only four years in the Hanlin Academy he returned home and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: After only four years in the Hanlin Academy he returned home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 作高望吟七章，以慕七賢。

translations.literal: He composed seven chapters of Odes Gazing at the Heights to admire the Seven Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He composed seven chapters of Odes Gazing at the Heights to admire the Seven Worthies.

sentences.zh: 七賢者，白沙、陽明、東廓、念菴、梁谿、念台、漳浦也。

translations.literal: The Seven Worthies were Baisha, Yangming, Dongkuo, Nian'an, Liangxi, Niantai, and Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Worthies were Baisha, Yangming, Dongkuo, Nian'an, Liangxi, Niantai, and Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 又著陽明釋毀錄、儒門法語、南畇文集。

translations.literal: He also wrote Records Refuting Slander of Yangming, Maxims of the Confucian School, and the Nanyun Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Records Refuting Slander of Yangming, Maxims of the Confucian School, and the Nanyun Collection.

sentences.zh: 嘗與門人林雲翥書云：「有原進於足下者有二：一曰無遽求高遠而略庸近。

translations.literal: He once wrote to his disciple Lin Yunzhu, saying: "There are two admonitions I wish to advance to you: first, do not hastily seek what is lofty and far while neglecting what is ordinary and near.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to his disciple Lin Yunzhu, saying: "There are two admonitions I wish to advance to you: first, do not hastily seek what is lofty and far while neglecting what is ordinary and near.

sentences.zh: 子臣弟友，君子之道。

translations.literal: Serving the ruler, serving the father, serving the elder brother, and serving friends—these are the Way of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the ruler, serving the father, serving the elder brother, and serving friends—these are the Way of the gentleman.

sentences.zh: 至聖以有餘不足為斤斤，孟子以堯、舜之道孝弟而已。

translations.literal: The Utmost Sage weighed surplus and deficiency with meticulous care; Mencius said the Way of Yao and Shun is simply filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: The Utmost Sage weighed surplus and deficiency with meticulous care; Mencius said the Way of Yao and Shun is simply filial piety and brotherly respect.

sentences.zh: 然則舍倫常日用事親從兄之事不為，而鉤深索隱，以為聖人之道有出於人心同然之外者，必且流於異端堅僻之行矣。

translations.literal: Then if one abandons the ordinary duties of daily life in serving parents and following elder brothers and does not perform them, yet probes deeply and searches out hidden meanings, thinking the sage's Way has something beyond what is commonly shared in the human heart, one will surely drift into the perverse conduct of heterodox schools.
translations.idiomatic: Then if one abandons the ordinary duties of daily life in serving parents and following elder brothers and does not perform them, yet probes deeply and searches out hidden meanings, thinking the sage's Way has something beyond what is commonly shared in the human heart, one will surely drift into the perverse conduct of heterodox schools.

sentences.zh: 一曰無妄生門戶異同之見，騰口說而遺踐履。

translations.literal: Second, do not rashly generate views of sectarian difference, letting the mouth speak while abandoning practice.
translations.idiomatic: Second, do not rashly generate views of sectarian difference, letting the mouth speak while abandoning practice.

sentences.zh: 朱子之會於鵝湖也，傾倒於陸子義利之說，此陽明拔本塞源之論，致良知之指，一脈相承。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xi met at Goose Lake, he was completely won over by Master Lu's doctrine of righteousness and profit; this is Yangming's argument to pull up the root and stop the source, and the aim of extending innate moral knowledge—one lineage transmitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xi met at Goose Lake, he was completely won over by Master Lu's doctrine of righteousness and profit; this is Yangming's argument to pull up the root and stop the source, and the aim of extending innate moral knowledge—one lineage transmitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 其因時救弊，乃不得已之苦衷，非角人我之見。

translations.literal: Their responses to the times to remedy abuses were unavoidable bitter expedients, not contests of personal views.
translations.idiomatic: Their responses to the times to remedy abuses were unavoidable bitter expedients, not contests of personal views.

sentences.zh: 僕詠遺經，蕩滌瑕滓，因有儒門法語。

translations.literal: I chant the classics handed down and wash away their blemishes; hence I have Maxims of the Confucian School.
translations.idiomatic: I chant the classics handed down and wash away their blemishes; hence I have Maxims of the Confucian School.

sentences.zh: 足下有志聖賢，當以念台劉子人譜、證人會二書入門，且無嘵嘵於紫陽、姚江之辨也。」

translations.literal: You aspire to the sages and worthies; you should take Master Liu Niantai's Chart of Man and the Zhengren Assembly as your entry, and not chatter endlessly about the dispute between Ziyang and Yaojiang."
translations.idiomatic: You aspire to the sages and worthies; you should take Master Liu Niantai's Chart of Man and the Zhengren Assembly as your entry, and not chatter endlessly about the dispute between Ziyang and Yaojiang."

sentences.zh: 定求卒年七十有八。

translations.literal: Dingqiu died at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Dingqiu died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 其孫啟豐官兵部尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Qifeng served as Minister of Works and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Qifeng served as Minister of Works and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 啟豐子紹升，頗傳家學，述儒行，有二林居集。

translations.literal: Qifeng's son Shaosheng rather transmitted the family learning, expounded Confucian conduct, and wrote the Erlin Dwelling Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng's son Shaosheng rather transmitted the family learning, expounded Confucian conduct, and wrote the Erlin Dwelling Collection.

sentences.zh: 然彭氏學兼朱、陸，識兼頓漸，啟豐、紹升頗入於禪。

translations.literal: Yet the Peng family's learning combined Zhu and Lu, and their understanding combined sudden and gradual enlightenment; Qifeng and Shaosheng rather entered into Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Peng family's learning combined Zhu and Lu, and their understanding combined sudden and gradual enlightenment; Qifeng and Shaosheng rather entered into Chan.

sentences.zh: 休寧戴震移書紹升辨之。

translations.literal: Dai Zhen of Xiuning wrote to Shaosheng to dispute this.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zhen of Xiuning wrote to Shaosheng to dispute this.

sentences.zh: 紹升又與吳縣汪縉共講儒學。

translations.literal: Shaosheng also together with Wang Ji of Wu County lectured on Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shaosheng also together with Wang Ji of Wu County lectured on Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 縉著三錄、二錄，尊孔子而遊乎二氏。

translations.literal: Ji wrote Three Records and Two Records, honoring Confucius while roaming among the two schools.
translations.idiomatic: Ji wrote Three Records and Two Records, honoring Confucius while roaming among the two schools.

sentences.zh: 此後江南理學微矣。

translations.literal: After this Neo-Confucian learning in Jiangnan declined.
translations.idiomatic: After this Neo-Confucian learning in Jiangnan declined.

sentences.zh: 湯之錡，字世調，宜興人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhiqi, courtesy name Shidiao, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhiqi, styled Shidiao, was from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 安貧力學，於書無所不讀，尤篤信周子主靜之說。

translations.literal: Content in poverty, he studied strenuously; in books there was nothing he did not read, and he especially devoutly believed in Master Zhou's doctrine of upholding stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Content in poverty, he studied strenuously; in books there was nothing he did not read, and he especially devoutly believed in Master Zhou's doctrine of upholding stillness.

sentences.zh: 或議其近於禪，之錡曰：「程子見學者靜坐，即歎其善學。
