translations.literal: Some criticized him as close to Chan; Zhiqi said: "When Master Cheng saw a student sitting in quiet, he immediately praised him as a good learner.
translations.idiomatic: Some criticized him as close to Chan; Zhiqi said: "When Master Cheng saw a student sitting in quiet, he immediately praised him as a good learner.

sentences.zh: 易言『齋戒，以神明其德』。

translations.literal: The Changes says, 'Fast and abstain, thereby to make the virtue bright.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'Fast and abstain, thereby to make the virtue bright.'

sentences.zh: 靜坐，即古人之齋戒，非禪也。」

translations.literal: Quiet sitting is the fasting and abstinence of the ancients; it is not Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet sitting is the fasting and abstinence of the ancients—it is not Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，一循古禮，就地寢苫。

translations.literal: In mourning for his parents he followed the ancient rites entirely, sleeping on the ground on a straw mat.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his parents he followed the ancient rites entirely, sleeping on the ground on a straw mat.

sentences.zh: 事諸父如父，昆弟無間言。

translations.literal: He served his uncles as he would his father, and among brothers there was never a harsh word.
translations.idiomatic: He served his uncles as he would his father, and among brothers there was never a harsh word.

sentences.zh: 既而得高攀龍复七規，喟然曰：「此其入學之門乎？」

translations.literal: Thereafter he obtained Gao Panlong's Seven Rules of Recovery and sighed, saying: "Is this the gate of entering learning?"
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he obtained Gao Panlong's Seven Rules of Recovery and sighed, saying: "Is this the gate of entering learning?"

sentences.zh: 仿其說為春秋兩會，聞風者不憚數千里來就學焉。

translations.literal: He modeled his teaching on them as the Spring and Autumn Two Assemblies, and those who heard of it did not shrink from coming thousands of li to study.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his teaching on them as the Spring and Autumn Two Assemblies, and those who heard of it did not shrink from coming thousands of li to study.

sentences.zh: 明亡，之錡年二十四，即棄舉子業。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, Zhiqi was twenty-four and immediately abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, Zhiqi was twenty-four and immediately abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees.

sentences.zh: 嘗論出處之道曰：「『潛龍勿用』，潛要確，若不確，則遁世不見知而悔矣。

translations.literal: He once discussed the Way of advancing and withdrawing, saying: "'The hidden dragon does not act'—the hidden must be firm; if not firm, then in withdrawing from the world one will not be recognized and will regret it.
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed the Way of advancing and withdrawing, saying: "'The hidden dragon does not act'—the hidden must be firm; if not firm, then in withdrawing from the world one will not be recognized and will regret it.

sentences.zh: 古來多少高明，只為此一悔所誤。」

translations.literal: How many brilliant men since antiquity have been ruined by this one regret alone.
translations.idiomatic: How many brilliant men since antiquity have been ruined by this one regret alone.

sentences.zh: 常州知府駱鍾麟請關西李顒講學毗陵，特遣使聘之，之錡堅辭不赴；

translations.literal: Changzhou prefect Luo Zhonglin invited Li Yong of Guanxi to lecture in Piling and specially sent an envoy to engage him; Zhiqi firmly declined and did not go;
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou prefect Luo Zhonglin invited Li Yong of Guanxi to lecture in Piling and specially sent an envoy to engage him; Zhiqi firmly declined and did not go;

sentences.zh: 後延主東林、延陵諸講席，又不就。

translations.literal: later he was invited to preside over lecture seats at Donglin and Yanling, but again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: later he was invited to preside over lecture seats at Donglin and Yanling, but again he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 之錡為學，專務切近，絕無緣飾。

translations.literal: In learning, Zhiqi devoted himself solely to what was close at hand, with absolutely no ornamental embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: In learning, Zhiqi devoted himself solely to what was close at hand, with absolutely no ornamental embellishment.

sentences.zh: 或詢陽明致良知之說及朱、陸異同者，之錡曰：「顧吾力行何如耳，多辨論何益？」

translations.literal: When someone asked about Yangming's doctrine of extending innate moral knowledge and the agreements and differences between Zhu and Lu, Zhiqi said: "Just look at how I put it into practice; what use is much disputation?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked about Yangming's doctrine of extending innate moral knowledge and the agreements and differences between Zhu and Lu, Zhiqi said: "Just look at how I put it into practice; what use is much disputation?"

sentences.zh: 一日，抱微疾，整襟危坐而逝，年六十二。

translations.literal: One day, with a slight illness, he straightened his robe and sat upright in dignity and passed away, at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: One day, with a slight illness, he straightened his robe and sat upright in dignity and passed away, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 及門金敞、顧培輩，建書院於惠山之麓，奉其主祀之，著偶然雲集。

translations.literal: His disciples Jin Chang, Gu Pei, and others built an academy at the foot of Huishan, enshrined him as its patron, and he wrote the Casual Cloud Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Jin Chang, Gu Pei, and others built an academy at the foot of Huishan, enshrined him as its patron, and he wrote the Casual Cloud Collection.

sentences.zh: 施璜，字虹玉，休寧人。

translations.literal: Shi Huang, courtesy name Hongyu, was a native of Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Huang, styled Hongyu, was from Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 少應試，見鄉先生講學紫陽，瞿然曰：「學者當如是矣！」

translations.literal: In youth he went to take the examinations; seeing a local elder lecturing at Ziyang, he started and said: "A student should be like this!
translations.idiomatic: In youth he went to take the examinations; seeing a local elder lecturing at Ziyang, he started and said: "A student should be like this!

sentences.zh: 遂棄舉業，發憤躬行。

translations.literal: He then abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees and resolved in earnest to practice personally.
translations.idiomatic: He then abandoned the pursuit of examination degrees and resolved in earnest to practice personally.

sentences.zh: 日以存何念、接何人、行何事、讀何書、吐何語五者自勘。

translations.literal: Daily he examined himself with five questions: what thought is preserved, what person is encountered, what affair is performed, what book is read, and what words are spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he examined himself with five questions: what thought is preserved, what person is encountered, what affair is performed, what book is read, and what words are spoken.

sentences.zh: 教學者九容以養其外，九思以養其內，九德以要其成，學者稱誠齋先生。

translations.literal: In teaching students he used the nine forms of bearing to cultivate the outer self, the nine reflections to cultivate the inner self, and the nine virtues to complete the whole; students called him Master Chengzhai.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching students he used the nine forms of bearing to cultivate the outer self, the nine reflections to cultivate the inner self, and the nine virtues to complete the whole; students called him Master Chengzhai.

sentences.zh: 已而遊梁谿，事高世泰。

translations.literal: Later he traveled to Liangxi and served Gao Shitai.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled to Liangxi and served Gao Shitai.

sentences.zh: 將歸，與世泰期某年月日當赴講。

translations.literal: When about to return, he set a date with Shitai for a certain year, month, and day when he would come to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: When about to return, he set a date with Shitai for a certain year, month, and day when he would come to lecture.

sentences.zh: 及期，世泰設榻以待，或曰：「千里之期，能必信乎？」

translations.literal: When the day came, Shitai prepared a couch and waited; someone said: "A promise a thousand li away—can it be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, Shitai prepared a couch and waited; someone said: "A promise a thousand li away—can it be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 世泰曰：「施生篤行君子也。

translations.literal: Shitai said: "Master Shi is a man of earnest conduct and a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shitai said: "Master Shi is a man of earnest conduct and a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 如不信，吾不復交天下士矣。」

translations.literal: If he is not trusted, I shall never again associate with scholars under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: If he is not trusted, I shall never again associate with scholars under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 言未既，璜果挈弟子至。

translations.literal: Before the words were finished, Huang indeed arrived leading his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Before the words were finished, Huang indeed arrived leading his disciples.

sentences.zh: 著有思誠錄、小學、近思錄發明。

translations.literal: He wrote Records of Thinking Sincerely, Elementary Learning, and Elucidations of Reflections on Things at Hand.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Thinking Sincerely, Elementary Learning, and Elucidations of Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 張夏，字秋韶，亦無錫人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xia, courtesy name Qiushao, was also a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xia, styled Qiushao, was also from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 隱居菰川之上，孝友力學。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion above Guchuan, filial and friendly, studying strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion above Guchuan, filial and friendly, studying strenuously.

sentences.zh: 初從馬世奇受經，後入東林書院，從高世泰學。

translations.literal: At first he received the classics from Ma Shiqi; later he entered Donglin Academy and studied under Gao Shitai.
translations.idiomatic: At first he received the classics from Ma Shiqi; later he entered Donglin Academy and studied under Gao Shitai.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，遂入世泰之室。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he entered Shitai's inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years he entered Shitai's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 世泰卒，其子弟相與立夏為師，事之如世泰。

translations.literal: When Shitai died, his disciples together established Xia as teacher and served him as they had Shitai.
translations.idiomatic: When Shitai died, his disciples jointly established Xia as teacher and served him as they had Shitai.

sentences.zh: 湯斌撫江蘇，至東林，與夏講學，韙其言。

translations.literal: Tang Bin governed Jiangsu, came to Donglin, and lectured with Xia, approving his words.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Bin governed Jiangsu, came to Donglin, and lectured with Xia, approving his words.

sentences.zh: 延至蘇州學宮，為諸生講孝經、小學。

translations.literal: He invited him to the Suzhou Confucian school and lectured to the students on the Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He invited him to the Suzhou Confucian school and lectured to the students on the Classic of Filial Piety and Elementary Learning.

sentences.zh: 退而注孝經解義、小學瀹注。

translations.literal: Retiring, he annotated Exposition of the Classic of Filial Piety and Exposition of Elementary Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring, he annotated Exposition of the Classic of Filial Piety and Exposition of Elementary Learning.

sentences.zh: 吳曰慎，字徽仲，歙縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Yueshen, courtesy name Huizhong, was a native of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yueshen, styled Huizhong, was from She County.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 盡心於宋五子書。

translations.literal: He devoted his heart entirely to the books of the Five Masters of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted his heart entirely to the books of the Five Masters of Song.

sentences.zh: 論學主乎敬，故自號曰靜菴。

translations.literal: In discussing learning he upheld reverence; therefore he styled himself Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing learning he upheld reverence; therefore he styled himself Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 初遊梁谿，講學東林書院。

translations.literal: At first he traveled to Liangxi and lectured at Donglin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At first he traveled to Liangxi and lectured at Donglin Academy.

sentences.zh: 已而歸歙，會講紫陽、還古兩書院，興起者眾。

translations.literal: Thereafter he returned to She and held joint lectures at the Ziyang and Huangu academies; many were stirred to action.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he returned to She and held joint lectures at the Ziyang and Huangu academies; many were stirred to action.

sentences.zh: 陸世儀，字道威，太倉州人。

translations.literal: Lu Shiyi, courtesy name Daowei, was a native of Taicang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shiyi, styled Daowei, was from Taicang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少從劉宗周講學。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Liu Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Liu Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 歸而鑿池十畝，築亭其中，不通賓客，自號桴亭。

translations.literal: Returning home he dug a pond of ten mu and built a pavilion in it, receiving no guests, and styled himself Futing.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home he dug a pond of ten mu and built a pavilion in it, receiving no guests, and styled himself Futing.

sentences.zh: 與同里陳瑚、盛敬、江士韶相約，為遷善改過之學。

translations.literal: Together with fellow townsman Chen Hu, Sheng Jing, and Jiang Shishao he agreed to pursue the learning of moving toward goodness and correcting faults.
translations.idiomatic: Together with fellow townsman Chen Hu, Sheng Jing, and Jiang Shishao he agreed to pursue the learning of moving toward goodness and correcting faults.

sentences.zh: 或橫經論難，或即事窮理，反覆以求一是。

translations.literal: Sometimes they spread the classics and debated difficulties; sometimes they investigated principle in concrete affairs, repeatedly seeking one correct conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they spread the classics and debated difficulties; sometimes they investigated principle in concrete affairs, repeatedly seeking one correct conclusion.

sentences.zh: 甚有商榷未定，徹夜忘寢，質明而後斷，或未斷而復辨者。

translations.literal: Often discussion remained unsettled and they forgot sleep through the night, deciding only at dawn, or not deciding and debating again.
translations.idiomatic: Often discussion remained unsettled and they forgot sleep through the night, deciding only at dawn, or not deciding and debating again.

sentences.zh: 著思辨錄，分小學、大學、立志、居敬、格致、誠正、修齊、治平、天道、人道、諸儒異學、經、子、史籍十四門。

translations.literal: He wrote Records of Reflective Discrimination, divided into fourteen categories: Elementary Learning, Great Learning, Establishing the Will, Upholding Reverence, Investigating Things, Sincerity and Rectification, Self-Cultivation and Family Regulation, Ordering the State and Bringing Peace, the Way of Heaven, the Way of Humanity, Different Schools and Heterodox Learning, Classics, Masters, and Historical Records.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of Reflective Discrimination, divided into fourteen categories: Elementary Learning, Great Learning, Establishing the Will, Upholding Reverence, Investigating Things, Sincerity and Rectification, Self-Cultivation and Family Regulation, Ordering the State and Bringing Peace, the Way of Heaven, the Way of Humanity, Different Schools and Heterodox Learning, Classics, Masters, and Historical Records.

sentences.zh: 世儀之學，主於敦守禮法，不虛談誠敬之旨，施行實政，不空為心性之功。

translations.literal: Shiyi's learning mainly upheld earnest observance of ritual and law, did not speak emptily of the aim of sincerity and reverence, implemented practical government, and did not make empty work of the achievements of mind and nature.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi's learning mainly upheld earnest observance of ritual and law, did not speak emptily of the aim of sincerity and reverence, implemented practical government, and did not make empty work of the achievements of mind and nature.

sentences.zh: 於近代講學諸家，最為篤實。

translations.literal: Among the schools of recent times that lectured and learned, he was the most earnest and practical.
translations.idiomatic: Among the schools of recent times that lectured and learned, he was the most earnest and practical.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「天下無講學之人，此世道之衰；

translations.literal: He said: "When there are no people who lecture and learn under Heaven, this is the decline of the age;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "When there are no people who lecture and learn under Heaven, this is the decline of the age;

sentences.zh: 天下皆講學之人，亦世道之衰。

translations.literal: when everyone under Heaven lectures and learns, that too is the decline of the age.
translations.idiomatic: when everyone under Heaven lectures and learns, that too is the decline of the age.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆之間，書院遍天下，呼朋引類，動輒千人，附影逐聲，廢時失事，甚有藉以行其私者，此所謂處士橫議也。」

translations.literal: Between the Jiajing and Longqing reigns, academies spread throughout the realm; calling companions and drawing classes, they often numbered a thousand; following shadows and chasing sounds, wasting time and neglecting affairs—some even used this to pursue private ends: this is what is called the unrestrained discourse of recluses.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jiajing and Longqing reigns, academies spread throughout the realm; calling companions and drawing classes, they often numbered a thousand; following shadows and chasing sounds, wasting time and neglecting affairs—some even used this to pursue private ends: this is what is called the unrestrained discourse of recluses.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今所當學者不止六藝，如天文、地理、河渠、兵法之類，皆切於世用，不可不講。」

translations.literal: He also said: "What should be learned today is not limited to the Six Arts; such things as astronomy, geography, waterways, and military strategy are all urgently useful in the world and must not go undiscussed."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "What should be learned today is not limited to the Six Arts; such things as astronomy, geography, waterways, and military strategy are all urgently useful in the world and must not go undiscussed."

sentences.zh: 所言深切著明，足砭虛憍之弊。

translations.literal: His words were deep, cutting, and clear, sufficient to remedy the evil of empty arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: His words were deep, cutting, and clear, sufficient to remedy the evil of empty arrogance.

sentences.zh: 其於明儒薛、胡、陳、王，皆平心論之。

translations.literal: Regarding the Ming Confucians Xue, Hu, Chen, and Wang, he discussed them all with an even mind.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding the Ming Confucians Xue, Hu, Chen, and Wang, he discussed them all with an even mind.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂學者曰：「世有大儒，決不別立宗旨。」

translations.literal: He also once told students: "When the age has a great Confucian, he will never separately establish a sectarian principle."
translations.idiomatic: He also once told students: "When the age has a great Confucian, he will never separately establish a sectarian principle."

sentences.zh: 故全祖望謂國初儒者，孫奇逢、黃宗羲、李顒最有名，而世儀少知者，

translations.literal: Therefore Quan Zuwang said that among early dynasty Confucians, Sun Qifeng, Huang Zongxi, and Li Yong were most famous, while Shiyi was little known.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Quan Zuwang said that among early dynasty Confucians, Sun Qifeng, Huang Zongxi, and Li Yong were most famous, while Shiyi was little known.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，從祀文廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, he was enshrined in the Confucian temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, he was enshrined in the Confucian temple.

sentences.zh: 瑚，字言夏，號確菴。

translations.literal: Hu, courtesy name Yanxia, styled Que'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hu, styled Yanxia and known as Que'an.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十六年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a provincial graduate in Ming Chongzhen year sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: He became a provincial graduate in Ming Chongzhen year sixteen.

sentences.zh: 世儀格致篇首提「敬天」二字，瑚由此用力，頗得要領。

translations.literal: At the head of Shiyi's chapter on investigating things he raised the two characters 'revering Heaven'; Hu exerted himself from this and rather grasped the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of Shiyi's chapter on investigating things he raised the two characters 'revering Heaven'; Hu exerted himself from this and rather grasped the essential point.

sentences.zh: 因定為日紀考德法，而揭敬勝、怠勝於每日之首，格致、誠正、修齊、治平於每月之終，益信「人皆可以為堯舜」非虛語也。

translations.literal: Therefore he established a daily record method for examining virtue, posting reverence victorious and sloth victorious at the head of each day and investigation, sincerity, self-cultivation, family regulation, state ordering, and bringing peace at the end of each month, trusting all the more that 'every man can become Yao or Shun' was no empty saying.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he established a daily record method for examining virtue, posting reverence victorious and sloth victorious at the head of each day and investigation, sincerity, self-cultivation, family regulation, state ordering, and bringing peace at the end of each month, trusting all the more that 'every man can become Yao or Shun' was no empty saying.

sentences.zh: 復取小學分為六：曰入孝，曰出悌，曰謹行，曰信言，曰親愛，曰學文；

translations.literal: He further divided Elementary Learning into six parts: entering filial piety, going forth brotherly respect, careful conduct, trustworthy speech, affectionate love, and studying literature;
translations.idiomatic: He further divided Elementary Learning into six parts: entering filial piety, going forth brotherly respect, careful conduct, trustworthy speech, affectionate love, and studying literature;

sentences.zh: 大學分為六：曰格致，曰誠意，曰正心，曰修身，曰齊家，曰治平。

translations.literal: Great Learning into six parts: investigating things, extending knowledge, rectifying the heart, cultivating the self, regulating the family, and ordering the state and bringing peace.
translations.idiomatic: Great Learning into six parts: investigating things, extending knowledge, rectifying the heart, cultivating the self, regulating the family, and ordering the state and bringing peace.

sentences.zh: 謂小學先行後知，大學先知後行，小學之終，即大學之始。

translations.literal: He held that in Elementary Learning action precedes knowledge, in Great Learning knowledge precedes action, and the end of Elementary Learning is the beginning of Great Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He held that in Elementary Learning action precedes knowledge, in Great Learning knowledge precedes action, and the end of Elementary Learning is the beginning of Great Learning.

sentences.zh: 瑚之為學，博大精深，以經世自任。

translations.literal: In learning, Hu was broad, deep, and great, taking ordering the world as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: In learning, Hu was broad, deep, and great, taking ordering the world as his own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 值婁江湮塞，江南大饑，瑚上當事救荒書，皆精切可施行，而時不能用。

translations.literal: When the Lou River was blocked and Jiangnan suffered great famine, Hu submitted famine-relief memorials to those in authority; all were precise, cutting, and practicable, but the times could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lou River was blocked and Jiangnan suffered great famine, Hu submitted famine-relief memorials to those in authority; all were precise, cutting, and practicable, but the times could not employ them.

sentences.zh: 明亡，絕意仕進，避地崑山之蔚村。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, he abandoned all thought of advancement and withdrew to Weicun in Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, he abandoned all thought of advancement and withdrew to Weicun in Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 田沮洳，瑚導鄉人築岸禦水，用兵家束伍法，不日而成。

translations.literal: The fields were marshy; Hu guided the villagers in building dikes to hold back the water, using the military method of binding units in fives, and in no time it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The fields were marshy; Hu guided the villagers in building dikes to hold back the water, using the military method of binding units in fives, and in no time it was completed.

sentences.zh: 父病，刺血籥天，原以身代。

translations.literal: When his father fell ill, he pricked his finger and drew blood to pray to Heaven, willing to die in his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: When his father fell ill, he pricked his finger and drew blood to pray to Heaven, willing to die in his father's place.

sentences.zh: 父卒，遺產悉讓之弟，

translations.literal: When his father died, he yielded all the inherited property to his younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he yielded all the inherited property to his younger brother.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年，卒，年六十有二。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 門人稱曰安道先生。

translations.literal: Disciples called him Master Andao.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples called him Master Andao.

sentences.zh: 巡撫湯斌即其故居為之立安道書院。

translations.literal: Governor Tang Bin established Andao Academy at his former residence.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tang Bin established Andao Academy at his former residence.

sentences.zh: 敬，字宗傳，號寒溪。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Zongchuan, styled Hanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Jing, styled Zongchuan and known as Hanxi.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 長世儀一歲。

translations.literal: He was one year older than Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was one year older than Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 矢志存誠主敬之學，篤於孝友。

translations.literal: He resolved to pursue the learning of preserving sincerity and upholding reverence and was earnest in filial piety and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved to pursue the learning of preserving sincerity and upholding reverence and was earnest in filial piety and friendship.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: In mourning for three years he did not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for three years he did not drink wine or eat meat.

sentences.zh: 有弟遇之無禮，敬終始怡怡。

translations.literal: He had a younger brother who treated him without courtesy; Jing from beginning to end remained cheerful.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother who treated him without courtesy; Jing from beginning to end remained cheerful.

sentences.zh: 士韶，字虞九，號藥園。

translations.literal: Shishao, courtesy name Yujiu, styled Yaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shishao, styled Yujiu and known as Yaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A county student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 其學以世儀為歸。

translations.literal: His learning took Shiyi as its goal.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took Shiyi as its goal.

sentences.zh: 同時理學諸儒多著述，士韶以為聖賢之旨，盡於昔儒之論說，惟在躬行而已。

translations.literal: Contemporary Neo-Confucian scholars mostly wrote books; Shishao held that the intent of the sages and worthies was fully expressed in the discourses of earlier Confucians and lay only in personal practice.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary Neo-Confucian scholars mostly wrote books; Shishao held that the intent of the sages and worthies was fully expressed in the discourses of earlier Confucians and lay only in personal practice.

sentences.zh: 晚年取所作焚之，故不傳於後云。

translations.literal: In his later years he took his writings and burned them, so they were not transmitted to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he took his writings and burned them, so they were not transmitted to posterity.

sentences.zh: 張履祥，字考夫，桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lvxiang, courtesy name Kaofu, was a native of Tongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lvxiang, styled Kaofu, was from Tongxiang.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming county student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a county student under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 世居楊園村，學者稱為楊園先生。

translations.literal: His family had long lived in Yangyuan Village; scholars called him Master Yangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived in Yangyuan Village; scholars called him Master Yangyuan.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪父。

translations.literal: At seven he lost his father.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at seven.

sentences.zh: 家貧，母沈教之曰：「孔、孟亦兩家無父兒也，只因有志，便做到聖賢。」

translations.literal: The family was poor; his mother Lady Shen taught him, saying: "Confucius and Mencius were also sons of families without fathers; only because they had the will, they attained to become sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; his mother Lady Shen taught him, saying: "Confucius and Mencius were also sons of families without fathers; only because they had the will, they attained to become sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 長，受業山陰劉宗周之門。

translations.literal: When grown, he received instruction at the gate of Liu Zongzhou in Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he received instruction at the gate of Liu Zongzhou in Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 時東南文社各立門戶，履祥退然如不勝，惟與同里顏統、錢寅，海鹽吳蕃昌輩以文行相砥刻。

translations.literal: At the time literary societies in the southeast each established their own sects; Lvxiang withdrew as though unable to compete, and only with fellow townsman Yan Tong and Qian Yin and with Wu Fanchang of Haiyan and others sharpened one another in literary accomplishment and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time literary societies in the southeast each established their own sects; Lvxiang withdrew as though unable to compete, and only with fellow townsman Yan Tong and Qian Yin and with Wu Fanchang of Haiyan and others sharpened one another in literary accomplishment and conduct.

sentences.zh: 統、寅、蕃昌相繼歿，為之經紀其家。

translations.literal: Tong, Yin, and Fanchang died one after another, and he managed their households.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, Yin, and Fanchang died one after another, and he managed their households.

sentences.zh: 自是與海鹽何汝霖、烏程凌克貞、歸安沈磊切劘講習，益務躬行。

translations.literal: From then on he with He Rulin of Haiyan, Ling Kezhen of Wucheng, and Shen Lei of Gui'an mutually sharpened one another in study and practice, devoting himself all the more to personal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he with He Rulin of Haiyan, Ling Kezhen of Wucheng, and Shen Lei of Gui'an mutually sharpened one another in study and practice, devoting himself all the more to personal conduct.

sentences.zh: 嘗以為聖人之於天道，「庸德之行，庸言之謹」，盡之矣。

translations.literal: He once held that the sage's relation to the Way of Heaven—'the conduct of ordinary virtue, the caution of ordinary speech'—fully expresses it.
translations.idiomatic: He once held that the sage's relation to the Way of Heaven—'the conduct of ordinary virtue, the caution of ordinary speech'—fully expresses it.

sentences.zh: 來學之士，一以友道處之。

translations.literal: Students who came to learn he treated entirely by the Way of friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came to learn he treated entirely by the Way of friendship.

sentences.zh: 謂門人當務經濟之學，著補農書。

translations.literal: He said disciples should devote themselves to practical learning and wrote Supplement to Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He said disciples should devote themselves to practical learning and wrote Supplement to Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 歲耕田十餘畝，草履箬笠，提筐佐饁。

translations.literal: Each year he plowed more than ten mu of fields, wearing straw sandals and a bamboo hat, carrying a basket to help with meals in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he plowed more than ten mu of fields, wearing straw sandals and a bamboo hat, carrying a basket to help with meals in the fields.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「人須有恆業。

translations.literal: He once said: "A man must have a constant occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "A man must have a constant occupation.

sentences.zh: 無恆業之人，始於喪其本心，終於喪其身。

translations.literal: A man without a constant occupation begins by losing his original mind and ends by losing his person.
translations.idiomatic: A man without a constant occupation begins by losing his original mind and ends by losing his person.

sentences.zh: 許魯齋有言：『學者以治生為急。』

translations.literal: Master Xu Luqi said: 'For students, managing livelihood is urgent.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Xu Luqi said: 'For students, earning a living is urgent.'

sentences.zh: 愚謂治生以稼穡為先。

translations.literal: I hold that in managing livelihood, farming and planting come first.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in earning a living, farming comes first.

sentences.zh: 能稼穡則可以無求於人，無求於人，則能立廉恥；

translations.literal: If one can farm and plant, one can be without asking from others; if without asking from others, one can establish integrity and shame;
translations.idiomatic: If one can farm, one need not depend on others; if one need not depend on others, one can uphold integrity and a sense of shame;

sentences.zh: 知稼穡之艱難，則不妄求於人，不妄求於人，則能興禮讓。

translations.literal: knowing the hardship of farming and planting, one will not rashly ask from others; if not rashly asking from others, one can promote ritual and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: knowing the hardship of farming, one will not rashly beg from others; if one does not rashly beg from others, one can promote ritual and yielding.

sentences.zh: 廉恥立，禮讓興，而人心可正，世道可隆矣。」

translations.literal: When integrity and shame are established and ritual and yielding arise, the human heart can be rectified and the age can be elevated.
translations.idiomatic: When integrity and shame are established and ritual and yielding arise, the human heart can be rectified and the age can be elevated.

sentences.zh: 初講宗周慎獨之學，晚乃專意程、朱。

translations.literal: At first he lectured on Zongzhou's learning of vigilance in solitude; in his later years he devoted himself solely to the Cheng and Zhu school.
translations.idiomatic: At first he lectured on Zongzhou's learning of vigilance in solitude; in his later years he devoted himself solely to the Cheng and Zhu school.

sentences.zh: 踐履篤實，學術純正。

translations.literal: His practice was earnest and solid, his learning pure and correct.
translations.idiomatic: His practice was earnest and solid, his learning pure and correct.

sentences.zh: 大要以為仁為本，以修己為務，而以中庸為歸。

translations.literal: In general he took benevolence as the root, self-cultivation as the task, and the Mean as the goal.
translations.idiomatic: In general he took benevolence as the root, self-cultivation as the task, and the Mean as the goal.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he died at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 著有原學記、讀易筆記、讀史偶記、言行見聞錄、經正錄、初學備忘、近古錄、訓子語、補農書、喪葬雜錄、訓門人語及文集四十五卷。

translations.literal: His writings included Record on the Origins of Learning, Notes on Reading the Changes, Occasional Notes on Reading History, Record of Words, Deeds, Things Seen and Heard, Correct Record of the Classics, Memoranda for Beginning Study, Record of Near Antiquity, Instructions to My Sons, Supplement to the Agricultural Treatise, Miscellaneous Records on Mourning and Burial, Instructions to Disciples, and a collected writings in forty-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Record on the Origins of Learning, Notes on Reading the Changes, Occasional Notes on Reading History, Record of Words, Deeds, Things Seen and Heard, Correct Record of the Classics, Memoranda for Beginning Study, Record of Near Antiquity, Instructions to My Sons, Supplement to the Agricultural Treatise, Miscellaneous Records on Mourning and Burial, Instructions to Disciples, and a collected writings in forty-five juan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，從祀文廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi, he was enshrined in the Confucian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi, he was enshrined in the Confucian Temple.

sentences.zh: 履祥初兄事顏統。

translations.literal: At first Lvxiang treated Yan Tong as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: At first Lvxiang treated Yan Tong as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 周鍾之寓桐鄉也，至其門者踵接。

translations.literal: When Zhou Zhong lodged in Tongxiang, those who came to his gate followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Zhong lodged in Tongxiang, visitors came to his gate in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 統曰：「鍾為人浮偽，不宜為所惑。」

translations.literal: Tong said: "Zhong as a man is superficial and false; one should not be misled by him."
translations.idiomatic: Tong said: "Zhong as a man is superficial and false; one should not be misled by him."

sentences.zh: 履祥嘗曰：「自得士鳳，而始聞過。

translations.literal: Lvxiang once said: "Since obtaining Shifeng, I first began to hear of my faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lvxiang once said: "Since obtaining Shifeng, I first began to hear of my faults.

sentences.zh: 餘不失足於周鍾、張溥之門者，皆其力也。」

translations.literal: That I did not set foot in the gates of Zhou Zhong and Zhang Pu was all due to his effort."
translations.idiomatic: That I did not set foot in the gates of Zhou Zhong and Zhang Pu was all due to his effort."

sentences.zh: 寅，字子虎。

translations.literal: Yin, courtesy name Zihu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yin, styled Zihu.

sentences.zh: 與履祥為硯席交。

translations.literal: He and Lvxiang were companions at desk and mat.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lvxiang were close companions at desk and mat.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸未冬，海寧祝淵以抗疏論救劉宗周被逮，履祥與寅送之吳門。

translations.literal: In the winter of the guiwei year of Chongzhen, Zhu Quan of Haining was arrested for submitting a memorial in protest to save Liu Zongzhou; Lvxiang and Yin escorted him to Wu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the guiwei year of Chongzhen, Zhu Quan of Haining was arrested for submitting a memorial in protest to save Liu Zongzhou; Lvxiang and Yin escorted him to Wu Gate.

sentences.zh: 次年，遂偕詣宗周門受業焉。

translations.literal: The next year they then together went to Zongzhou's gate to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they then together went to Zongzhou's gate to receive instruction.

sentences.zh: 自是寅造履益謹，寇盜充斥不廢學。

translations.literal: From then on Yin visited Lvxiang with even greater care, and though bandits and robbers filled the land he did not abandon his studies.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Yin visited Lvxiang with even greater care, and though bandits and robbers filled the land he did not abandon his studies.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 汝霖，字商隱，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Rulin, courtesy name Shangyin, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: He Rulin, styled Shangyin, was from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 嘗與友人曰：「周、程、張、朱一脈，吾輩不可令斷絕。」

translations.literal: He once said to a friend: "The lineage of Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu must not be allowed to break off among us.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to a friend: "The lineage of Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu must not be allowed to break off among us.

sentences.zh: 居喪三年，未嘗飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: In mourning for three years he never drank wine or ate meat.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for three years he never drank wine or ate meat.

sentences.zh: 隱居澉浦紫雲村，學者稱紫雲先生。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion at Ziyun Village in Ganpu; scholars called him Master Ziyun.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion at Ziyun Village in Ganpu; scholars called him Master Ziyun.

sentences.zh: 履祥子維恭，嘗受業於汝霖、克貞之門。

translations.literal: Lvxiang's son Weigong once received instruction at the gates of Rulin and Kezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Lvxiang's son Weigong once received instruction at the gates of Rulin and Kezhen.

sentences.zh: 又有吳璜、安道、邱雲，皆履祥友，並命維恭師事焉。

translations.literal: There were also Wu Huang, Andao, and Qiu Yun, all friends of Lvxiang, and he ordered Weigong to take them all as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Wu Huang, Andao, and Qiu Yun, all friends of Lvxiang, and he ordered Weigong to take them all as teachers.

sentences.zh: 曰：「數人皆深造自得，君子人也。」

translations.literal: He said: "These several men all attained deep cultivation and self-understanding; they are men of the gentlemanly type.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "These several men all attained deep cultivation and self-understanding; they are men of the gentlemanly type.

sentences.zh: 璜，秀水人。

translations.literal: Huang was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was a native of Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 剛直好義，勢利不動心。

translations.literal: Upright and fond of righteousness, gain and advantage did not move his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and fond of righteousness, gain and advantage did not move his heart.

sentences.zh: 安道​​，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Andao was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Andao was a native of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 雲，桐鄉人。

translations.literal: Yun was a native of Tongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a native of Tongxiang.

sentences.zh: 安道​​嘗言：「君子之異於小人，中國之異於夷狄，人類之異於禽獸，有禮無禮而已。

translations.literal: Andao once said: "How the gentleman differs from the petty man, how China differs from the barbarians, how humanity differs from birds and beasts—it is only a matter of having ritual or not.
translations.idiomatic: Andao once said: "How the gentleman differs from the petty man, how China differs from the barbarians, how humanity differs from birds and beasts—it is only a matter of having ritual or not.

sentences.zh: 士何可不學禮？」

translations.literal: How can a scholar not study ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: How can a scholar not study ritual?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「東林諸公，大抵是重名節。

translations.literal: He also said: "The gentlemen of Donglin, broadly speaking, valued name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The gentlemen of Donglin, broadly speaking, valued name and integrity.

sentences.zh: 然止數君子，餘皆有名而無節也。」

translations.literal: Yet only a few were true gentlemen; the rest had name but no integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Yet only a few were true gentlemen; the rest had name but no integrity."

sentences.zh: 克貞，字渝安，烏程人。

translations.literal: Kezhen, courtesy name Yu'an, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Kezhen, styled Yu'an, was from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 履祥交最篤。

translations.literal: His friendship with Lvxiang was the closest.
translations.idiomatic: His friendship with Lvxiang was the closest.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「父子兄弟安得人人大中、明道、伊川，夫婦安得人人伯鸞、德曜，在處之得其道耳。」

translations.literal: He once said: "How can every father and son be like Da Zhong, Mingdao, and Yichuan, or every husband and wife like Bo Luan and De Yao—it lies only in treating one another according to the proper Way.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "How can every father and son be like Da Zhong, Mingdao, and Yichuan, or every husband and wife like Bo Luan and De Yao—it lies only in treating one another according to the proper Way.

sentences.zh: 與履祥遊蕺山之門者，有屠安世、鄭宏。

translations.literal: Those who with Lvxiang traveled to the gate of Jishan included Tu Anshi and Zheng Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Those who with Lvxiang traveled to the gate of Jishan included Tu Anshi and Zheng Hong.

sentences.zh: 安世，秀水人。

translations.literal: Anshi was a native of Xiushui.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Anshi was a native of Xiushui.

sentences.zh: 聞宗周講學，喜曰：「苟不聞道，虛生何為！」

translations.literal: Hearing that Zongzhou was lecturing, he rejoiced and said: "If one does not hear the Way, what is the use of living in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Zongzhou was lecturing, he rejoiced and said: "If one does not hear the Way, what is the use of living in vain!

sentences.zh: 遂執贄納拜焉。

translations.literal: He then presented his gift and entered as a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented his gift and entered as a disciple.

sentences.zh: 宗周既歿，從父兄偕隱於海鹽之鄉。

translations.literal: After Zongzhou died, he followed his father and elder brothers in withdrawing together to the countryside of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongzhou died, he followed his father and elder brothers in withdrawing together to the countryside of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 病作，不粒食者十有七年。

translations.literal: When illness came upon him, he went without grain food for seventeen years.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came upon him, he went without grain food for seventeen years.

sentences.zh: 得宗周書，力疾鈔錄。

translations.literal: Obtaining Zongzhou's writings, he copied them out despite his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Obtaining Zongzhou's writings, he copied them out despite his illness.

sentences.zh: 反躬責己，無時或怠。

translations.literal: He turned inward and blamed himself, never slackening for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: He turned inward and blamed himself, never slackening for a moment.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「朝聞夕死，何敢不勉！」

translations.literal: He once said: "Hear in the morning and die in the evening—how dare one not exert oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Hear in the morning and die in the evening—how dare one not exert oneself!"

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 宏，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Hong was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Hong was a native of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 與弟景元俱從劉宗周受業，篤於友愛。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Jingyuan he received instruction from Liu Zongzhou and was earnest in brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his younger brother Jingyuan he received instruction from Liu Zongzhou and was earnest in brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 景元短世。

translations.literal: Jingyuan died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan died young.

sentences.zh: 乙酉後絕意進取，躬灌園蔬養母，屢空，晏如也。

translations.literal: After the yiyou year he abandoned all thought of advancement, personally watered garden vegetables to support his mother, often destitute, yet perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After the yiyou year he abandoned all thought of advancement, personally watered garden vegetables to support his mother, often destitute, yet perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 敝衣草履，不以屑意。

translations.literal: Wearing worn clothes and straw sandals, he did not regard it as beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing worn clothes and straw sandals, he did not regard it as beneath him.

sentences.zh: 嘗徒跣行雨中，人不能識也。

translations.literal: He once walked barefoot in the rain, and people could not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: He once walked barefoot in the rain, and people could not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 洤，字人齋，海寧人。

translations.literal: Quan, courtesy name Renzhai, was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quan, styled Renzhai, was from Haining.

sentences.zh: 乾隆丙辰舉人。

translations.literal: A juren in the bingchen year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren in the bingchen year of the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 私淑履祥，為梓其遺書。

translations.literal: Privately admiring Lvxiang, he printed his posthumous writings.
translations.idiomatic: Privately admiring Lvxiang, he printed his posthumous writings.

sentences.zh: 所纂有淑艾錄。

translations.literal: What he compiled includes Records of Cultivating Goodness.
translations.idiomatic: What he compiled includes Records of Cultivating Goodness.

sentences.zh: 吳蕃昌、沈磊在孝友傳。

translations.literal: Wu Fanchang and Shen Lei are in the Biographies of Filial Piety and Friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fanchang and Shen Lei are in the Biographies of Filial Piety and Friendship.

sentences.zh: 沈昀，字朗思，本名蘭先，字甸華，仁和人。

translations.literal: Shen Yun, courtesy name Langsi, original name Lanxian, styled Dianhua, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yun, styled Langsi, originally named Lanxian and also styled Dianhua, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 劉宗周講學蕺山，昀渡江往聽。

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhou lectured at Jishan; Yun crossed the river to go and listen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongzhou lectured at Jishan; Yun crossed the river to go and listen.

sentences.zh: 與應撝謙友。

translations.literal: He was a friend of Ying Huiqian.
translations.idiomatic: He was a friend of Ying Huiqian.

sentences.zh: 其學以誠敬為宗，以適用為主，而力排二氏。

translations.literal: His learning took sincerity and reverence as its principle, practical application as its main theme, and forcefully rejected the two schools.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took sincerity and reverence as its principle, practical application as its main theme, and forcefully rejected the two schools.

sentences.zh: 家貧絕炊，掘階前馬蘭草食之。

translations.literal: His family was so poor that cooking ceased; he dug the horse orchid grass before the steps and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: His family was so poor that cooking ceased; he dug the horse orchid grass before the steps and ate it.

sentences.zh: 鄰有遺之米者，昀宛轉推辭，忽僕於地，其人驚駭潛去。

translations.literal: A neighbor brought him rice; Yun tactfully declined, then suddenly fell to the ground; the man, startled and terrified, slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor brought him rice; Yun tactfully declined, then suddenly fell to the ground; the man, startled and terrified, slipped away.

sentences.zh: 良久方甦，因笑曰：「其意可感，然適以困我。」

translations.literal: After a long while he revived and then laughed, saying: "His intent is moving, yet it just troubles me.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he revived and then laughed, saying: "His intent is moving, yet it just troubles me.

sentences.zh: 撝謙歎曰：「我於交接之際，自謂不苟。

translations.literal: Huiqian sighed and said: "In social dealings I consider myself not careless.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian sighed and said: "In social dealings I consider myself not careless.

sentences.zh: 以視沈先生，猶覺愧之。」

translations.literal: Compared with Master Shen, I still feel ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Master Shen, I still feel ashamed."

sentences.zh: 宗周身後傳其學者頗滋諍訟。

translations.literal: After Zongzhou's death those who transmitted his learning rather multiplied lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongzhou's death those who transmitted his learning rather multiplied lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 昀曰：「尼父言『躬行君子』，若騰其口說以求勝，非所望於吾也。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "Confucius spoke of 'the gentleman who acts in person'; if one raises one's mouth to speak in order to win, that is not what is hoped for from us.
translations.idiomatic: Yun said: "Confucius spoke of 'the gentleman who acts in person'; if one raises one's mouth to speak in order to win, that is not what is hoped for from us.

sentences.zh: 以喪禮久廢，緝士喪禮說，以授同郡陸寅。

translations.literal: Because mourning rites had long been abandoned, he compiled Expositions on the Scholar's Mourning Rites and transmitted them to fellow townsman Lu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Because mourning rites had long been abandoned, he compiled Expositions on the Scholar's Mourning Rites and transmitted them to fellow townsman Lu Yin.

sentences.zh: 疾革，門人問曰：「夫子今日何如？」

translations.literal: When his illness grew critical, a disciple asked: "Master, how are you today?"
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical, a disciple asked: "Master, how are you today?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「心中無一物，惟誠敬而已。」

translations.literal: He said: "In my heart there is nothing at all—only sincerity and reverence."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "In my heart there is nothing at all—only sincerity and reverence."

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 窮無以為殮，撝謙涕泣不知所出。

translations.literal: So poor that there was nothing for the encoffining, Huiqian wept and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: So poor that there was nothing for the encoffining, Huiqian wept and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 曰：「我不敢輕授賻襚，以汙先生。」

translations.literal: He said: "I dare not lightly bestow funeral gifts, lest I defile the master.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I dare not lightly bestow funeral gifts, lest I defile the master.

sentences.zh: 其門人姚宏任趨進曰：「如宏任者，可以殮先生乎？」

translations.literal: His disciple Yao Hongren hurried forward and said: "One like Hongren—can he encoffin the master?"
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Yao Hongren hurried forward and said: "One like Hongren—can he encoffin the master?"

sentences.zh: 撝謙曰：「子篤行，殆可也。」

translations.literal: Huiqian said: "You are earnest in conduct; perhaps you may."
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian said: "You are earnest in conduct; perhaps you may."

sentences.zh: 姚遂殮之，葬於湖上。

translations.literal: Yao then encoffined him and buried him by the lake.
translations.idiomatic: Yao then encoffined him and buried him by the lake.

sentences.zh: 宏任，字敬恆，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Hongren, courtesy name Jingheng, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hongren, styled Jingheng, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母，賢婦也。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, his mother was a virtuous woman.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, his mother was a virtuous woman.

sentences.zh: 宏任隱巿廛，其母偶見貿絲銀色下劣，慍甚，曰：「汝亦為此乎？」

translations.literal: Hongren hid himself in the marketplace; his mother once saw that the silver color of the silk he traded was inferior and was greatly angry, saying: "You also do this?
translations.idiomatic: Hongren hid himself in the marketplace; his mother once saw that the silver color of the silk he traded was inferior and was greatly angry, saying: "You also do this?

sentences.zh: 宏任長跪謝，原得改行，乃受業於撝謙。

translations.literal: Hongren knelt long in apology, willing to change his occupation, and then received instruction under Huiqian.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren knelt long in apology, willing to change his occupation, and then received instruction under Huiqian.

sentences.zh: 日誦大學一過，一言一行，服膺師說，遇事必歸於忠厚。

translations.literal: Daily he recited the Great Learning once through; in every word and action he kept close to his teacher's doctrine, and in affairs always returned to what was generous and honest.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he recited the Great Learning once through; in every word and action he kept close to his teacher's doctrine, and in affairs always returned to what was generous and honest.

sentences.zh: 撝謙不輕受人物，惟宏任之餽不辭。

translations.literal: Huiqian did not lightly accept things from others, but he did not decline Hongren's gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian did not lightly accept things from others, but he did not decline Hongren's gifts.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾知其非不義也。」

translations.literal: He said: "I know they are not unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "I know they are not unrighteous."

sentences.zh: 宏任每時其乏而致之，終身不倦。

translations.literal: Hongren each time waited until Huiqian was in need and then presented them, never tiring throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren each time waited until Huiqian was in need and then presented them, never tiring throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 撝謙卒，執喪如古師弟子之禮。

translations.literal: When Huiqian died, he observed mourning according to the ancient rites between teacher and disciple.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiqian died, he observed mourning according to the ancient rites between teacher and disciple.

sentences.zh: 姚江黃宗炎許之曰：「是篤行傳中人也。」

translations.literal: Huang Zongyan of Yaojiang approved him, saying: "This is a man of the Biography of Earnest Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongyan of Yaojiang approved him, saying: "This is a man of the Biography of Earnest Conduct.

sentences.zh: 晚年以非罪陷縲絏。

translations.literal: In his later years he was imprisoned on a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was imprisoned on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 憲使閱囚入獄，宏任方朗誦大學，憲使異之，入其室，皆程、朱書；

translations.literal: The provincial judge entered the prison to review the prisoners; Hongren was just reciting the Great Learning aloud; the judge was astonished, entered his room, and found only books of the Cheng and Zhu school;
translations.idiomatic: The provincial judge entered the prison to review the prisoners; Hongren was just reciting the Great Learning aloud; the judge was astonished, entered his room, and found only books of the Cheng and Zhu school;

sentences.zh: 與之語，大驚，即日釋之。

translations.literal: speaking with him, he was greatly startled and released him that same day.
translations.idiomatic: speaking with him, he was greatly startled and released him that same day.

sentences.zh: 然宏任卒以貧死。

translations.literal: Yet Hongren in the end died in poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hongren in the end died in poverty.

sentences.zh: 葉敦艮，字靜遠，西安人。

translations.literal: Ye Dungen, courtesy name Jingyuan, was a native of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Dungen, styled Jingyuan, was from Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 劉宗周弟子。

translations.literal: A disciple of Liu Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was a disciple of Liu Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗貽書陸世儀，討論學術。

translations.literal: He once sent a letter to Lu Shiyi discussing learning.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent a letter to Lu Shiyi discussing learning.

sentences.zh: 世儀喜曰：「證人尚有緒言，吾得慰未見之憾矣。」

translations.literal: Shiyi rejoiced and said: "The Zhengren school still has surviving words; I am able to comfort the regret of not having met."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi rejoiced and said: "The Zhengren school still has surviving words; I am able to comfort the regret of not having met."

sentences.zh: 劉汋，字伯繩，宗周子。

translations.literal: Liu Zhuo, courtesy name Bosheng, was the son of Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhuo, styled Bosheng, was Liu Zongzhou's son.

sentences.zh: 宗周家居講學，諸弟子聞教未達，輒私於汋。

translations.literal: When Zongzhou lectured at home, if disciples heard the teaching but did not grasp it, they would consult Zhuo privately.
translations.idiomatic: While Zongzhou taught at home, any disciple who failed to grasp a point would seek Zhuo out in private.

sentences.zh: 汋應機開譬，具有條理。

translations.literal: Zhuo responded according to the occasion with illuminating explanations, all well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo would meet each question on its own terms and unfold it with lucid, well-ordered explanations.

sentences.zh: 宗周殉國難，明唐、魯二王皆遣使祭，廕汋官，汋辭。

translations.literal: When Zongzhou died for the national calamity, both the Tang and Lu princes of Ming sent envoys to sacrifice; they offered Zhuo an inherited office, and Zhuo declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongzhou perished in the dynastic crisis, the Tang and Lu princes of the Ming each sent envoys to offer sacrifice and sought to grant Zhuo an inherited office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 既葬，居蕺山一小樓二十年，杜門絕人事，考訂遺經，以竟父業。

translations.literal: After the burial, he lived in a small tower on Jishan for twenty years, shut his door to all worldly affairs, collated and revised the surviving classics, and thereby completed his father's work.
translations.idiomatic: Once the funeral rites were done, he spent twenty years in a small pavilion on Mount Ji, sealing himself off from the world while collating his father's unfinished classics to bring that legacy to completion.

sentences.zh: 有司或請見，雖通家故舊，亦峻拒之。

translations.literal: When officials sometimes requested an audience, even close family friends he sternly refused.
translations.idiomatic: If local officials asked to see him, he turned them away coldly—even old friends from connected families.

sentences.zh: 所與接者，惟史孝感、惲日初數人。

translations.literal: Those with whom he associated were only Shi Xiaoxian, Yun Ruchu, and a few others.
translations.idiomatic: The only men he kept company with were Shi Xiaoxian, Yun Ruchu, and a handful of others.

sentences.zh: 或勸之舉講會，不應。

translations.literal: Some urged him to hold lecture meetings; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When people urged him to convene public lectures, he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 臨卒，戒其子曰：「若等安貧讀書，守人譜以終身足矣。」

translations.literal: Near death, he admonished his sons, saying: "You need only be content in poverty, read books, and keep to the Renpu for life.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he warned his sons: "Be content in poverty, keep reading, and live your lives according to the Renpu—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 人譜，宗周所著書。

translations.literal: Renpu was a book written by Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Renpu was a work composed by Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 所臥之榻，假之祁氏。

translations.literal: The couch on which he slept was borrowed from the Qi family.
translations.idiomatic: The bed he slept on belonged to the Qi family and was only on loan to him.

sentences.zh: 疾亟，強起易之，曰：「吾豈可終於祁氏之榻？」

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he forced himself to rise and change it, saying: "How can I end my days on the Qi's couch?"
translations.idiomatic: As the illness turned grave, he roused himself to have it replaced, saying, "How can I die on a couch borrowed from the Qis?"

sentences.zh: 應撝謙，字潛齋，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Ying Huiqian, courtesy name Qianzhai, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Huiqian, styled Qianzhai, came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: Filial devotion ran to the core of his character.

sentences.zh: 殫心理學，以躬行實踐為主，不喜陸、王家言。

translations.literal: He devoted himself utterly to Neo-Confucian learning, taking personal practice as the foundation and disliking the teachings of the Lu and Wang schools.
translations.idiomatic: He poured himself into moral philosophy, grounding everything in lived practice and having little use for the Lu and Wang lineages.

sentences.zh: 足跡不出百里，隘屋短垣，貧甚，恬如也。

translations.literal: His footsteps never went beyond a hundred li; in a narrow house with low walls he was very poor, yet perfectly content.
translations.idiomatic: He rarely traveled more than fifty miles from home, lived in a cramped cottage behind a low wall, and was desperately poor—yet utterly at peace.

sentences.zh: 杭州知府嵇宗孟數式廬，欲有所贈，囁嚅未出；

translations.literal: Hangzhou prefect Ji Zongmeng often paid ceremonial visits; he wished to make a gift, but hesitated and the words never came out.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zongmeng, prefect of Hangzhou, often called on him with formal courtesy and wanted to offer him something, but always faltered before the words left his lips.

sentences.zh: 及讀撝謙所作無悶先生傳，乃不敢言，

translations.literal: After reading Huiqian's Biography of Master Wumen, he no longer dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had read Huiqian's Biography of Master Wumen, he never again ventured to broach the subject of gifts.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，詔徵博學鴻儒，大臣項景襄、張天馥交章薦之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, an edict summoned Broad Learning and Eloquence scholars; the grand ministers Xiang Jingxiang and Zhang Tianfu jointly memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, when an edict went out summoning men of broad learning and eloquence, the grand ministers Xiang Jingxiang and Zhang Tianfu jointly recommended him.

sentences.zh: 撝謙輿床以告有司曰：「撝謙非敢卻薦，實病不能行耳！」

translations.literal: Huiqian was carried on a bed to tell the officials: "Huiqian does not dare refuse the recommendation; I am truly too ill to travel!
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian had himself carried on a couch to the yamen and told the officials: "It is not that I dare refuse the recommendation—I am genuinely too ill to travel!

sentences.zh: 客有勸者曰：「昔太山孫明復嘗因石介等請，以成丞相之賢，何果於卻薦哉？」

translations.literal: A guest who urged him said: "In former times Sun Mingfu of Mount Tai once accepted the invitation through Shi Jie and others in order to fulfill the prime minister's virtue—why be so adamant in refusing recommendation?
translations.idiomatic: One visitor pressed him: "Sun Mingfu of Mount Tai once accepted nomination at the urging of Shi Jie and the rest so that a worthy chief minister might be served—why be so stubborn about declining?

sentences.zh: 撝謙曰：「我不能以我之不可，學明復之可。」

translations.literal: Huiqian said: "I cannot take what I am not capable of and imitate what Mingfu was capable of.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqian replied: "I cannot take my own incapacity and pretend it is Mingfu's capacity.

sentences.zh: 乃免徵。

translations.literal: Thus he was exempted from summons.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he was excused from the summons.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year of the reign, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 撝謙於易、書、詩、禮、樂、春秋、孝經、四書各有著說。

translations.literal: Huiqian had separate treatises on the Changes, Documents, Poetry, Rites, Music, Spring and Autumn, Classic of Filial Piety, and the Four Books.
translations.idiomatic: For each of the Changes, Documents, Poetry, Rites, Music, Spring and Autumn, Classic of Filial Piety, and Four Books, Huiqian wrote his own commentary.

sentences.zh: 又撰教養全書四十一卷，分選舉、學校、治官、田賦、水利、國計、漕運、治河、師役、鹽法十考，略仿文獻通考，而於明代事實尤詳。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Comprehensive Book on Nurturing and Education in forty-one juan, divided into ten examinations—selection, schools, governance of officials, field tax, waterworks, state finance, grain transport, river control, military service, and salt law—roughly modeled on the Comprehensive Examination of Literature, but especially detailed on Ming facts.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Comprehensive Book on Nurturing and Education in forty-one juan, organized into ten topical surveys—on selection, schools, official administration, land tax, irrigation, state finance, grain transport, river works, military service, and the salt monopoly—loosely following the Comprehensive Examination of Literature but with particular fullness on Ming institutions.

sentences.zh: 其不載律算者，以徐光啟已有成書；

translations.literal: That he did not include law and calculation was because Xu Guangqi already had completed works.
translations.idiomatic: He omitted law and mathematics because Xu Guangqi had already produced authoritative books in those fields.

sentences.zh: 不載輿地者，以顧炎武、顧祖禹方事纂輯也。

translations.literal: That he did not include geography was because Gu Yanwu and Gu Zuyu were then engaged in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He left out geography because Gu Yanwu and Gu Zuyu were already at work on that subject.

sentences.zh: 又有性理大中二十八卷。

translations.literal: He also had Great Harmony of Human Nature in twenty-eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Great Harmony of Human Nature in twenty-eight juan.

sentences.zh: 門人錢塘凌嘉邵、沈士則傳其學。

translations.literal: His disciples Ling Jiashao of Qiantang and Shen Shize transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Ling Jiashao of Qiantang and Shen Shize carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 朱鶴齡，字長孺，吳江人。

translations.literal: Zhu Heling, courtesy name Zhangru, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Heling, styled Zhangru, came from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A Ming student.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 穎敏嗜學，嘗箋注杜甫、李商隱詩，盛行於世。

translations.literal: Quick-witted and devoted to learning, he once annotated Du Fu's and Li Shangyin's poetry, which circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and insatiably studious, he produced commentaries on the poetry of Du Fu and Li Shangyin that won wide circulation.

sentences.zh: 鼎革後，屏居著述。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change, he withdrew to his home and devoted himself to writing.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming he retired from public life and wrote in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 晨夕一編，行不識途路，坐不知寒暑。

translations.literal: Morning and evening with one book in hand, walking he did not know the road, sitting he did not know cold or heat.
translations.idiomatic: He read from dawn to dusk with a book always in hand, so absorbed that on the road he lost his way and at his desk he forgot cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 人或謂之愚，遂自號愚菴。

translations.literal: When people called him foolish, he styled himself the Hermit of Folly.
translations.idiomatic: When others mocked him as a fool, he took the sobriquet Hermit of Folly.

sentences.zh: 嘗自謂「疾惡如仇，嗜古若渴。

translations.literal: He once said of himself: "I hate evil as an enemy and love antiquity as if thirsty.
translations.idiomatic: He described himself this way: "I hate wickedness as one hates a personal enemy, and I thirst for antiquity as for water.

sentences.zh: 不妄受人一錢，不虛誑人一語」云。

translations.literal: I do not rashly accept a single cash from others, nor falsely deceive others with a single word."
translations.idiomatic: I never take a penny I have not earned, and I never tell a man a lie."

sentences.zh: 著愚庵詩文集。

translations.literal: He wrote the Collected Poetry and Prose of the Hermit of Folly.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yu'an shiwen ji, the collected poetry and prose of the Hermit of Folly.

sentences.zh: 初為文章之學，及與顧炎武友，炎武以本原相勗，乃湛思覃力於經註疏及儒先理學。

translations.literal: At first he pursued the study of belles-lettres; after becoming friends with Gu Yanwu, Yanwu urged him with the fundamentals, and he then plunged deep effort into classic commentaries and exegesis and the Neo-Confucian learning of earlier sages.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a literary scholar, but once Gu Yanwu became his friend and pressed him toward first principles, he turned his full energy to classical commentaries and the moral philosophy of the earlier masters.

sentences.zh: 以易理至宋儒已明，然左傳、國語所載佔法，皆言像也，本義精矣，而多未備，撰易廣義​​略四卷。

translations.literal: Because the principles of the Changes had already been clarified by Song Confucians, yet the divinatory methods recorded in the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States all speak of images, and though the original meaning was refined much remained incomplete, he wrote Outline of the Extended Meaning of the Changes in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that Song scholars had already clarified the Changes in principle, but that the divinatory methods preserved in the Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States all turn on hexagram images—and that the original meaning, though refined, was still incomplete—he wrote Outline of the Extended Meaning of the Changes in four juan.

sentences.zh: 以蔡氏釋書未精，斟酌於漢學、宋學之間，撰尚書埤傳十七卷。

translations.literal: Because Cai's exegesis of the Documents was not refined, he weighed Han and Song learning and wrote Extended Commentary on the Venerated Documents in seventeen juan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Cai Shen's commentary on the Documents insufficiently rigorous, he balanced Han and Song approaches and wrote Extended Commentary on the Venerated Documents in seventeen juan.

sentences.zh: 以朱子掊擊詩小序太過，與同縣陳啟源參考諸家說，兼用啟源說，疏通序義，撰詩經通義二十卷。

translations.literal: Because Zhu Xi attacked the Small Preface to the Poetry too severely, he consulted various scholars' views together with Chen Qiyuan of the same county, also using Qiyuan's views, clarified the meaning of the Preface, and wrote Comprehensive Meaning of the Classic of Poetry in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Zhu Xi had been too harsh on the Small Preface to the Poetry, he worked through the commentarial tradition with his fellow townsman Chen Qiyuan, incorporated Qiyuan's insights, clarified the Preface's meaning, and produced Comprehensive Meaning of the Classic of Poetry in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 以胡氏傳春秋多偏見鑿說，乃合唐、宋以來諸儒之解，撰春秋集說二十二卷。

translations.literal: Because Hu's commentary on the Spring and Autumn contained many biased and forced interpretations, he combined explanations of Tang and Song scholars and wrote Collected Explanations of the Spring and Autumn in twenty-two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hu An'guo's Spring and Autumn commentary was riddled with partisan and forced readings, he gathered Tang and Song interpretations into Collected Explanations of the Spring and Autumn in twenty-two juan.

sentences.zh: 又以杜氏注左傳未盡合，俗儒又以林氏注紊之，詳證參考，撰讀左日鈔十四卷。

translations.literal: Also because Du's commentary on the Zuo Commentary was not entirely correct and vulgar scholars further confused it with Lin's commentary, he verified and consulted in detail and wrote Daily Notes on Reading the Zuo in fourteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Du Yu's Zuo Commentary not wholly reliable and popular scholars further muddled it with Lin's commentary, he sifted the evidence carefully and wrote Daily Notes on Reading the Zuo in fourteen juan.

sentences.zh: 又有禹貢長箋十二卷，作於胡渭禹貢錐指之前，雖不及渭書，而備論古今利害，旁引曲證，亦多創獲。

translations.literal: He also had Extended Commentary on the Tribute of Yu in twelve juan, written before Hu Wei's Pointed Commentary on the Tribute of Yu; though it did not match Hu's book, in fully discussing ancient and modern advantages and harms, with side citations and indirect proofs, it also yielded many original findings.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Extended Commentary on the Tribute of Yu in twelve juan, earlier than Hu Wei's Pointed Commentary on the Tribute of Yu; it fell short of Hu's work, yet in weighing ancient and modern costs and benefits, with wide citation and indirect argument, it produced many fresh insights.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒。

translations.literal: In his seventies and more he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 啟源，字長發。

translations.literal: Qiyuan, courtesy name Changfa.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiyuan, styled Changfa.

sentences.zh: 著有毛詩稽古編。

translations.literal: He wrote Investigating Antiquity in the Mao Classic of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Investigating Antiquity in the Mao Classic of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 其詮釋經旨，一準毛傳，而鄭箋佐之。

translations.literal: In interpreting the meaning of the classics, he took the Mao Commentary as standard and used Zheng Xuan's commentary to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: In explicating the classics he treated the Mao Commentary as normative and drew on Zheng Xuan's glosses as support.

sentences.zh: 訓詁聲音以爾雅為主，草木蟲魚以陸疏為則，於漢學可謂專門。

translations.literal: For glosses and pronunciation he took the Erya as primary; for plants, insects, and fish he took Lu's Commentary as model—in Han learning he may be called a specialist.
translations.idiomatic: For lexical glosses and pronunciation he relied chiefly on the Erya; for flora and fauna he followed Lu Ji—making him a specialist in Han exegetical learning.

sentences.zh: 又有尚書辨略二卷，讀書偶筆二卷，存耕堂藁四卷。

translations.literal: He also had Outline of the Documents in two juan, Occasional Notes on Reading in two juan, and Drafts from the Cun Geng Hall in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Outline of the Documents in two juan, Occasional Notes on Reading in two juan, and Drafts from the Cun Geng Hall in four juan.

sentences.zh: 范鎬鼎，字彪西，洪洞人。

translations.literal: Fan Gaoding, courtesy name Biaoxi, was a native of Hongdong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Gaoding, styled Biaoxi, came from Hongdong.

sentences.zh: 性孝友，闡明絳州辛全之學。

translations.literal: By nature filial and friendly, he elucidated the learning of Xin Quan of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and brotherly by nature, he carried forward the teaching of Xin Quan of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士，以母老不仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi, a jinshi, he did not take office because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kangxi, Though he passed the jinshi examination, he declined office because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 河、汾間人士多從之受經。

translations.literal: Many scholars between the Yellow and Fen Rivers received the classics from him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the Yellow and Fen river region studied the classics under him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以博學鴻儒薦，未起。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was recommended as Broad Learning and Eloquence but did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was recommended for the Broad Learning and Eloquence examination but never took up appointment.

sentences.zh: 立希賢書院，置田贍學者。

translations.literal: He established the Xixian Academy and set aside fields to support scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Xixian Academy and endowed fields to support students.

sentences.zh: 輯理學備考三十卷，廣理學備考四十八卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Reference Materials for Neo-Confucian Learning in thirty juan and Expanded Reference Materials for Neo-Confucian Learning in forty-eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Reference Materials for Neo-Confucian Learning in thirty juan and its expanded sequel in forty-eight juan.

sentences.zh: 國朝理學備考二十六卷，採辛全、孫奇逢、熊賜履、張夏、黃宗羲諸家緒綸，附以己說，議論醇正。

translations.literal: Reference Materials for Neo-Confucian Learning of the Dynasty in twenty-six juan gathered the threads of Xin Quan, Sun Qifeng, Xiong Cilü, Zhang Xia, Huang Zongxi, and other schools, appended his own views, and the discussions were pure and correct.
translations.idiomatic: His Reference Materials for Neo-Confucian Learning of the Dynasty in twenty-six juan drew together the strands of Xin Quan, Sun Qifeng, Xiong Cilü, Zhang Xia, Huang Zongxi, and others, added his own commentary, and the resulting discussions were sober and upright.

sentences.zh: 又著五經堂文集五卷，語錄一卷。

translations.literal: He also wrote Collected Works of the Five Classics Hall in five juan and Recorded Sayings in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Collected Works of the Five Classics Hall in five juan and Recorded Sayings in one juan.

sentences.zh: 又以其父芸茂有垂棘編，作續垂棘編十九卷，三晉詩選四十卷。

translations.literal: Also because his father Yunmao had the Chuiji compilation, he wrote Continuation of the Chuiji in nineteen juan and Selected Poetry of the Three Jin in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Yunmao had compiled the Chuiji, he produced a Continuation of the Chuiji in nineteen juan and a Selected Poetry of the Three Jin in forty juan.

sentences.zh: 同時為辛全之學者，有絳州党成、李生光。

translations.literal: Contemporaries who studied Xin Quan's learning included Dang Cheng and Li Shengguang of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Among his contemporaries who followed Xin Quan's teaching were Dang Cheng and Li Shengguang of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 成，字憲公。

translations.literal: Cheng, courtesy name Xiangong.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Cheng, styled Xiangong.

sentences.zh: 其學以明理去私為本。

translations.literal: His learning took clarifying principle and removing selfishness as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching rested on clarifying moral principle and stripping away private desire.

sentences.zh: 生平不求人知，鎬鼎曾揚之於人，意甚不懌，時目為狷者。

translations.literal: All his life he did not seek to be known; when Gaoding once praised him to others, he was very displeased, and people of the time regarded him as an uncompromising man.
translations.idiomatic: He never courted recognition in life; when Gaoding once commended him publicly he was deeply offended, and contemporaries marked him as a man of uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 其辨朱、陸異同：「論者多以陸為尊德性，朱為道問學。

translations.literal: In his discrimination of the differences and sameness of Zhu and Lu: "Discussants mostly take Lu as honoring moral nature and Zhu as pursuing learning through inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In distinguishing Zhu Xi from Lu Jiuyuan he wrote: "Commentators usually say Lu honored innate moral nature while Zhu pursued learning through inquiry.

sentences.zh: 此言殊未然。

translations.literal: This statement is quite not so.
translations.idiomatic: That formulation misses the mark.

sentences.zh: 蓋朱子之道問學，實以尊德性也，陸氏則自錮其德性矣，何尊之可云？

translations.literal: For Zhu's pursuing learning through inquiry in fact takes honoring moral nature as its aim; Lu's school instead imprisoned its moral nature—how can one speak of honoring it?
