translations.idiomatic: Zhu's path of inquiry through learning was itself aimed at honoring moral nature; Lu's school, by contrast, caged that nature—what honor is there to speak of?

sentences.zh: 陸子嘗曰：『不求本根，馳心外物，理豈在於外物乎？』

translations.literal: Master Lu once said: 'If one does not seek the root and base but sets the heart on external things, how can principle lie in external things?
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu once said, 'Without seeking one's root and base, the mind races after external things—can principle really lie outside the self?

sentences.zh: 此告子義外之學也。

translations.literal: This is the learning of Gaozi that makes righteousness external.
translations.idiomatic: That is Gaozi's doctrine of external righteousness.

sentences.zh: 朱子曰：『本心物理，原無內外。

translations.literal: Master Zhu said: 'The original mind and physical principle originally have no inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi replied, 'Mind and principle know no inner-outer divide.

sentences.zh: 以外物為外者，是告子義外之學也。』

translations.literal: To take external things as external is the learning of Gaozi that makes righteousness external.
translations.idiomatic: To treat external things as wholly outside is Gaozi's doctrine of external righteousness.

sentences.zh: 即此數語，可以見二家之異同矣。

translations.literal: From these few words one can see the differences and sameness of the two schools.
translations.idiomatic: In those few sentences the contrast between the two schools stands clear.

sentences.zh: 若粗論其同，二家皆欲扶世教，崇天理，去私慾，其秉心似無大異者。

translations.literal: If one roughly discusses their sameness, both schools wished to support worldly teaching, exalt heavenly principle, and remove selfish desire; in their fundamental intent they seem not greatly different.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, both schools sought to uphold public morality, reverence heavenly principle, and purge selfish desire—their underlying aims seem much the same.

sentences.zh: 而實究其學，則博文約禮者，孔、顏之家法，屢見於論語，朱子得其正矣。

translations.literal: But when one truly investigates their learning, 'broad in culture and precise in ritual' is the family method of Confucius and Yan Hui, repeatedly seen in the Analects—Zhu obtained the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a close reading shows that 'broad in culture and disciplined in ritual'—the household method of Confucius and Yan Hui, repeated throughout the Analects—is the path Zhu truly inherited.

sentences.zh: 陸氏乃言『六經皆我註腳』，又言『不識一字，管取​​堂堂作大丈夫』。

translations.literal: Lu's school then said 'the Six Classics are all footnotes to me,' and also said 'not knowing a single character, one can still stand forth as a great man.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's followers went so far as to say 'the Six Classics are all annotations to me,' and even 'without knowing a single character one may still stand tall as a true man.

sentences.zh: 豈不偏哉！」

translations.literal: Is this not biased!
translations.idiomatic: Surely that is one-sided!

sentences.zh: 其辨論如此。

translations.literal: His argument was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his argument.

sentences.zh: 生光，字闇章。

translations.literal: Shengguang, courtesy name Anzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengguang, styled Anzhang.

sentences.zh: 未冠為諸生。

translations.literal: Before coming of age he became a student.
translations.idiomatic: He became a licentiate before he had even come of age.

sentences.zh: 辛全倡學河、汾，遂往受業。

translations.literal: When Xin Quan advocated learning between the Fen and Yellow Rivers, he went to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Quan opened his school in the Fen-Yellow region, Shengguang went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 篤於內行，事親至孝，全深重之。

translations.literal: Devoted in inner conduct, filial to parents to the utmost, Quan deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous in private conduct and profoundly filial, he won Xin Quan's highest regard.

sentences.zh: 明亡，絕意仕進，自號汾曲逸民。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, he abandoned all thought of office and styled himself the Recluse of the Fen Bend.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming collapse he renounced official ambition and called himself the Recluse of the Fen Bend.

sentences.zh: 構一草堂，日夕讀書其中，以二南大義，程、朱微言，訓門弟子。

translations.literal: He built a thatched hall and day and night read books therein, instructing disciples with the great meaning of the Two Souths and the subtle words of the Cheng and Zhu school.
translations.idiomatic: He built a grass-thatched study, read there from morning to night, and taught disciples the moral core of the Two Souths and the fine points of the Cheng-Zhu tradition.

sentences.zh: 著有儒教辨正、崇正黜邪彙編，凡萬餘言。

translations.literal: He wrote Rectifying Confucian Teaching and Collected Writings for Honoring the Correct and Rejecting the Heterodox, altogether more than ten thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Rectifying Confucian Teaching and Collected Writings for Honoring the Correct and Rejecting the Heterodox, totaling more than ten thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 白奐彩，字含貞，華州人。

translations.literal: Bai Huancai, courtesy name Hanzhen, was a native of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Huancai, styled Hanzhen, came from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 私淑於長安馮從吾，玩易洗心，詩、禮、春秋，多所自得。

translations.literal: He privately revered Feng Congwu of Chang'an, cultivated the Changes to cleanse the mind, and in Poetry, Rites, and Spring and Autumn gained much of his own insight.
translations.idiomatic: Though he never studied directly under Feng Congwu of Chang'an, he revered him as a master, used the Changes to purify the mind, and reached many independent insights in the Poetry, Rites, and Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 蓄書之富，陝以西罕儷。

translations.literal: The wealth of books he stored was rarely matched west of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His library was among the richest anywhere west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 校讎精詳，淹貫靡遺。

translations.literal: Collating was precise and detailed; his erudition was thorough and nothing omitted.
translations.idiomatic: His textual collation was meticulous, his learning wide and nothing left unattended.

sentences.zh: 而衝遜自將，若一無所知。

translations.literal: Yet he was humble and self-restrained, as if knowing nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he carried himself with such modest reserve that he seemed to know nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 與同州黨湛、蒲城王化泰諸人相切叚。

translations.literal: He closely associated with Dang Zhan of Tongzhou, Wang Huatai of Pucheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He kept close company with Dang Zhan of Tongzhou, Wang Huatai of Pucheng, and others.

sentences.zh: 率同志結社，不入城巿，不謁官府，終日晏坐一室，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Leading like-minded men he formed a society, did not enter cities or markets, did not visit officials, and all day sat quietly in one room with hand never leaving the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered kindred spirits into a fellowship, shunned towns and markets, never called on magistrates, and spent whole days seated in one room, book never out of hand.

sentences.zh: 同知郝斌式廬，聆奐彩論議，退而歎曰：「關中文獻也！」

translations.literal: Assistant prefect Hao Bin paid a ceremonial visit; hearing Huancai's discourse, he withdrew and sighed: "The literary tradition of Guanzhong!"
translations.idiomatic: Assistant prefect Hao Bin came on a formal visit; after hearing Huancai discourse he withdrew and exclaimed, "Here is the literary soul of Guanzhong!"

sentences.zh: 湛，字子澄。

translations.literal: Zhan, courtesy name Zicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Zhan, styled Zicheng.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「人生須作天地間第一等事，為天地間第一等人。」

translations.literal: He once said: "In life one must do the foremost deed under heaven and be the foremost person under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He once declared: "A man must perform the highest work in the world and become the highest kind of man in the world.

sentences.zh: 故自號兩一。

translations.literal: Therefore he styled himself Liangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Hence his sobriquet: Liangyi, 'the two foremost.'

sentences.zh: 究宋、明以來諸儒論學語，揭其會心者於壁，默坐土室，澄心反觀，久之，恍然有契。

translations.literal: He investigated the discourse on learning of Song and Ming Confucians, posted those that struck his heart on the wall, sat silently in an earthen chamber, clarified the mind and turned inward to observe, and after long time suddenly attained comprehension.
translations.idiomatic: He studied how Song and Ming scholars had talked about learning, copied the passages that moved him onto his wall, and in a plain earthen room sat in silence, clarifying the mind and turning inward until, after long effort, understanding came in a flash.

sentences.zh: 自是動靜雲為，卓有柄持。

translations.literal: From then on in movement and stillness, in speech and action, he had a firm handle on things.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, whether in stillness or action, his conduct had a firm center.

sentences.zh: 聞李顒倡道盩厔，冒雪履冰，不憚數百里訪質所學。

translations.literal: Hearing that Li Yong advocated the Way in Zhouzhi, he braved snow and tread ice, not fearing several hundred li to visit and test what he had learned.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Li Yong was teaching in Zhouzhi, he crossed snow and ice and traveled hundreds of miles without hesitation to put his learning to the test.

sentences.zh: 相與盤桓數日，每至夜半，未嘗見惰容。

translations.literal: They lingered together for several days, often until midnight, and he was never seen with a lazy countenance.
translations.idiomatic: They kept company for days, often talking until midnight, and never once did he show a slack or weary face.

sentences.zh: 其志篤養邃如此。

translations.literal: His will was thus earnest and his self-cultivation deep.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his resolve and the seriousness of his self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 化泰，字省庵。

translations.literal: Huatai, courtesy name Sheng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huatai, styled Sheng'an.

sentences.zh: 性方嚴峭直，面斥人過，辭色不少貸。

translations.literal: By nature stern, strict, and upright, he rebuked others' faults to their faces and never softened his words or expression.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and unyielding by nature, he confronted people's faults to their faces and never softened his tone.

sentences.zh: 人有一長，即欣然推遜，自以為不及。

translations.literal: If someone had a single strength, he would gladly defer and yield, thinking himself inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if someone possessed even one genuine merit, he would gladly step aside and praise that person as his better.

sentences.zh: 關學初以馬嗣煜嗣馮從吾，而奐彩、湛、化泰皆有名於時。

translations.literal: At first Guan learning was continued by Ma Siyu after Feng Congwu, while Huancai, Zhan, and Huatai were all famous in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong learning had first passed from Feng Congwu to Ma Siyu; Huancai, Zhan, and Huatai were all celebrated figures of their day.

sentences.zh: 武功馮雲程、康賜呂、張承烈，同州李士濱、張珥，朝邑王建常、關獨可，咸寧羅魁，韓城程良受，蒲城甯維垣，邠州王吉相，淳化宋振麟，皆篤志勵學，得知行合一之旨。

translations.literal: Feng Yuncheng, Kang Silü, and Zhang Chengli of Wugong; Li Shibin and Zhang Er of Tongzhou; Wang Jianchang and Guan Duk of Chaoyi; Luo Kui of Xianning; Cheng Liangshou of Hancheng; Ning Weiyuan of Pucheng; Wang Jixiang of Binzhou; Song Zhenlin of Chunhua—all were earnest in will and diligent in learning, attaining the meaning of unity of knowledge and action.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yuncheng, Kang Silü, and Zhang Chengli of Wugong; Li Shibin and Zhang Er of Tongzhou; Wang Jianchang and Guan Duk of Chaoyi; Luo Kui of Xianning; Cheng Liangshou of Hancheng; Ning Weiyuan of Pucheng; Wang Jixiang of Binzhou; Song Zhenlin of Chunhua—all pursued learning with fierce devotion and grasped the ideal of uniting knowledge and action.

sentences.zh: 至乾隆間，武功孫景烈亦能接關中學者之傳。

translations.literal: By the Qianlong period, Sun Jinglie of Wugong was also able to carry on the transmission of Guanzhong scholars.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qianlong reign, Sun Jinglie of Wugong was still able to carry forward the Guanzhong scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 景烈，字酉峰。

translations.literal: Jinglie, courtesy name Youfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jinglie, styled Youfeng.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三年進士，授檢討，以言事放歸。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianlong, a jinshi, appointed compiler, and dismissed for memorializing on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianlong, he passed the jinshi examination, served as a Hanlin compiler, and was sent home after speaking out on policy.

sentences.zh: 教生徒以克己復禮。

translations.literal: He taught students to restrain the self and return to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his students to restrain the self and return to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 居平雖盛暑必肅衣冠。

translations.literal: In ordinary life, even in the height of summer he always wore formal dress.
translations.idiomatic: Even in midsummer he always kept to formal dress.

sentences.zh: 韓城王杰為入室弟子。

translations.literal: Wang Jie of Hancheng was his closest disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie of Hancheng was his foremost disciple.

sentences.zh: 嘗語人曰：「先生冬不爐，夏不扇，如邵康節；

translations.literal: He once told others: "The master uses no brazier in winter and no fan in summer, like Shao Kangjie;
translations.idiomatic: He once said of his teacher: "In winter he used no brazier, in summer no fan—like Shao Kangjie;

sentences.zh: 學行如薛文清。」

translations.literal: his learning and conduct are like Xue Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: his learning and conduct were worthy of Xue Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「先生歸籍三十年，雖不廢講學，獨絕聲氣之交。

translations.literal: He also said: "The master returned to his native place for thirty years; though he never ceased lecturing, he entirely cut off connections for reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "For thirty years after returning home the master never stopped teaching, yet he refused every tie built on mere reputation.

sentences.zh: 為關中學者宗，有自來矣。」

translations.literal: As the patriarch of Guanzhong scholars, this had been so from the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: As the acknowledged head of Guanzhong learning, that standing was his from the start."

sentences.zh: 胡承諾，字君信，天門人。

translations.literal: Hu Chengnuo, courtesy name Junxin, was a native of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chengnuo, styled Junxin, came from Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎舉人。

translations.literal: A Ming Chongzhen-era provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the provincial examination in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 國變後，隱居不仕，臥天門巾、柘間，

translations.literal: After the dynastic change, he lived in seclusion and did not serve, dwelling between Tianmen's Jin and Zhe hills.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic change he refused office and lived in retirement among the Jin and Zhe hills of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，部銓縣職。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi year twelve, the Board of Personnel assigned him a county post.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year twelve, the Board of Personnel assigned him a county post.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，檄徵入都。

translations.literal: In Kangxi year five, an official summons ordered him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year five, an official summons ordered him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，至京師，以詩呈侍郎嚴正矩云：「垂老只思還舊業，暮年所急匪輕肥。」

translations.literal: In the sixth year he reached the capital and presented a poem to Vice Minister Yan Zhengju, saying: "In old age I think only of returning to my former work; what urgency in one's later years is not light comfort and gain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he reached Beijing and presented a poem to Vice Minister Yan Zhengju: "In old age I think only of returning to my old calling; what a man needs in his later years is not ease and profit.

sentences.zh: 既而告歸，得請。

translations.literal: Soon after he requested leave to return and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to go home and was permitted to leave.

sentences.zh: 構石莊於西村，自號石莊老人。

translations.literal: He built the Stone Villa in the western village and styled himself the Old Man of the Stone Villa.
translations.idiomatic: He built Stone Villa in a western village and styled himself the Old Man of the Stone Villa.

sentences.zh: 窮年誦讀，於書無所不窺，而深自韜晦。

translations.literal: Year after year he read and recited; there was no book he did not examine, yet he deeply concealed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He read year round, leaving no book unexamined, yet kept himself deeply hidden from the world.

sentences.zh: 晚著繹志。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote the Exposition of Intent.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote the Exposition of Intent.

sentences.zh: 繹志者，繹己所志也。

translations.literal: Exposition of Intent means expounding what one intends.
translations.idiomatic: The title Exposition of Intent means to unfold what one sets one's heart upon.

sentences.zh: 凡聖賢、帝王、名臣、賢士與凡民之志業，莫不兼綜條貫，原本道德，切近人情，酌古而宜今，為有體有用之學。

translations.literal: Whether the aspirations and undertakings of sages, emperors, famous ministers, worthy scholars, or common people, he comprehensively organized them, rooted them in morality, close to human feeling, weighing the ancient to suit the present—a learning with substance and use.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed the aims and careers of sages, emperors, great ministers, worthy scholars, and ordinary people alike, grounding everything in moral principle, keeping it close to human feeling, and weighing antiquity against the present to produce a learning both principled and practical.

sentences.zh: 凡二十餘萬言，皆根柢於諸經，博稽於諸史，旁羅百家，而折衷於周、程、張、朱之說。

translations.literal: Altogether more than two hundred thousand characters, all rooted in the classics, broadly consulting the histories, gathering in the hundred schools, and reconciling them with the teachings of Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The work runs to more than two hundred thousand characters, rooted in the classics, drawing on the histories, ranging across the hundred schools, and reconciling them with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 承諾自擬其書於徐幹中論、顏之推家訓，然其精粹奧衍，非二書所及也。

translations.literal: Chengnuo compared his book to Xu Gan's Balanced Discourses and Yan Zhitui's Family Instructions, yet its essence and depth exceed those two books.
translations.idiomatic: Chengnuo likened the book to Xu Gan's Balanced Discourses and Yan Zhitui's Family Instructions, yet in subtlety and depth it surpasses both.

sentences.zh: 二十六年六月，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 所著有讀書說六卷，文體類淮南、抱朴，麟雜細碎，隨事觀理而體察之，殆繹志取材之餘，與是書相表裡。

translations.literal: His writings include Reading Notes in six juan; the style resembles the Huainanzi and Baopuzi, miscellaneous and minute, observing principle in each matter—probably material left from composing the Exposition of Intent, complementing that book.
translations.idiomatic: He also left Reading Notes in six juan, written in a style reminiscent of the Huainanzi and Baopuzi—miscellaneous, minute observations on whatever came to hand, likely surplus material from the Exposition of Intent and its natural companion.

sentences.zh: 曹本榮，字欣木，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Cao Benrong, courtesy name Xinmu, was a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Benrong, styled Xinmu, came from Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，改翰林院庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, a jinshi, he was changed to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shunzhi, After passing the jinshi examination he entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 布袍蔬食，以清節自勵。

translations.literal: In cloth robe and plain food, he took integrity as his discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He wore plain cloth and ate simple food, holding himself to a standard of austere integrity.

sentences.zh: 八年，授秘書院編修。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed compiler of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed a compiler in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 應詔，上聖學疏千言，其略云：「皇上得二帝三王之統，則當以二帝三王之學為學。

translations.literal: Responding to an edict, he submitted a memorial on sagely learning of a thousand words; the gist was: "Your Majesty has received the succession of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; then you should take the learning of the Two Emperors and Three Kings as your learning.
translations.idiomatic: Answering an edict, he submitted a thousand-word memorial on sagely learning: "Your Majesty has inherited the mandate of the Two Emperors and Three Kings; you should therefore make their learning your own.

sentences.zh: 誠宜開張聖聽，修德勤學，舉四書、五經及通鑑中有裨身心要務治平大道者，內則深宮燕閒，朝夕討論，外則經筵進講，敷對周詳。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open wide your sagely hearing, cultivate virtue and study diligently, selecting from the Four Books, Five Classics, and Comprehensive Mirror passages that benefit mind and body, essential affairs of governance, and the great Way of order—within, in the inner palace during leisure, discussing morning and evening; without, lecturing at the classics mat, answering comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: Open your ears to counsel, cultivate virtue, and study diligently. From the Four Books, Five Classics, and Comprehensive Mirror choose what nourishes mind and body and what bears on the great Way of governance—in the inner palace discuss it morning and evening, and at the classics mat expound it fully.

sentences.zh: 君德既修，祈天永命，必基於此。」

translations.literal: Once the ruler's virtue is cultivated, praying Heaven for enduring mandate must be based on this.
translations.idiomatic: Once the ruler's virtue is cultivated, the prayer for Heaven's enduring mandate must rest on this foundation.

sentences.zh: 有詔嘉納。

translations.literal: An edict praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne issued an edict of praise and acceptance.

sentences.zh: 十年，擢右春坊右贊善兼國子監司業，刊白鹿洞學規以教士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Companion of the Eastern Palace and concurrently Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, printing the Rules of Bailudong Academy to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was promoted to Right Assistant Companion of the Eastern Palace and concurrently Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and had the Rules of Bailudong Academy printed to instruct students.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉中允。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Approver.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Approver.

sentences.zh: 十二年，世祖甄拔詞臣品端學裕者充日講官，本榮與焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Shizu Emperor selected literary officials of upright character and ample learning to serve as daily lecturers; Benrong was among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Shizu Emperor selected upright, learned members of the Hanlin to serve as daily lecturers, and Benrong was among them.

sentences.zh: 十三年，升秘書院侍講、左春坊左庶子兼侍讀，日侍講幄，辨論經義。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Secretariat Reader, Left Assistant Companion of the Eastern Palace and concurrent Lecturer, daily attending the lecture curtain and debating the meaning of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he rose to Secretariat Reader, Left Assistant Companion of the Eastern Palace and concurrent Lecturer, attending the lecture curtain daily to debate classical meaning.

sentences.zh: 敕本榮同傅以漸撰易經通註九卷，鎔鑄眾說，詞理簡明，為說經之圭臬。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Fu Yijian to compile the Comprehensive Commentary on the Classic of Changes in nine juan, fusing many explanations with concise and clear reasoning, becoming the standard for explaining the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Fu Yijian to compile the Comprehensive Commentary on the Classic of Changes in nine juan, fusing many schools into clear, concise exposition that became the standard for classical commentary.

sentences.zh: 本榮又著五大儒語、周張精義、王羅擇編諸書。

translations.literal: Benrong also wrote Sayings of the Five Great Confucians, Essential Meaning of Zhou and Zhang, and Selected Compilation of Wang and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Benrong also wrote Sayings of the Five Great Confucians, Essential Meaning of Zhou and Zhang, and Selected Compilation of Wang and Luo.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，充順天鄉試正考官，九月，充經筵講官，十一月，以失察同考官作弊，部議革職，上以其侍從講幄日久，宥之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year he served as chief examiner of the Shuntian provincial examination; in the ninth month he served as classics mat lecturer; in the eleventh month, for failure to detect cheating by a co-examiner, the Board recommended dismissal, but the emperor pardoned him because he had long served at the lecture curtain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he served as chief examiner of the Shuntian provincial examination in the eighth month and as classics mat lecturer in the ninth; in the eleventh month the Board recommended his dismissal for failing to detect a co-examiner's cheating, but the emperor pardoned him for his long service at the lecture curtain.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷翰林院侍讀學士，改國史院侍讀學士，

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Hanlin Reader and then to Reader in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was transferred to Hanlin Reader and then to Reader in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，以病請回籍，卒於揚州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, on grounds of illness he requested return to his native place and died in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kangxi, he later asked to return home on grounds of illness and died in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 本榮之學，從陽明致知之說，故論次五大儒，以程、朱、薛與陸、王並行。

translations.literal: Benrong's learning followed the Yangming doctrine of extending knowledge; therefore in arranging the Five Great Confucians he placed Cheng, Zhu, and Xue on equal footing with Lu and Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Benrong's learning followed Wang Yangming's doctrine of extending innate knowledge, so in his arrangement of the Five Great Confucians he placed Cheng, Zhu, and Xue on a par with Lu and Wang.

sentences.zh: 既告歸，宦橐蕭然，晏如也。

translations.literal: After he retired, his official purse was empty, yet he was perfectly content.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement his official funds were gone, yet he was entirely at peace.

sentences.zh: 疾革，門生計東在側，猶教以窮理盡性之學。

translations.literal: When critically ill, his disciple Ji Dong was at his side; he still taught the learning of exhausting principle and fully realizing nature.
translations.idiomatic: Even on his deathbed, with his disciple Ji Dong at his side, he still taught the learning of exhausting principle and fully realizing nature.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，容城孫奇逢痛惜之。

translations.literal: On the day he died, Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his death Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 子宜溥，由廕生薦舉博學鴻儒，試，授檢討。

translations.literal: His son Yipu, through inherited student status, was recommended for Broad Learning and Eloquence; after the examination he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yipu, by inherited student status, was recommended for Broad Learning and Eloquence and, after examination, was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 張貞生，字簣山，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhensheng, courtesy name Guishan, was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhensheng, styled Guishan, came from Luling.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，官翰林院侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, a jinshi, he served as Hanlin Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, a jinshi, he served as Hanlin Reader.

sentences.zh: 時議遣大臣巡察，貞生上書諫。

translations.literal: When the court debated dispatching grand ministers on inspection tours, Zhensheng submitted a memorial remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated sending grand ministers on inspection tours, Zhensheng submitted a memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 召對，所言又過戇。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, his words were again overly blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, his words proved blunt to the point of rashness.

sentences.zh: 下考功議，革職為民，蒙恩鐫二級去官。

translations.literal: The Board of Personnel deliberated and stripped him of office, reducing him to commoner; by grace his rank was reduced two grades and he left office.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Personnel recommended stripping him of office and reducing him to commoner status; by imperial grace he was merely reduced two ranks and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 初闡陽明良知之說，其後乃一宗考亭。

translations.literal: At first he expounded Yangming's doctrine of innate knowledge; afterward he took Kaoting as his sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: He had first expounded Wang Yangming's doctrine of innate knowledge, but later acknowledged Kaoting alone.

sentences.zh: 居京師，寓吉安館中，蓬蒿滿徑，突無炊煙。

translations.literal: Living in the capital, he lodged in the Ji'an hostel; weeds filled the path and no cooking smoke rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he lodged at the Ji'an hostel, where weeds choked the path and no smoke rose from the stove.

sentences.zh: 瀕行不能具裝，故人餽贐，一無所受，其狷介如此。

translations.literal: When about to leave he could not assemble travel gear; friends offered parting gifts but he accepted none—such was his uncompromising integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to leave he could not even assemble travel clothes; friends offered parting gifts, but he refused every one—such was his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋奉特旨起補原官。

translations.literal: Soon a special edict recalled him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a special edict recalled him to his former post.

sentences.zh: 至京，卒。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the capital and died there.

sentences.zh: 著庸書二十卷，玉山遺響集。

translations.literal: He wrote Commonplace Writings in twenty juan and the Collection of Resonances from Mount Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He left Commonplace Writings in twenty juan and the Collection of Resonances from Mount Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉原淥，字昆石，安丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanlu, courtesy name Kunshi, was a native of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanlu, styled Kunshi, came from Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 明末盜賊蜂起，原淥與仲兄某率鄉人壘土為堡以御賊。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, bandits rose everywhere; Yuanlu and his second elder brother led the villagers to pile earth into a fort to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming, bandits swarmed the countryside; Yuanlu and his second elder brother led the villagers to pile earth into a fort for defense.

sentences.zh: 賊至，守堡者多死。

translations.literal: When bandits came, many defending the fort died.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived, many defenders of the fort were killed.

sentences.zh: 仲兄出鬥，身中九矢，力戰。

translations.literal: The second elder brother went out to fight, took nine arrows in his body, and battled fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: His second brother went out to fight, took nine arrows, and battled on.

sentences.zh: 原淥從之，發數十矢，矢盡，仲兄麾之去。

translations.literal: Yuanlu followed him, shot several dozen arrows; when the arrows were exhausted, the second elder brother ordered him to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlu followed, loosing dozens of arrows; when they were spent his brother ordered him to retreat.

sentences.zh: 原淥大呼曰：「離兄一步非死所。」

translations.literal: Yuanlu shouted loudly: "One step from my brother is no place to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanlu shouted: "Any step away from my brother is no place for me to die!

sentences.zh: 乃斬二渠帥，獲馬六匹，賊遁去。

translations.literal: He then beheaded two bandit chiefs, obtained six horses, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut down two bandit chiefs, seized six horses, and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 亂定，以力耕致富。

translations.literal: When order was restored, he grew wealthy through hard farming.
translations.idiomatic: After order returned he grew prosperous through hard farming.

sentences.zh: 既而推膏腴與兄，以其餘為長兄立後，兼贍亡姊家。

translations.literal: Then he yielded the best land to his brother, used the remainder to establish an heir for his eldest brother, and also supported his deceased sister's family.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave the best fields to his brother, used what remained to establish an heir for his eldest brother, and supported his deceased sister's household.

sentences.zh: 謝人事，求長生之術。

translations.literal: He withdrew from worldly affairs and sought the art of longevity.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from worldly affairs and sought the art of longevity.

sentences.zh: 得咯血疾，遂棄去。

translations.literal: When he contracted a hemoptysis illness, he abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: When he developed a coughing-blood illness, he abandoned that pursuit.

sentences.zh: 後讀宋儒書，乃篤信朱子之學，集朱子書作續近思錄。

translations.literal: Later reading Song Confucians, he came to believe firmly in Zhu Xi's learning and compiled Zhu Xi's writings into Continuation of Reflections on Things at Hand.
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading Song Confucians, he came to believe firmly in Zhu Xi's teaching and compiled Zhu Xi's writings into Continuation of Reflections on Things at Hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「學者居敬窮理，二者皆法先王而已。

translations.literal: He once said: "For scholars, reverent attentiveness and exhausting principle—both are simply modeling the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "For the scholar, reverent attentiveness and exhausting principle both mean nothing more than taking the former kings as model.

sentences.zh: 『小心翼翼，昭事上帝』，居敬之功也。

translations.literal: 'Be careful and fearful, serving the Lord on high'—that is the achievement of reverent attentiveness.
translations.idiomatic: 'Be careful and fearful in serving the Lord on High'—that is the work of reverent attentiveness.

sentences.zh: 『不識不知，順帝之則』，窮理之功也。」

translations.literal: 'Without knowing and without forcing, following the Lord's rule'—that is the achievement of exhausting principle.
translations.idiomatic: 'Without knowing and without forcing, following the Lord's rule'—that is the work of exhausting principle.

sentences.zh: 每五更起，謁祠後，與弟子講論，常至夜分。

translations.literal: Every day he rose at the fifth watch, after visiting the shrine discussed with disciples, often until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: He rose every day at the fifth watch, visited the family shrine, and lectured with disciples, often until midnight.

sentences.zh: 仲兄疾，籥天祈以身代。

translations.literal: When his second elder brother fell ill, he prayed to Heaven offering himself in his brother's place.
translations.idiomatic: When his second brother fell ill, he prayed to Heaven to take the illness upon himself.

sentences.zh: 兄死，三日內水漿不入口。

translations.literal: When his brother died, for three days he took no food or drink.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother died, he took no food or drink for three days.

sentences.zh: 又為鄉人置義倉，儉歲煮粥以食飢人。

translations.literal: He also established a charity granary for the villagers; in lean years he cooked porridge to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a charity granary for his village and in lean years cooked porridge to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「人與我一天而已，何畛域之有焉？」

translations.literal: He once said: "Others and I share one Heaven—what boundaries can there be?
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Others and I share one Heaven—what boundary can there be between us?

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 著讀書日記、四書近思續錄四卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Reading Diary and Continuation of Reflections on the Four Books in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left Reading Diary and Continuation of Reflections on the Four Books in four juan.

sentences.zh: 後數十年，昌樂有閻循觀、周士宏，濰縣有姜國霖、劉以貴、韓夢周，德州有孫於簠、梁鴻翥，膠州有法坤宏，同縣有張貞，猶能守原淥之學。

translations.literal: Several decades later, Yan Xunguan and Zhou Shihong of Changle, Jiang Guolin, Liu Yigui, and Han Mengzhou of Weixian, Sun Yufan and Liang Hongzhu of Dezhou, Fa Kunhong of Jiaozhou, and Zhang Zhen of the same county were still able to preserve Yuanlu's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Decades later, Yan Xunguan and Zhou Shihong of Changle; Jiang Guolin, Liu Yigui, and Han Mengzhou of Weixian; Sun Yufan and Liang Hongzhu of Dezhou; Fa Kunhong of Jiaozhou; and Zhang Zhen of the same county were still able to preserve Yuanlu's teaching.

sentences.zh: 國霖，字雲一，濰縣人。

translations.literal: Guolin, courtesy name Yunyi, was a native of Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Guolin, styled Yunyi, came from Weixian.

sentences.zh: 父客燕中感病，國霖往省，跣走千里，至則父已歿。

translations.literal: His father took ill while traveling in Yan and Guolin went to visit; he ran barefoot a thousand li, but when he arrived his father had already died.
translations.idiomatic: His father fell ill while traveling in the north; Guolin went to see him, running barefoot for a thousand li, but arrived to find him already dead.

sentences.zh: 無錢巿棺，以衣裹屍，負之行，乞食歸里。

translations.literal: Having no money to buy a coffin, he wrapped the corpse in clothing, carried it on his back, and begged food all the way home.
translations.idiomatic: Without money for a coffin, he wrapped the body in clothes, carried it on his back, and begged food all the way home.

sentences.zh: 泣告族黨曰：「父死不能斂，又不能葬，欲以身殉，又有老母在。

translations.literal: Weeping, he told the clan elders: "My father died and I could not encoffin him, nor yet bury him; I wish to die with him, but my old mother still lives.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he told the clan elders: "Father died and I could not encoffin or bury him; I wish to die with him, yet my old mother still lives.

sentences.zh: 長者何以教我？」

translations.literal: How should your elders instruct me?
translations.idiomatic: What counsel do you elders give me?

sentences.zh: 人憐其孝，為捐金以葬。

translations.literal: People pitied his filial piety and contributed money for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his filial devotion, the community collected money for the burial.

sentences.zh: 母易怒，一日怒甚，國霖作小兒嬉戲狀，長跪膝前，執母手，摑其面。

translations.literal: His mother was easily angered; one day when she was very angry, Guolin acted like a child at play, knelt long before her knees, took her hand, and lightly slapped her face.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had a quick temper; one day when she was furious, Guolin knelt before her like a playful child, took her hand, and gently patted her cheek.

sentences.zh: 母大笑，怒遂已，時年五十矣。

translations.literal: His mother laughed greatly and her anger then ceased; he was fifty years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: His mother burst out laughing and her fury subsided; he was fifty at the time.

sentences.zh: 師事昌樂周士宏，嘗與國霖至莒，樂其山川，死即葬於莒。

translations.literal: He took Zhou Shihong of Changle as his teacher; once he and Guolin went to Ju, delighted in its mountains and rivers, and when he died he was buried in Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Zhou Shihong of Changle; he and Guolin once visited Ju, fell in love with its landscape, and when he died he was buried there.

sentences.zh: 國霖築室墓側，安貧守素，不求於人。

translations.literal: Guolin built a room beside the tomb, kept to poverty and plain living, and sought nothing from others.
translations.idiomatic: Guolin built a cottage beside the grave, lived in poverty and simplicity, and asked nothing of anyone.

sentences.zh: 值歉歲，莒人恐其餓死，聞於官而周之粟，亦弗卻也。

translations.literal: In a lean year the people of Ju feared he would starve; they reported it to the officials and the county supplied him grain, and he did not refuse it either.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year the people of Ju feared he might starve, reported it to the magistrate, and when grain was sent he accepted it without refusal.

sentences.zh: 昌樂閻循觀問國霖喜讀何書，曰：「論語，終身味之不盡。」

translations.literal: Yan Xunguan of Changle asked Guolin what book he most liked to read; he said: "The Analects—one can savor it all one's life without exhausting it."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xunguan of Changle asked which book Guolin loved best; he answered: "The Analects—one could taste it for a lifetime and never exhaust it."

sentences.zh: 以貴，字滄嵐。

translations.literal: Yigui, courtesy name Canglan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yigui, styled Canglan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi, a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 任蒼梧令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 地瑤、僮雜處，營茶山書院，以詩、書為教。

translations.literal: The region had Yao and Zhuang peoples living together; he established the Chashan Academy and took Poetry and Documents as the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The district was mixed with Yao and Zhuang peoples; he founded the Chashan Academy and taught through the Poetry and Documents.

sentences.zh: 歸里後，杜門著書，有藜乘集。

translations.literal: After returning home he shut his door and wrote books, leaving the Licheng Collection.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he sealed himself off to write, leaving the Licheng Collection.

sentences.zh: 夢周，字公复。

translations.literal: Mengzhou, courtesy name Gongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mengzhou, styled Gongfu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Qianlong, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 其學以存養、省察、致知三者為入德之資。

translations.literal: His learning took preserving and nurturing, introspection, and extending knowledge as the three resources for entering virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching rested on preserving and nurturing, introspection, and extending knowledge as the three foundations of moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 每跬步必以禮，以恥求聞達為尚。

translations.literal: At every step he must observe ritual, and he honored shame at seeking fame and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He measured every step by ritual propriety and held it shameful to court fame and office.

sentences.zh: 後為來安知縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Lai'an and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Lai'an and won a reputation for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 長洲彭紹升稱其治來如元魯山。

translations.literal: Peng Shaosheng of Changzhou praised his governance of Lai'an as like that of Lu Shan of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shaosheng of Changzhou said his administration of Lai'an rivaled that of Lu Shan under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有理堂文集，表方名，獎忠節，皆有關於世道。

translations.literal: He had the Collected Works of the Hall of Principle, commending worthy names and rewarding loyalty and integrity—all relevant to the moral order of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Collected Works of the Hall of Principle, praising worthy men and honoring loyalty and integrity—writings all bearing on the moral health of the age.

sentences.zh: 鴻翥，字志南，德州人。

translations.literal: Hongzhu, courtesy name Zhinan, was a native of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hongzhu, styled Zhinan, came from Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 每治一經，案上不列他書。

translations.literal: Whenever he worked on one classic, he placed no other books on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: When studying any one classic, he kept no other book on his desk.

sentences.zh: 有疑義，思之累日夜，必得而後已。

translations.literal: When there was a doubtful point, he thought on it for days and nights on end and did not stop until he had resolved it.
translations.idiomatic: If a passage puzzled him, he would brood over it day and night until he had settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 益都李文藻一見奇之，為之延譽，遂知名於世。

translations.literal: Li Wenzao of Yidu was astonished at first sight and spread his reputation for him; thus he became known in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenzao of Yidu was struck by him at first meeting and spread his name, and so he became known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以優行貢成均。

translations.literal: Because of outstanding conduct he was recommended to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: On account of exemplary conduct he was recommended to the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有周易觀運等書。

translations.literal: He had Observing the Movement of the Changes and other books.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Observing the Movement of the Changes and other works.

sentences.zh: 坤宏，字鏡野，膠州人。

translations.literal: Kunhong, courtesy name Jingye, was a native of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fa Kunhong, styled Jingye, came from Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 得傳習錄，大喜，以為如己意所出。

translations.literal: When he obtained the Records for Practice and Transmission, he rejoiced greatly, thinking it exactly expressed what he himself had meant.
translations.idiomatic: When he obtained Wang Yangming's Records for Practice and Transmission, he was overjoyed, feeling it voiced exactly what he had long thought.

sentences.zh: 其學以陽明為宗，以不自欺為本。

translations.literal: His learning took Yangming as its patriarch and not deceiving oneself as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching took Wang Yangming as patriarch and sincerity with oneself as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年舉人，官大理評事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate, he served as reviewing censor in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate, he served as reviewing censor in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有奇。

translations.literal: He died, aged more than eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over eighty.

sentences.zh: 循觀，字懷庭，昌樂人。

translations.literal: Xunguan, courtesy name Huaiting, was a native of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xunguan, styled Huaiting, came from Changle.

sentences.zh: 專志洛、閩之學，省身克己，刻苦自立。

translations.literal: He devoted himself solely to the learning of Luoyang and Minzhou, examining himself and restraining the self, laboring hard to stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to the Luoyang and Fujian traditions, examining himself, restraining desire, and striving to stand on his own feet.

sentences.zh: 治經不立一家言，而要歸於自得。

translations.literal: In studying the classics he did not establish a single school's doctrine, but the essential aim was self-attainment.
translations.idiomatic: He did not bind himself to any one school's reading of the classics, but sought genuine self-possession.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十四年進士，吏部考功司主事。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, he served as secretary in the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, he served as secretary in the Bureau of Merit in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 著困勉齋私記、西澗文集及尚書春秋說。

translations.literal: He wrote Private Notes of the Striving in Adversity Studio, Collected Works of the Western Stream, and commentaries on the Documents and Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Private Notes of the Striving in Adversity Studio, Collected Works of the Western Stream, and commentaries on the Documents and Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 任瑗，字恕菴，淮安山陽人。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan, courtesy name Shuan, was a native of Shanyang, Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan, styled Shuan, came from Shanyang in Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 年十八，棄舉子業，講學。

translations.literal: At eighteen he abandoned the pursuit of examination essays and lectured on learning.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he gave up examination essays and devoted himself to teaching.

sentences.zh: 靜坐三年，歎曰：「聖人之道，歸於中庸，極於『精義入神以致用也，利用安身以崇德也』，豈是之謂哉？」，

translations.literal: After sitting in meditation for three years, he sighed and said: "The Way of the sages returns to the Mean and reaches its height in 'Refining meaning to enter the spirit in order to put it to use; putting use to the body in order to exalt virtue'—is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: After three years of silent meditation he sighed: "The sages' Way comes to rest in the Mean and rises to its height in 'Refining meaning to enter the spirit for practical use; putting use to the body to exalt virtue'—surely that is the point.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，大吏舉瑗應博學鴻詞，廷試罷歸。

translations.literal: In Qianlong 1, senior officials recommended Yuan to answer the Broad Learning and Eloquence summons; after the palace examination was finished, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1, senior officials recommended Ren Yuan for the Broad Learning and Eloquence examination; after the palace test he returned home without appointment.

sentences.zh: 韓夢周語人曰：「任君體用具備，有明以來無此鉅儒。」

translations.literal: Han Mengzhou told others: "Master Ren's substance and function are complete; since the Ming there has been no such great Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mengzhou told others: "Master Ren's substance and function are complete; since the Ming there has been no scholar of his stature.

sentences.zh: 及韓將北歸，瑗語之曰：「山左人多質直，君當接引後進，以續正學。」

translations.literal: When Han was about to return north, Yuan told him: "People of Shandong are mostly plain and straight; you should guide the younger generation and continue the orthodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was about to return north, Yuan told him: "Shandong men are plain and upright; you should guide the younger generation and carry on the orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 因作反經說以示之。

translations.literal: He therefore wrote the Discourse on Returning to the Classics to show him.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote the Discourse on Returning to the Classics and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 年八十二，卒。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 著有纂注朱子文類一百卷，論語困知錄二卷，反經說一卷，陽明傳習錄辨二卷，知言劄記二卷，朱子年譜一卷。

translations.literal: His writings include Annotated Compilation of Zhu Xi's Literary Categories in one hundred juan, Records of Painful Learning on the Analects in two juan, Discourse on Returning to the Classics in one juan, Discrimination of Yangming's Records for Practice and Transmission in two juan, Notes on Knowing Words in two juan, and Chronological Biography of Zhu Xi in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Annotated Compilation of Zhu Xi's Literary Categories in one hundred juan, Records of Painful Learning on the Analects in two juan, Discourse on Returning to the Classics in one juan, Discrimination of Yangming's Records for Practice and Transmission in two juan, Notes on Knowing Words in two juan, and Chronological Biography of Zhu Xi in one juan.

sentences.zh: 顏元，字易直，博野人。

translations.literal: Yan Yuan, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yuan, styled Yizhi, came from Boye.

sentences.zh: 明末，父戍遼東，歿於關外。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, his father was garrisoned in Liaodong and died beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming his father was posted to Liaodong and died beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 元貧無立錐，百計覓骨歸葬，世稱孝子。

translations.literal: Yuan was so poor he had not a foot of land; by every possible means he sought his father's bones for burial, and the world called him a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was destitute, without even a patch of ground to stand on; he tried every means to recover his father's remains for burial, and the world hailed him as a filial son.

sentences.zh: 居喪，守朱氏家禮惟謹。

translations.literal: During mourning he scrupulously observed the Zhu Family Rituals.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he scrupulously followed the Zhu Family Rituals.

sentences.zh: 古禮，「初喪，朝一溢米，夕一溢米，食之無算」。

translations.literal: The ancient rite says: "At the first mourning, one overflowing measure of rice in the morning and one in the evening, with eating without limit."
translations.idiomatic: The ancient rite says: "At the first mourning, one overflowing cup of rice in the morning and one in the evening, with eating without limit."

sentences.zh: 家禮刪去「無算」句，元遵之。

translations.literal: The Family Rituals deleted the phrase "without limit," and Yuan followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Family Rituals deleted the phrase "without limit," and Yuan obeyed.

sentences.zh: 過朝夕不敢食，當朝夕，遇哀至，又不能食，病幾殆。

translations.literal: He passed the morning and evening meals without daring to eat; at the appointed times for morning and evening, when grief came he could not eat, and he nearly died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped the morning and evening meals entirely; when grief seized him at those hours he could not eat at all, and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 又喪服傳：「既練，舍外寢，始食菜果。

translations.literal: Also the Record of Mourning Garments says: "After the second year of mourning, leave the outer chamber, begin eating vegetables and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Mourning Garments also says: "After the second year of mourning, leave the outer chamber and begin eating vegetables and fruit.

sentences.zh: 飯素食，哭無時。」

translations.literal: Eat plain food, weep without fixed times.
translations.idiomatic: Eat plain food and weep without fixed times.

sentences.zh: 家禮改為「練後，止朝夕哭，惟朔望未除者會哭，凡哀至皆制不哭」。

translations.literal: The Family Rituals changed this to: "After the second year of mourning, stop weeping at morning and evening; only on the first and fifteenth of the month do those not yet out of mourning gather to weep; whenever grief comes, all must restrain themselves and not weep."
translations.idiomatic: The Family Rituals changed this to: "After the second year of mourning, stop weeping at morning and evening; only on the first and fifteenth do those not yet out of mourning gather to weep; whenever grief comes, all must restrain themselves and not weep."

sentences.zh: 元亦遵之。

translations.literal: Yuan also followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan followed that as well.

sentences.zh: 既覺其過抑情，校以古喪禮非是。

translations.literal: Then he felt it excessively suppressed emotion; comparing it with the ancient mourning rites, he found it incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Then he realized it suppressed feeling too harshly; compared with the ancient mourning rites, it was wrong.

sentences.zh: 因嘆先王制禮，盡人之性，後儒無德無位，不可作也。

translations.literal: He therefore sighed that when the former kings made ritual, they fully expressed human nature; later Confucians without virtue and without position should not compose ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed that the former kings had fashioned ritual to give full expression to human nature, and that later Confucians without virtue or standing had no business rewriting it.

sentences.zh: 於是著存學、存性、存治、存人四編以立教。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote the four compilations Preserving Learning, Preserving Nature, Preserving Governance, and Preserving Humanity to establish his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote Preserving Learning, Preserving Nature, Preserving Governance, and Preserving Humanity—the four compilations that founded his teaching.

sentences.zh: 名其居曰習齋。

translations.literal: He named his dwelling the Practice Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He named his dwelling the Practice Studio.

sentences.zh: 肥鄉漳南書院，邑人郝文燦請元往教。

translations.literal: At the Zhangnan Academy in Feixiang, the local man Hao Wencan invited Yuan to go and teach.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhangnan Academy in Feixiang, Hao Wencan invited Yuan to teach there.

sentences.zh: 有文事、武備、經史、藝能等科，從遊者數十人。

translations.literal: There were departments for literary affairs, military preparedness, classics and history, and technical skills; several dozen followed him to study.
translations.idiomatic: The academy had departments for literary studies, military preparedness, classics and history, and technical skills; several dozen students followed him.

sentences.zh: 會天大雨，漳水溢，牆垣堂舍悉沒，人跡殆絕。

translations.literal: A great rain came, the Zhang River overflowed, walls and halls were all submerged, and human traces nearly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Then came torrential rains; the Zhang River burst its banks, walls and halls were submerged, and scarcely a soul remained.

sentences.zh: 元歎曰：「天不欲行吾道也！」

translations.literal: Yuan sighed: "Heaven does not wish my Way to be practiced!
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sighed: "Heaven does not wish my Way to be practiced!

sentences.zh: 乃辭歸。

translations.literal: He then resigned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 後八年而卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Eight years later he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died eight years later, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 門人李塨、王源編元年譜二卷，鍾錂輯言行錄二卷，辟異錄二卷。

translations.literal: His disciples Li Gong and Wang Yuan compiled his Chronological Biography in two juan; Zhong Ling compiled Recorded Words and Conduct in two juan and Refutation of Heterodoxies in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Li Gong and Wang Yuan compiled his Chronological Biography in two juan; Zhong Ling compiled Recorded Words and Conduct in two juan and Refutation of Heterodoxies in two juan.

sentences.zh: 王源，字昆繩，大興人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuan, courtesy name Kun Sheng, was a native of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan, styled Kun Sheng, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 兄潔，少從梁以樟遊。

translations.literal: His elder brother Jie in youth followed Liang Yizhang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Jie in youth traveled with Liang Yizhang.

sentences.zh: 以樟談宋儒學，源方髫齔，聞之不首肯，唯喜習知前代典要及關塞險隘攻守方略。

translations.literal: When Yizhang discussed Song Confucian learning, Yuan was still a child and did not nod assent; he only delighted in mastering the essential institutions of former ages and the strategic geography of passes and defenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhang talked Song Neo-Confucianism, Yuan was still a boy and would not assent; he cared only to master the institutions of earlier ages and the strategic geography of frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 年四十，遊京師。

translations.literal: At forty he traveled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 或病其不為時文，源笑曰：「是尚需學而能乎？」

translations.literal: Some faulted him for not writing examination essays; Yuan laughed and said: "Does that still need to be learned before one can do it?
translations.idiomatic: When someone mocked him for not writing examination essays, Yuan laughed: "Does one really need to study before one can do that?

sentences.zh: 因就試，中康熙三十二年舉人。

translations.literal: He therefore took the examination and passed as a provincial graduate in Kangxi 32.
translations.idiomatic: He took the examination anyway and became a provincial graduate in Kangxi 32.

sentences.zh: 或勸更應禮部試，謝曰：「吾寄焉為謀生計，使無詬厲已耳！」

translations.literal: Some urged him to take the Ministry examination; he declined, saying: "I rely on it only to make a living, so as to avoid reproach—that is all!
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to sit for the metropolitan examination, he declined: "I only use it to earn a living and avoid reproach—that is all!

sentences.zh: 崑山徐乾學開書局於洞庭山，招致天下名士，源與焉。

translations.literal: Xu Qianxue of Kunshan opened a book bureau on Mount Dongting and gathered famous men from all under Heaven; Yuan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue of Kunshan opened a book bureau on Mount Dongting and gathered eminent scholars from across the realm; Yuan was among them.

sentences.zh: 於儕輩中獨與劉獻廷善，日討論天地陰陽之變，伯王大略，兵法、文章、典制，古今興亡之故，方域要害，近代人才邪正，其意見皆相同。

translations.literal: Among his peers he alone befriended Liu Xianting; daily they discussed the transformations of Heaven and earth, yin and yang, the grand strategy of hegemony and kingship, military methods, literature, institutions, the causes of rise and fall through antiquity and the present, strategic points of territories, and the right and wrong of recent men—their views were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Among his peers he alone befriended Liu Xianting; day after day they debated the transformations of Heaven and earth, the grand strategy of hegemony and kingship, military science, literature, institutions, the rise and fall of dynasties, strategic geography, and the merits of recent men—and found themselves always in agreement.

sentences.zh: 獻廷歿，言之輒流涕。

translations.literal: When Xianting died, speaking of him he would always weep.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianting died, mention of him always brought Yuan to tears.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遇李塨，大悅之，曰：「自獻廷歿，豈意復見君乎！」

translations.literal: Before long he met Li Gong and was greatly delighted, saying: "Since Xianting died, I never expected to see you again!
translations.idiomatic: Soon he met Li Gong and was overjoyed: "Since Xianting died, I never thought to meet anyone like you again!

sentences.zh: 塨微言聖學，源聞之沛然。

translations.literal: Gong spoke subtly of sagely learning, and Yuan heard it with full acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Gong spoke subtly of sagely learning, and Yuan drank it in eagerly.

sentences.zh: 因持大學辨業去，是之。

translations.literal: He therefore took the Distinguishing Practice of the Great Learning and went away approving it.
translations.idiomatic: He took away Li Gong's Distinguishing Practice of the Great Learning and approved it wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 塨乃為極言顏元明親之道，源曰：「吾知所歸矣。」

translations.literal: Gong then spoke at length of Yan Yuan's Way of clarifying the near, and Yuan said: "I know where I should go.
translations.idiomatic: Gong then expounded Yan Yuan's Way of clarifying what is near, and Yuan said: "Now I know where I belong.

sentences.zh: 遂介塨往博野執贄元門，時年五十有六矣。

translations.literal: He therefore had Gong introduce him to Boye to present gifts at Yuan's gate; he was then fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Gong introduced him to Boye, where at fifty-six he presented himself as Yan Yuan's disciple.

sentences.zh: 後客死淮上。

translations.literal: Later he died as a guest on the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as a guest on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 所著平書十卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: His writings include the Book of Balance in ten juan and Collected Works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Book of Balance in ten juan and Collected Works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 程廷祚，字啟生，上元人。

translations.literal: Cheng Tingzuo, courtesy name Qisheng, was a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Tingzuo, styled Qisheng, came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 初識武進惲鶴生，始聞顏、李之學。

translations.literal: At first he knew Yun Hesheng of Wujin and first heard of the learning of Yan and Li.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yun Hesheng of Wujin he first encountered the Yan-Li school.

sentences.zh: 康熙庚子歲，塨南游金陵，廷祚屢過問學。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year of Kangxi, when Gong traveled south to Jinling, Tingzuo repeatedly visited to inquire about learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year of the Kangxi reign, when Li Gong traveled south to Jinling, Tingzuo repeatedly visited him to study.

sentences.zh: 讀顏氏存學編，題其後云：「古之害道，出於儒之外；

translations.literal: Reading Yan's Preserving Learning, he wrote at the end: "In antiquity what harmed the Way came from outside Confucianism;
translations.idiomatic: Reading Yan's Preserving Learning, he wrote at the end: "In antiquity what harmed the Way came from outside Confucianism;

sentences.zh: 今之害道，出於儒之中。

translations.literal: what harms the Way today comes from within Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: what harms the Way today comes from within Confucianism.

sentences.zh: 顏氏起於燕、趙，當四海倡和翕然同氣之日，乃能折衷至當，而有以斥其非，蓋五百年間一人而已。」

translations.literal: Yan arose in Yan and Zhao; when all under Heaven echoed in harmonious agreement, he alone could weigh things to the proper mean and have the means to reject what was wrong—perhaps one man in five hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Yan arose in Yan and Zhao at a time when the whole empire sang in chorus; he alone could strike the true mean and reject what was false—a man perhaps once in five hundred years.

sentences.zh: 故嘗謂：「為顏氏其勢難於孟子，其功倍於孟子。」

translations.literal: He therefore once said: "To be Yan is harder than being Mencius, and the achievement is twice Mencius's.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore said: "To be Yan is harder than being Mencius, and the achievement is twice as great.

sentences.zh: 於是力屏異說，以顏氏為主，而參以顧炎武、黃宗羲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he forcefully barred heterodox doctrines, took Yan as master, and combined this with Gu Yanwu and Huang Zongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he forcefully barred heterodox doctrines, took Yan as his master, and blended that teaching with Gu Yanwu and Huang Zongxi.

sentences.zh: 故其讀書極博，而皆歸於實用，

translations.literal: Therefore though his reading was extremely broad, it all returned to practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Though his reading was prodigious, everything returned to practical use.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉博學鴻詞，至京師，有要人慕其名，囑密友達其意，曰：「主我，翰林可得也。」

translations.literal: In Qianlong year one, recommended for Broad Learning and Eloquence, he reached the capital; a powerful man admired his name and sent a friend with an offer: "Take me as patron and a Hanlin post is yours."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year one, recommended for Broad Learning and Eloquence, he reached the capital; a powerful man admired his name and sent a friend with an offer: "Take me as patron and a Hanlin post is yours."

sentences.zh: 廷祚拒之，卒報罷。

translations.literal: Tingzuo refused him and in the end failed the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo refused and ultimately failed the examination.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上特詔舉經明行修之士，廷祚又以江蘇巡撫薦，复罷歸。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor specially ordered the recommendation of scholars clear in the classics and upright in conduct; Tingzuo was again recommended by the Jiangsu governor and again dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor specially ordered recommendations of scholars clear in the classics and upright in conduct; Tingzuo was again recommended by the Jiangsu governor and again sent home without appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有七。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 著易通六卷，大易擇言三十卷，尚書通議三十卷，青溪詩說三十卷，春秋識小錄三卷，禮說二卷，魯說二卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Comprehensive Meaning of the Changes in six juan, Selected Words on the Great Changes in thirty juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Documents in thirty juan, Poetry Commentary of the Clear Stream in thirty juan, Small Records of Recognizing the Spring and Autumn in three juan, Discourse on Ritual in two juan, and Lu Discourse in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Comprehensive Meaning of the Changes in six juan, Selected Words on the Great Changes in thirty juan, Comprehensive Discussion of the Documents in thirty juan, Poetry Commentary of the Clear Stream in thirty juan, Small Records of Recognizing the Spring and Autumn in three juan, Discourse on Ritual in two juan, and Lu Discourse in two juan.

sentences.zh: 惲鶴生，字皋聞，武進人。

translations.literal: Yun Hesheng, courtesy name Gaowen, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Hesheng, styled Gaowen, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 因交李塨得睹顏氏遺書，自稱私淑弟子。

translations.literal: Through acquaintance with Li Gong he was able to see Yan's surviving books and styled himself a private disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Through Li Gong he gained access to Yan's surviving books and styled himself a private disciple.

sentences.zh: 於經長毛詩，著詩說，以毛、鄭為宗。

translations.literal: In the classics he excelled in the Mao Classic of Poetry; he wrote a Poetry Commentary taking Mao and Zheng as authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the classics he excelled in the Mao Classic of Poetry; he wrote a Poetry Commentary grounded in the Mao and Zheng traditions.

sentences.zh: 李塨，字剛主，蠡縣人。

translations.literal: Li Gong, courtesy name Gangzhu, was a native of Li County.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong, styled Gangzhu, came from Li County in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 弱冠與王源同師顏元。

translations.literal: In his early twenties he studied under Yan Yuan together with Wang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he and Wang Yuan both studied under Yan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 躬耕善稼穡，雖儉歲必有收，而食必粢糲，妻妾子婦執苦身之役。

translations.literal: He personally farmed and was skilled at agriculture; though in lean years he always had a harvest, his food was always coarse grain, and wives, concubines, sons, and daughters-in-law performed laborious bodily tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He farmed with his own hands and was skilled at agriculture; even in lean years he always had a harvest, yet he ate only coarse grain while wives, concubines, sons, and daughters-in-law performed the hardest household labor.

sentences.zh: 舉康熙二十九年舉人。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in Kangxi year twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Kangxi year twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 晚歲授通州學正，浹月，以母老告歸。

translations.literal: In his later years he was appointed director of studies at Tongzhou; within a month he requested leave to return because his mother was old.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was appointed director of studies at Tongzhou, but within a month he asked to go home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 塨博學工文辭，與慈溪姜宸英齊名。

translations.literal: Gong was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition, equal in fame to Jiang Chenying of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was broadly learned and a master of prose, ranked alongside Jiang Chenying of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 又嘗為其友治劇邑，逾年，政教大行，用此名動公卿間。

translations.literal: He also once governed a difficult county for a friend; within a year government and teaching flourished greatly, and by this his name moved among grandees and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He once governed a difficult county on a friend's behalf; within a year both administration and moral instruction flourished, and his name resounded among the high officials.

sentences.zh: 明珠、索額圖當國，皆嘗延教其子，不就。

translations.literal: When Mingzhu and Songgotu held power, both once invited him to teach their sons, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzhu and Songgotu held power, each invited him to tutor his sons, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 安溪李光地撫直隸，薦其學行於朝，固辭而不謝。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi of Anxi, as governor of Zhili, recommended his learning and conduct to the court; he firmly declined and did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi of Anxi, governing Zhili, recommended his learning and conduct to the court; Gong firmly declined and offered no thanks.

sentences.zh: 諸王交聘，輒避而之他。

translations.literal: When various princes sent successive invitations, he always avoided them by going elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When various princes sent invitations, he always slipped away elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 既而從毛奇齡學。

translations.literal: Later he studied under Mao Qiling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Mao Qiling.

sentences.zh: 著周易傳註七卷，筮考一卷，郊社考辨一卷，論語傳註二卷，大學傳註一卷，中庸傳註一卷，傳注問一卷，李氏學樂錄二卷，大學辨業四卷，聖經學規二卷，論學二卷，小學稽業五卷，恕谷後集十三卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Commentary and Annotation on the Changes in seven juan, Examination of Divination in one juan, Discrimination of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices in one juan, Commentary and Annotation on the Analects in two juan, Commentary and Annotation on the Great Learning in one juan, Commentary and Annotation on the Mean in one juan, Questions on Commentary and Annotation in one juan, Li's Record of Learning Music in two juan, Distinguishing Practice of the Great Learning in four juan, Rules of Sacred Classic Learning in two juan, Discourse on Learning in two juan, Investigation of Elementary Learning in five juan, and Later Collection of Shugu in thirteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Commentary and Annotation on the Changes in seven juan, Examination of Divination in one juan, Discrimination of Suburban and Altar Sacrifices in one juan, commentaries on the Analects, Great Learning, and Mean, Questions on Commentary and Annotation, Li's Record of Learning Music, Distinguishing Practice of the Great Learning, Rules of Sacred Classic Learning, Discourse on Learning, Investigation of Elementary Learning, and Later Collection of Shugu in thirteen juan.

sentences.zh: 塨學務以實用為主，解釋經義多與宋儒不合。

translations.literal: Gong's learning always took practical use as its master; his explanations of classical meaning often did not accord with Song Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's teaching always put practical use first; his readings of the classics often diverged from Song Confucian orthodoxy.

sentences.zh: 又其自命太高，於程、朱之講學，陸、王之證悟，皆謂之空談。

translations.literal: Also his self-regard was too high; he called the lecturing of Cheng and Zhu and the enlightenment of Lu and Wang all empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: He also set himself too high, dismissing the lecturing of Cheng and Zhu and the enlightenment teachings of Lu and Wang as empty talk.

sentences.zh: 蓋明季心學盛行，儒禪淆雜，其曲謹者又闊於事情，沿及順、康朝，猶存餘說，蓋顏元及塨力以務實相爭。

translations.literal: For in the late Ming mind-learning flourished, Confucianism and Chan were mixed, while those who were narrowly scrupulous were also ignorant of affairs; this extended into the Shunzhi and Kangxi reigns with surviving doctrines—Yan Yuan and Gong forcefully contended for practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, mind-learning had flourished and Confucianism mingled with Chan; the narrowly scrupulous were ignorant of practical affairs, and even into the Shunzhi and Kangxi reigns those doctrines lingered—Yan Yuan and Gong forcefully championed practical learning against them.

sentences.zh: 存其說可補諸儒枵腹之弊，然不可獨以立訓，盡廢諸家。

translations.literal: Preserving their doctrine can remedy the hollow-bellied defect of the Confucians, yet one cannot establish instruction solely on it and completely discard all other schools.
translations.idiomatic: Their doctrine can remedy the hollow pedantry of other Confucians, yet it cannot stand alone as the sole teaching nor justify discarding every other school.

sentences.zh: 其論易，以觀像為主，兼用互體，謂「聖教罕言性天，乾坤四德，必歸人事，屯蒙以下，亦皆以人事立言。

translations.literal: In his discussion of the Changes he took observing images as primary and also used mutual hexagrams, saying: "Sagely teaching rarely speaks of nature and Heaven; the four virtues of Qian and Kun must return to human affairs; from Zhun and Meng downward, all likewise speak from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the Changes he took image-reading as primary and also used mutual hexagrams, arguing: "Sagely teaching rarely speaks of nature and Heaven; the four virtues of Qian and Kun must return to human affairs, and from Zhun and Meng onward every hexagram speaks through human affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳摶龍圖，劉牧鉤隱，以及探無極、推先天，皆使易道入於無用」。

translations.literal: Chen Tuan's Dragon Diagram, Liu Mu's Hooked Hiddenness, and also probing the Supreme Ultimate and pushing the Prior Heaven—all make the Way of the Changes enter uselessness."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tuan's Dragon Diagram, Liu Mu's Hooked Hiddenness, probing the Supreme Ultimate, and pushing the Prior Heaven—all of these drive the Way of the Changes into uselessness."

sentences.zh: 排擊未免過激。

translations.literal: The attack was unavoidably somewhat excessive.
translations.idiomatic: His polemics were at times excessively harsh.

sentences.zh: 然明人以心學竄入易學，率持禪偈以詁經，言數者反置象佔於不問。

translations.literal: Yet Ming people smuggled mind-learning into the study of the Changes, generally holding Chan verses to gloss the classics, while those who spoke of numbers in turn left image-divination unasked.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ming scholars had smuggled mind-learning into the Changes, usually glossing the classics with Chan-style verses while number mystics ignored hexagram divination entirely.

sentences.zh: 誣飾聖訓，弊不可窮。

translations.literal: Falsifying and adorning the sage's teaching—the evil cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They falsified and adorned the sage's teaching, and the harm was endless.

sentences.zh: 塨引而歸之人事，深得垂教之旨。

translations.literal: Gong led it back to human affairs and deeply obtained the aim of handing down teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Gong brought the Changes back to human affairs and thus recovered the sage's true aim.

sentences.zh: 又以大學格物為周禮三物，謂孔子時古大學教法所謂六德、六行、六藝者，規矩尚存。

translations.literal: He also took the Great Learning's investigation of things as the three categories of the Rites of Zhou, saying that in Confucius's time the ancient Great Learning teaching of the so-called Six Virtues, Six Conducts, and Six Arts still had its rules intact.
translations.idiomatic: He also identified the Great Learning's investigation of things with the three categories of the Rites of Zhou, arguing that in Confucius's day the ancient Great Learning curriculum—the Six Virtues, Six Conducts, and Six Arts—still survived intact.

sentences.zh: 故格物之學，人人所習，不必再言。

translations.literal: Therefore the learning of investigating things was what everyone practiced and need not be spoken of again.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating things was something everyone already practiced and need not be reiterated.

sentences.zh: 惟以明德、親民標其目，以誠意指其入手而已。

translations.literal: Only with clarifying virtue and loving the people as its headings and making sincere intent the point of entry.
translations.idiomatic: One need only take clarifying virtue and loving the people as headings and sincere intent as the point of entry.

sentences.zh: 格物一傳，可不必補。

translations.literal: The single chapter on investigating things need not be supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: The lost chapter on investigating things need not be restored.

sentences.zh: 其說本之顏元。

translations.literal: His doctrine was based on Yan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The doctrine came from Yan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 毛奇齡惡其異己，作逸講箋以攻之。

translations.literal: Mao Qiling hated that he differed from himself and wrote the Supplementary Notes of the Lost Lecture to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qiling resented his dissent and wrote the Supplementary Notes of the Lost Lecture to attack him.

sentences.zh: 而當時學者多韙塨說焉。

translations.literal: Yet many scholars of the time approved Gong's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many scholars of the time sided with Gong.

sentences.zh: 刁包，字蒙吉，晚號用六居士，祁州人。

translations.literal: Diao Bao, courtesy name Mengji, in his later years styled himself the Recluse of Using Six, a native of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Bao, styled Mengji, in later life called himself the Recluse of Using Six and came from Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 明天啟舉人。

translations.literal: A Ming Tianqi-era provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the provincial examination in the Tianqi reign of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 再上春官，不第。

translations.literal: Going again to the spring office, he did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: He tried again for the metropolitan examination but failed.

sentences.zh: 遂棄舉子業，有志聖賢之學。

translations.literal: He therefore abandoned the pursuit of examination essays and aspired to the learning of sages and worthies.
