translations.idiomatic: He abandoned examination essays and devoted himself to the learning of sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 初聞孫奇逢講良知，心鄉之。

translations.literal: At first hearing Sun Qifeng lecture on innate knowledge, his heart went toward it.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was drawn to Sun Qifeng's lectures on innate knowledge.

sentences.zh: 既讀高攀龍書，大喜，曰：「不讀此書，幾虛過一生。」

translations.literal: After reading Gao Panlong's books, he rejoiced greatly and said: "Without reading this book, I nearly wasted my life.
translations.idiomatic: After reading Gao Panlong's works he was overjoyed and said: "Without this book I would have wasted my life.

sentences.zh: 為主奉之，或有過差，即跪主前自訟。

translations.literal: He took him as master and served him; if there was any fault, he immediately knelt before the master and confessed it to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He took Gao as his master; whenever he fell short he knelt before Gao's tablet and confessed the fault aloud.

sentences.zh: 流賊犯祁州，包毀家倡眾誓固守，城得不破。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded Qizhou, Bao destroyed his property to rally the people in sworn defense, and the city was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked Qizhou, Bao ruined his estate to rally a sworn defense, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 時有二璫主兵事，探卒報賊勢張甚，二璫怒其惑眾，將斬之。

translations.literal: At the time two eunuchs controlled military affairs; a scout reported the bandits' strength as very great, and the two eunuchs angrily accused him of misleading the people and were about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Two eunuchs then controlled military affairs; when a scout reported the bandits were very strong, they accused him of spreading panic and were about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 包厲聲曰：「必殺彼，請先殺包。」

translations.literal: Bao said in a stern voice: "If you must kill him, please kill Bao first.
translations.idiomatic: Bao shouted: "If you must kill him, kill me first.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They relented.

sentences.zh: 二璫相謂曰：「使若居官者，其不為楊、左乎？」

translations.literal: The two eunuchs said to each other: "If such a one held office, would he not be another Yang or Zuo?
translations.idiomatic: The two eunuchs said to each other: "If this man held office, would he not be another Yang Lian or Zuo Guangdou?

sentences.zh: 賊既去，流民載道，設屋聚養之，病者給醫藥，全活尤多。

translations.literal: After the bandits left, refugees filled the roads; he set up houses to gather and nurture them, gave medicine to the sick, and especially many were fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: After the bandits withdrew, refugees filled the roads; he set up shelters, fed the hungry, medicated the sick, and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 有山左難婦七十餘人，擇老成家人護以歸。

translations.literal: There were more than seventy distressed women from Shandong; he chose reliable household members to escort them home.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy distressed women from Shandong needed escort home; he chose reliable household members to guard them.

sentences.zh: 臨行，八拜以重託，家人皆感泣，竭力衛送。

translations.literal: At parting he bowed eight times to entrust them heavily; the household members all wept with emotion and exerted themselves to guard and send them.
translations.idiomatic: At parting he bowed eight times to entrust them; the escorts wept and guarded them all the way.

sentences.zh: 歷六府，盡歸其家。

translations.literal: Passing through six prefectures, all were returned to their homes.
translations.idiomatic: They passed through six prefectures and every woman reached her home.

sentences.zh: 甲申，國變，設莊烈愍皇帝主於所居之順積樓，服斬衰，朝夕哭臨如禮。

translations.literal: In jiashen the dynasty changed; he set up a tablet to the martyred Emperor Zhuanglie at his dwelling, the Shunji Tower, wore the coarsest mourning, and morning and evening wept according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In jiashen, when the dynasty fell, he enshrined the martyred Emperor Chongzhen at his Shunji Tower, wore the coarsest mourning, and wept morning and evening according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 偽命敦趣，包以死拒，幾及於難。

translations.literal: A false command urgently summoned him; Bao refused with death and nearly met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When a false summons came he refused at the risk of death and nearly came to harm.

sentences.zh: 遂隱居不出，於城隅辟地為齋曰潛室，亭曰肥遯。

translations.literal: He therefore lived in seclusion without emerging; at the corner of the city he opened land for a studio called the Hidden Room and a pavilion called Fat Retire.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from public life, cleared land at the city edge for a studio called the Hidden Room and a pavilion called Fat Retire.

sentences.zh: 日閉戶讀書其中，無間寒暑，學者宗焉，執經之履滿戶外。

translations.literal: Daily he shut his door and read books therein without interruption through cold or heat; scholars took him as patriarch, and the footsteps of those carrying the classics filled the space outside his door.
translations.idiomatic: He read behind closed doors year round regardless of season; scholars flocked to him until the path outside his door was worn smooth by students.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀，鬚髮盡白。

translations.literal: During mourning for his father he was destroyed by grief and his beard and hair all turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his father, he was wrecked by grief until his beard and hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 三年不飲酒食肉，不內寢。

translations.literal: For three years he did not drink wine or eat meat and did not sleep indoors.
translations.idiomatic: For three years he drank no wine, ate no meat, and slept outdoors.

sentences.zh: 及母卒，號慟嘔血，病數月，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wailed and vomited blood, was ill for several months, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he wailed until he vomited blood, fell ill for months, and died.

sentences.zh: 所著有易酌、四書翊注、潛室劄記、用六集，皆本義理，明白正大。

translations.literal: His writings include Deliberations on the Changes, Assisting Annotation on the Four Books, Notes of the Hidden Room, and the Using Six Collection—all based on principle and meaning, clear and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Deliberations on the Changes, Assisting Annotation on the Four Books, Notes of the Hidden Room, and the Using Six Collection—all principled, clear, and upright.

sentences.zh: 又選斯文正統九十六卷，專以品行為主，若言是人非，雖絕技無取。

translations.literal: He also selected Orthodox Literary Tradition in ninety-six juan, taking conduct as the sole criterion; if the words were right but the person wrong, even supreme skill was not taken.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Orthodox Literary Tradition in ninety-six juan, judging authors by conduct alone—if the man was unworthy, no brilliance of style could save him.

sentences.zh: 包初與新城王餘佑為石交。

translations.literal: At first Bao and Wang Yuyou of Xincheng were sworn friends like stone.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and Wang Yuyou of Xincheng were once friends close as bonded stone.

sentences.zh: 餘佑，字介祺。

translations.literal: Yuyou, courtesy name Jieqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuyou, styled Jieqi.

sentences.zh: 父延善，邑諸生，尚氣誼。

translations.literal: His father Yanshan was a county student and valued honor and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanshan was a county licentiate who prized honor and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 當明末，散萬金產結客。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he spent ten thousand in gold of his estate to gather clients.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming he spent a fortune entertaining clients.

sentences.zh: 有子三，長餘恪，季餘嚴，餘佑其仲也。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Yuke, the youngest Yuyan, and Yuyou was the middle one.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest Yuke, the youngest Yuyan, and Yuyou in the middle.

sentences.zh: 明亡，延善率三子與雄縣馬魯建義旗，傳檄討賊。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, Yanshan led the three sons and Ma Lu of Xiong County to raise a banner of righteousness and issue a proclamation against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, Yanshan led his three sons and Ma Lu of Xiong County to raise a righteous banner and issue a proclamation against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 時容城孫奇逢亦起兵，共恢復雄、新、容三縣，斬其偽官。

translations.literal: At the time Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng also raised troops; together they recovered the three counties of Xiong, Xin, and Rong and beheaded their false officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qifeng of Rongcheng also raised troops; together they recovered Xiong, Xin, and Rong and executed the puppet officials.

sentences.zh: 順治初，延善為仇家所陷，執赴京。

translations.literal: In the early Shunzhi period, Yanshan was framed by an enemy family and seized and taken to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, an enemy family framed Yanshan and he was seized and taken to the capital.

sentences.zh: 餘恪揮兩弟出，為復仇計，獨身赴難，父子死燕巿。

translations.literal: Yuke sent out his two younger brothers to plan revenge and alone went to meet disaster; father and son died in the Yan market.
translations.idiomatic: Yuke sent his two younger brothers away to plan revenge and went alone to meet disaster; father and son died in the Beijing market.

sentences.zh: 餘嚴夜率壯士入仇家，殲其老弱三十口。

translations.literal: Yuyan by night led stalwart men into the enemy family and destroyed its old and weak—thirty mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyan by night led strong men into the enemy household and killed thirty of its members, old and young.

sentences.zh: 名捕甚急，上官有知其枉者，力解乃免。

translations.literal: Wanted posters were very urgent; a superior who knew he had been wronged forcefully intervened and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The manhunt was fierce, but a superior who knew he had been wronged intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 餘佑隱易州之五公山，自號五公山人。

translations.literal: Yuyou hid on Mount Wugong in Yizhou and styled himself the Mountain Man of the Five Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Yuyou hid on Mount Wugong in Yizhou and styled himself the Mountain Man of the Five Lords.

sentences.zh: 嘗受業於孫奇逢，學兵法，後更從奇逢講性命之學。

translations.literal: He once received instruction from Sun Qifeng, studied military methods, and later again followed Qifeng in lecturing on the learning of nature and destiny.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Sun Qifeng, learned military science, and later returned to Qifeng for the learning of nature and destiny.

sentences.zh: 隱居教授，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Living in seclusion he taught, not seeking fame and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in retirement and sought neither fame nor office.

sentences.zh: 教人以忠孝，務實學。

translations.literal: He taught people loyalty and filial piety and practical learning.
translations.idiomatic: He taught loyalty, filial piety, and practical learning.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 李來章，字禮山，襄城人。

translations.literal: Li Laizhang, courtesy name Lishan, was a native of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Laizhang, styled Lishan, came from Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 生有神識。

translations.literal: From birth he had divine discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed unusual insight.

sentences.zh: 嘗觀石工集庭中斷石，輾轉弗合，語之曰：「去宿土，當自合。

translations.literal: Once watching stonemasons gather broken stones in the courtyard that would not fit together however turned, he said to them: "Remove the old soil and they will join of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once he watched stonemasons trying to fit broken stones in a courtyard; however they turned, the pieces would not join. He told them: "Remove the old soil and they will fit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 是即吾學人心、道心之謂。」

translations.literal: That is what I mean by the human mind and the moral mind in my learning.
translations.idiomatic: That is what I mean by the human mind and the moral mind.

sentences.zh: 聞者異之。

translations.literal: Hearing this, people were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners were astonished.

sentences.zh: 工詩古文辭。

translations.literal: He was skilled in poetry and ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in poetry and ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年舉人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, Provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi, he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 嘗學於魏象樞，魏戒之曰：「欲除妄念，莫如立志。」

translations.literal: He once studied under Wei Xiangshu; Wei admonished him: "To remove wandering thoughts, nothing is better than setting the will.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wei Xiangshu, who admonished him: "To banish wandering thoughts, nothing works like setting the will.

sentences.zh: 來章因作書紳語略，其持論以不背先儒有益世用為主。

translations.literal: Laizhang therefore wrote Brief Words Written on the Girdle; his position took not betraying earlier Confucians and benefiting worldly use as its master.
translations.idiomatic: Laizhang wrote Brief Words Written on the Girdle, holding that learning must not betray the earlier Confucians and must benefit practical life.

sentences.zh: 再學於孫奇逢、李顒。

translations.literal: He studied again under Sun Qifeng and Li Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He studied further under Sun Qifeng and Li Yong.

sentences.zh: 時奇逢講學百泉，來章與冉覲祖諸人講學嵩陽，兩河相望，一時稱極盛焉。

translations.literal: At the time Qifeng lectured at Baiquan and Laizhang with Ran Jinzu and others lectured at Songyang; the two rivers faced each other and for a time were called at their greatest flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qifeng taught at Baiquan while Laizhang, Ran Jinzu, and others taught at Songyang; the two river valleys faced each other and the age was called one of supreme flourishing.

sentences.zh: 再主南陽書院，作南陽學規、達天錄以教學者，士習日上。

translations.literal: Again he headed the Nanyang Academy, wrote the Nanyang Rules of Learning and Records of Reaching Heaven to instruct scholars, and local custom daily improved.
translations.idiomatic: He again headed the Nanyang Academy, wrote the Nanyang Rules of Learning and Records of Reaching Heaven, and local custom steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老謝歸。

translations.literal: Soon because his mother was old he thanked them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 重葺紫雲書院，讀書其中，學者多自遠而至。

translations.literal: He rebuilt the Ziyun Academy, read books therein, and many scholars came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the Ziyun Academy, read there, and scholars came from far away.

sentences.zh: 母病目，來章每夙興舌舐之，目復明。

translations.literal: When his mother's eyes were ill, Laizhang every morning licked them with his tongue and her eyes recovered sight.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's eyes failed, Laizhang licked them with his tongue each morning until her sight returned.

sentences.zh: 謁選廣東連山縣。

translations.literal: Awaiting appointment he was sent to Lianshan County in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Awaiting appointment, he was assigned to Lianshan County in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 連山民僅七村，丁只二千。

translations.literal: Lianshan had only seven villages of Han people and two thousand male taxpayers.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshan had only seven Han villages and two thousand registered males.

sentences.zh: 外瑤戶大排居五，小排一十有七，數且盈萬人。

translations.literal: Outside were Yao households: five large settlements and seventeen small ones, numbering nearly ten thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them lived Yao communities—five large settlements and seventeen small ones, nearly ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 重山複嶺，瘦石巉削，田居十分之一。

translations.literal: Layer upon layer of heavy mountains, lean stone steep and cut; fields occupied one tenth.
translations.idiomatic: Steep mountains rose in layers, the rock bare and cruel; arable land was one tenth of the land.

sentences.zh: 瑤或負險跳梁。

translations.literal: The Yao sometimes relied on perilous terrain to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao sometimes exploited the terrain to rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 來章慨然曰：「瑤異類，亦有人性，當推誠以待之。」

translations.literal: Laizhang sighed and said: "The Yao are a different kind, yet they also have human nature; one should treat them with sincere good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Laizhang said with feeling: "The Yao are another people, yet they too have human nature; we must treat them with sincere good faith.

sentences.zh: 乃仿明王守仁遺意，日延耆老問民疾苦，招流亡，勸之開墾，薄其賦。

translations.literal: He therefore modeled himself on the surviving intent of Wang Shouren of the Ming, daily inviting elders to ask about the people's hardships, recruiting the displaced, urging them to open wasteland, and lightening their taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Shouren's example, he daily summoned elders to hear the people's hardships, recalled refugees, urged reclamation, and lightened taxes.

sentences.zh: 复深入瑤穴，為之置約延師，以至誠相感。

translations.literal: He also went deep into Yao caves, set up compacts for them and extended teachers, moving them with utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He went deep into Yao villages, established compacts, sent teachers, and moved them with utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 創連山書院，著學規，日進縣人申教之。

translations.literal: He founded the Lianshan Academy, wrote rules of learning, and daily had county people come to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Lianshan Academy, wrote rules of learning, and had county people instructed daily.

sentences.zh: 而瑤民之秀者，亦知鄉學，誦讀聲徹巖谷。

translations.literal: And among the Yao, the talented also came to know the village schools, and the sound of recitation reached through the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Talented Yao youths also entered the village schools, and the sound of recitation echoed through the valleys.

sentences.zh: 學使者交獎曰：「忠信篤敬，蠻貊信可行矣。」

translations.literal: The education intendant jointly praised him: "With loyalty, faith, earnestness, and respect, even among barbarians the Way can be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: The education intendant praised him jointly: "With loyalty, faith, earnestness, and respect, even among frontier peoples the Way can be practiced.

sentences.zh: 行取，授兵部主事，監北新倉，革運官餽遺。

translations.literal: Selected for promotion, he was appointed secretary in the Ministry of War, supervised the Beixin granary, and abolished the transport officials' gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for promotion, he was appointed secretary in the Ministry of War, supervised the Beixin granary, and abolished gifts to transport officials.

sentences.zh: 旋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon he cited illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 大學士田從典、侍郎李先復交章以實學可大用薦，得旨徵召，不出。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Tian Congdian and Vice Minister Li Xianfu jointly memorialized recommending his practical learning as fit for great use; he received an order summoning him but did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Tian Congdian and Vice Minister Li Xianfu jointly recommended his practical learning for high office; an imperial summons came, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 年六十八，卒。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 所著有禮山園文集、洛學編、連陽八排瑤風土記、衾影錄。

translations.literal: His writings include Collected Works of the Lishan Garden, Records of Lu Learning, Record of the Customs of the Eight Yao Settlements of Lianyang, and Record of the Shadow of the Quilt.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collected Works of the Lishan Garden, Records of Lu Learning, Record of the Customs of the Eight Yao Settlements of Lianyang, and Record of the Shadow of the Quilt.

sentences.zh: 冉覲祖，字永光，先賢鄆國公裔。

translations.literal: Ran Jinzu, courtesy name Yongguang, was a descendant of the sage Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Ran Jinzu, styled Yongguang, was a descendant of the sage Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 元末有為中牟丞者，因家焉，

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan a forebear served as assistant magistrate of Zhongmou and settled the family there.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yuan a forebear served as assistant magistrate of Zhongmou and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, he ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 杜門潛居，爰取四書集注研精覃思二十年。

translations.literal: He shut his door and lived in seclusion, then took the Collected Commentaries on the Four Books and for twenty years refined his thought with deep absorption.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion and for twenty years immersed himself in Zhu Xi's Collected Commentaries on the Four Books.

sentences.zh: 章求其旨，句求其解，字求其訓，身體心驗，訂正群言，歸於一是，名曰玩注詳說。

translations.literal: For each chapter he sought its aim, for each sentence its explanation, for each character its gloss; he embodied it in person and tested it in mind, corrected the sayings of the schools, and returned them to unity—calling it Detailed Explanation for Reflective Reading.
translations.idiomatic: He sought the aim of every chapter, the sense of every sentence, and the gloss of every character; testing each in life and correcting rival interpretations, he unified the tradition in Detailed Explanation for Reflective Reading.

sentences.zh: 遞及群經，各有專書，兼採漢儒、宋儒之說。

translations.literal: Extending to the other classics, each had its special book, combining the doctrines of Han and Song Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to the other classics, writing a dedicated book for each and drawing on both Han and Song learning.

sentences.zh: 十八年，開博學鴻儒科，巡撫將薦之，欲一見覲祖。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Broad Learning and Eloquence examination was opened; the governor was about to recommend him and wished to see Jinzu once.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Broad Learning and Eloquence examination opened, the governor wished to recommend him and asked to meet him.

sentences.zh: 覲祖曰：「往見，是求薦也。」

translations.literal: Jinzu said: "To go and see him is to seek recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzu said: "If I go to see him, I am seeking recommendation.

sentences.zh: 堅不往。

translations.literal: He firmly did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to go.

sentences.zh: 少詹事耿介延主嵩陽書院，與諸生講孟子一章，剖析天人，分別理欲，眾皆悚聽。

translations.literal: Junior Mentor Geng Jie invited him to head the Songyang Academy; lecturing one chapter of Mencius to the students, he analyzed Heaven and man and distinguished principle from desire, and all listened in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Mentor Geng Jie invited him to head the Songyang Academy; lecturing one chapter of Mencius, he analyzed Heaven and man and distinguished principle from desire, and all listened in awe.

sentences.zh: 三十年，成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he passed the jinshi examination and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 是歲聖祖遍試翰林，禦西暖閣，詢家世籍貫獨詳，有「氣度老成」之褒。

translations.literal: That year the Sage Emperor tested the entire Hanlin in the West Warm Pavilion, inquiring about family background and native place with unusual detail, with praise for his "mature bearing."
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor tested the Hanlin in the West Warm Pavilion, questioning him with unusual detail about family and origin, and praised his mature bearing.

sentences.zh: 越日，賜宴瀛台，上獨識之，曰：「爾是河南解元耶？」

translations.literal: The next day, at a banquet at Yingtai, the emperor alone recognized him and said: "Are you the Henan provincial first-place graduate?
translations.idiomatic: The next day at a banquet on Yingtai the emperor recognized him alone and said: "Are you the Henan provincial top graduate?

sentences.zh: 蓋以示優異也。

translations.literal: This was to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: It was a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十有二。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 竇克勤，字敏修，柘城人。

translations.literal: Dou Keqin, courtesy name Minxiu, was a native of Zhecheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Keqin, styled Minxiu, came from Zhecheng.

sentences.zh: 聞耿介傳百泉之學，從遊嵩陽。

translations.literal: Hearing that Geng Jie transmitted the learning of Baiquan, he followed him to study at Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Geng Jie carried on the Baiquan teaching, he studied with him at Songyang.

sentences.zh: 六年，鄉舉至京師，謁睢州湯斌。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he passed the provincial examination and reached the capital, calling on Tang Bin of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he passed the provincial examination, went to the capital, and visited Tang Bin of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 一夕，請業，斌謂師道不立，由教官之失職。

translations.literal: One evening he asked instruction; Bin said the teacher's Way was not established because educational officials failed in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: One evening he sought instruction; Bin said the teacher's Way had collapsed because educational officials had failed their duty.

sentences.zh: 勸克勤就教職，選泌陽教諭。

translations.literal: He urged Keqin to take an educational post; Keqin was selected as instructor of Biyang.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Keqin to take a teaching post, and Keqin was appointed instructor of Biyang.

sentences.zh: 泌陽地小而僻，人鮮知學，克勤立五社學，月朔稽善過而勸懲之。

translations.literal: Biyang was small and remote, and people rarely knew learning; Keqin established five community schools, and on the first of each month checked good and bad conduct and encouraged or punished accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Biyang was small and remote and learning was rare; Keqin founded five community schools and on the first of each month reviewed conduct, rewarding the good and correcting the bad.

sentences.zh: 暇則齋居讀書，雖饘粥不繼，晏如也。

translations.literal: In leisure he lived simply and read books; though porridge sometimes failed to follow, he was perfectly content.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he lived simply and read; even when porridge ran short he was perfectly content.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年進士，選庶吉士，丁母憂歸，服除，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor; on his mother's death he returned, and after mourning was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, he passed the jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, returned on his mother's death, and after mourning was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 一日，聖祖命諸翰林作楷書，克勤書「學宗孔、孟，法在堯、舜，而其要在慎獨」十四字以進，聖祖覽而器之。

translations.literal: One day the Sage Emperor ordered the Hanlin scholars to write in regular script; Keqin wrote fourteen characters—"Learning takes Confucius and Mencius as its patriarchs, the method lies with Yao and Shun, and its core is vigilance in solitude"—and submitted them; the Sage Emperor read them and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor ordered the Hanlin to write in regular script; Keqin submitted fourteen characters—"Learning takes Confucius and Mencius as patriarchs, the method lies with Yao and Shun, and its core is vigilance in solitude"—and the emperor valued him.

sentences.zh: 尋以父老乞歸。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave to return because his father was old.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked to return home because his father was elderly.

sentences.zh: 嘗於柘城東郊立朱陽學院，倡導正學。

translations.literal: He once established the Zhuyang Academy in the eastern suburbs of Zhecheng to advocate orthodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zhuyang Academy in the eastern suburbs of Zhecheng to promote orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 中州自夏峰、嵩陽外，朱陽學者稱盛。

translations.literal: In the Central Plain, apart from Xiafeng and Songyang, Zhuyang scholars were called flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Xiafeng and Songyang, Zhuyang became the most flourishing center of learning in the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，著有孝經闡義。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-four; his writings include Exposition of the Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four, leaving Exposition of the Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 李光坡，字耜卿，安谿人，​​大學士光地之弟也。

translations.literal: Li Guangpo, courtesy name Siqing, was a native of Anxi and the younger brother of Grand Secretary Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangpo, styled Siqing, came from Anxi and was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Li Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 生五歲，與伯叔兄弟俱陷賊壘。

translations.literal: At five years of age he and his elder and younger uncles and brothers were all trapped in a bandit stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of five he and his uncles and brothers were all trapped in a bandit camp.

sentences.zh: 既脫難後，受學家庭，宗尚宋儒及鄉先正蒙引存疑諸書。

translations.literal: After escaping the calamity, he received learning at home, revering Song Confucians and such local predecessors as Mengyin and Cunyi.
translations.idiomatic: After escaping, he studied at home, revering Song Confucians and local predecessors such as Mengyin and Cunyi.

sentences.zh: 次第講治十三經，濂、洛、關、閩書，旁及子、史。

translations.literal: In sequence he lectured on the Thirteen Classics, the books of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, and also the masters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He worked through the Thirteen Classics, the Lian-Luo-Guan-Min masters, and the masters and histories.

sentences.zh: 質不甚敏，以勤苦致熟。

translations.literal: His native quality was not very quick; through labor and hardship he achieved mastery.
translations.idiomatic: He was not naturally quick, but achieved mastery through relentless labor.

sentences.zh: 論學主程、朱，論易主邵子，兼取揚雄太玄，發明性理，以闡大義。

translations.literal: In discussing learning he took Cheng and Zhu as master; in discussing the Changes he took Master Shao as master, also taking Yang Xiong's Supreme Mystery, elucidating human nature and principle to expound the great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In learning he followed Cheng and Zhu; in the Changes he followed Shao Yong, also drawing on Yang Xiong's Supreme Mystery to elucidate principle and nature.

sentences.zh: 壯歲專意三禮，以三禮之學至宋而微，至明幾絕，儀禮尤世所罕習，積四十年，成三禮述註六十九卷，以鄭康成為主，疏解簡明，不蹈支離，亦不侈奧博，自成一家言。

translations.literal: In his prime he devoted himself solely to the Three Rites; as the learning of the Three Rites had declined by the Song and nearly died by the Ming, and the Rites of Etiquette was especially rarely practiced in the world, accumulating forty years he completed Expository Commentary on the Three Rites in sixty-nine juan, taking Zheng Xuan as master—explanation concise and clear, not falling into fragmentation, nor extravagantly abstruse, forming a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: In his prime he devoted himself to the Three Rites; judging that this field had waned since the Song and nearly died in the Ming, especially the Rites of Etiquette, he spent forty years producing Expository Commentary on the Three Rites in sixty-nine juan, following Zheng Xuan—concise, clear, neither fragmented nor extravagantly abstruse.

sentences.zh: 其兄光地嘗著周官筆記一篇，光地子鍾倫亦著周禮訓纂二十一卷，皆標舉要旨，弗以考證辨論為長，與光坡相近，其家學如是也。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guangdi once wrote a note on the Offices of Zhou; Guangdi's son Zhonglun also wrote Annotated Compilation of the Rites of Zhou in twenty-one juan—all marking out essential points, not taking textual verification and debate as their strength, close to Guangpo; such was their family learning.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Guangdi wrote a note on the Offices of Zhou, and Guangdi's son Zhonglun wrote Annotated Compilation of the Rites of Zhou in twenty-one juan; both marked essentials rather than pursuing philological debate—much like Guangpo's method.

sentences.zh: 光坡家居不仁，康熙四十五年，入都，與其兄光地講貫。

translations.literal: Guangpo lived at home without taking office; in Kangxi year forty-five he entered the capital to study with his elder brother Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangpo lived at home without taking office; in Kangxi year forty-five he entered the capital to study with his elder brother Guangdi.

sentences.zh: 著性論三篇，辨論理氣先後動靜，以訂近儒之差。

translations.literal: He wrote three essays on human nature, debating the priority and sequence of principle and material force, movement and stillness, to correct the errors of recent Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote three essays on human nature, debating the order of principle and qi, movement and stillness, to correct recent Confucian errors.

sentences.zh: 及歸，光地貽以詩曰：「後生茂起須家法，我老棲遲望子傳。」

translations.literal: When he returned, Guangdi sent him a poem: "The younger generation must flourish through family method; in old age I linger, hoping my son will transmit.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Guangdi sent a poem: "The younger generation must flourish through family method; in old age I linger, hoping my son will carry it on.

sentences.zh: 其惓惓於光坡如此。

translations.literal: Such was his earnest concern for Guangpo.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his earnest hope for Guangpo.

sentences.zh: 光地嘗論東吳顧炎武與光坡皆數十年用心經學，精勤不輟，卓然可以傳於後云。

translations.literal: Guangdi once said that Gu Yanwu of Dongwu and Guangpo both applied their minds to the classics for decades without ceasing, with diligence and effort, standing out and able to transmit to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi said that Gu Yanwu of Dongwu and Guangpo had both devoted decades to the classics with unceasing diligence, producing work that would stand after them.

sentences.zh: 光坡天性至孝，父病篤，炷香焚掌叩天以祈延壽，病果愈。

translations.literal: Guangpo's nature was supremely filial; when his father was critically ill, he burned incense and seared his palm, knocking his head on Heaven to pray for extended life, and the illness indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Supremely filial by nature, when his father lay critically ill Guangpo burned incense, seared his palm, and prayed Heaven for longer life—and the illness lifted.

sentences.zh: 及舉孝廉方正，有司將以光坡應選，而光坡寢疾矣。

translations.literal: When Filial Integrity and Uprightness was recommended, the officials were about to nominate Guangpo, but Guangpo had already fallen gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: When the Filial Integrity and Uprightness recommendation came, officials meant to nominate Guangpo, but he was already gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有三。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 又有皋軒文編。

translations.literal: He also had the Collected Writings of Gaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also left the Collected Writings of Gaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 鍾倫，字世得。

translations.literal: Zhonglun, courtesy name Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhonglun, styled Shide.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年舉人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, Provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi, he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 初受三禮於光坡，又與宣城梅文鼎、長洲何焯、宿遷徐用錫、河間王之銳、同縣陳萬策等互相討論，其學具有本原。

translations.literal: At first he received the Three Rites from Guangpo, and also with Mei Wending of Xuancheng, He Chuo of Changzhou, Xu Yongxi of Suqian, Wang Zhirui of Hejian, and Chen Wance of the same county mutually discussed; his learning had a true foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He first studied the Three Rites under Guangpo, then debated with Mei Wending, He Chuo, Xu Yongxi, Wang Zhirui, and Chen Wance; his learning had solid foundations.

sentences.zh: 未仕而卒。

translations.literal: He died without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He died without ever taking office.

sentences.zh: 莊亨陽，字复齋，靖南人。

translations.literal: Zhuang Hengyang, courtesy name Fuqi, was a native of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Hengyang, styled Fuqi, came from Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年進士，知山東濰縣。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, a jinshi, he served as magistrate of Weixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, a jinshi, he served as magistrate of Weixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 母就養，卒於途。

translations.literal: When his mother came to live with him, she died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother came to live with him, she died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 歸而廬墓三年，自是未嘗一日離其父。

translations.literal: Returning, he mourned at the tomb for three years; from then on he never left his father for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and mourned at her tomb for three years; thereafter he never left his father for a day.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初元，禮部尚書楊名時薦士七人，亨陽與焉，授國子監助教。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, Minister of Rites Yang Mingshi recommended seven scholars; Hengyang was among them and was appointed assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's first year, Minister of Rites Yang Mingshi recommended seven scholars; Hengyang was among them and was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial College.

sentences.zh: 當是時，上方鄉用儒術，尚書楊名時、孫嘉淦，大學士趙國麟咸以耆壽名德領太學事，相與倡明正學。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor above was employing Confucian methods in the countryside; Ministers Yang Mingshi and Sun Jiagan and Grand Secretary Zhao Guolin, all aged and of famed virtue, headed Imperial College affairs and together advocated orthodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the throne was promoting Confucian governance; Yang Mingshi, Sun Jiagan, and Grand Secretary Zhao Guolin—all venerable men of renown—headed the Imperial College and jointly revived orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 六堂之長，則亨陽與安溪官獻瑤、無錫蔡德晉等，皆一時之俊。

translations.literal: The heads of the six halls were Hengyang, Guan Xianyao of Anxi, Cai Dejin of Wuxi, and others—all outstanding men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The heads of the six halls included Hengyang, Guan Xianyao of Anxi, and Cai Dejin of Wuxi—all outstanding men of the age.

sentences.zh: 每朔望謁夫子，釋菜禮畢，六堂師登講座，率國子生以次執經質疑。

translations.literal: Every first and fifteenth they worshipped the Master; after the vegetable-offering ritual the six hall masters ascended the lecture seat and led Imperial College students in turn to hold the classics and raise doubts.
translations.idiomatic: On the first and fifteenth of each month they worshipped the Master; after the vegetable offering the six hall masters lectured while students took turns holding the classics and raising questions.

sentences.zh: 旬日則六堂師分佔一經，各於其書齋會講南北學，弦誦之聲，夜分不絕。

translations.literal: Every ten days the six hall masters each took one classic and met in their studies to lecture on the Northern and Southern schools; the sound of recitation did not cease until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days each hall master took one classic and lectured in his study to the Northern and Southern schools; recitation continued until midnight.

sentences.zh: 都下號為「四賢、五君子」。

translations.literal: The capital called them the "Four Worthies and Five Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: The capital called them the Four Worthies and Five Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部主事，外補德安府同知，擢徐州府。

translations.literal: Transferred to secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, externally appointed vice prefect of De'an Prefecture, promoted to prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, appointed vice prefect of De'an, and promoted to prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐仍歲水災，亨陽相川澤，諮耆民，具方略，請廣開上游水道，以洩異漲，且告石林可危。

translations.literal: Xuzhou still suffered yearly floods; Hengyang surveyed rivers and marshes, consulted elders, prepared plans, and requested broadly opening upstream waterways to discharge abnormal floods, also reporting that Shilin was in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou suffered yearly floods; Hengyang surveyed rivers and marshes, consulted elders, and petitioned to open upstream channels to discharge floodwaters, warning that Shilin was in danger.

sentences.zh: 未及施工而石林決，沛縣城將潰，民竄逃。

translations.literal: Before construction could begin Shilin burst; Peixian city was about to collapse and the people fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Before work could begin Shilin burst; the walls of Peixian were about to give way and the people fled.

sentences.zh: 亨陽駕輕舠行告父老曰：「太守來，爾民何往？」

translations.literal: Hengyang rode a light boat and went to tell the elders: "The prefect has come—where are you people going?
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang took a light boat and told the elders: "Your prefect is here—where are you going?

sentences.zh: 親率眾堵築，七日夜城完。

translations.literal: He personally led the crowd in building dikes; in seven days and nights the city was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led the people in building dikes; in seven days and nights the city held.

sentences.zh: 在徐三年，兩遇大荒，勤賑事，幾不暇眠食。

translations.literal: In three years at Xuzhou he twice encountered great famine and worked tirelessly at relief, scarcely finding time to sleep or eat.
translations.idiomatic: In three years at Xuzhou he faced two great famines and worked at relief until he scarcely slept or ate.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷按察司副使，分巡淮徐海道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to vice commissioner of the surveillance commission, touring the Huai-Xu-Hai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to vice surveillance commissioner for the Huai-Xu-Hai circuit.

sentences.zh: 亨陽通算術，及董河防，推究高深測量之宜，上書當路，大略謂：「淮、徐水患，在壅毛城鋪而徐州壞，壅天然減水壩而鳳、潁、泗壞，壅車邏、昭關等壩而淮、揚之上下河皆壞。

translations.literal: Hengyang was versed in mathematics; when he supervised river defense he investigated the proper methods of elevation and measurement and wrote to those in power, in general saying: "The water calamity of Huai and Xu lies in blocking Maochengpu and ruining Xuzhou, blocking the Natural Flood-Reduction Dam and ruining Feng, Ying, and Si, blocking the Che, Luo, Zhaoguan, and other dams and ruining the upper and lower rivers of Huai and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Hengyang knew mathematics; supervising river works, he studied elevation and measurement and wrote to the authorities: "Huai-Xu flooding comes from blocking Maochengpu and ruining Xuzhou, blocking the Natural Flood-Reduction Dam and ruining Feng, Ying, and Si, and blocking the Che, Luo, and Zhaoguan dams and ruining the upper and lower Huai-Yang rivers.

sentences.zh: 宜開毛城鋪以注洪澤湖，則徐州之患息；

translations.literal: One should open Maochengpu to pour into Hongze Lake, then Xuzhou's calamity will cease;
translations.idiomatic: Open Maochengpu into Hongze Lake and Xuzhou's trouble will cease;

sentences.zh: 開天然壩以注高、寶諸湖，則上江之患息；

translations.literal: open the Natural Dam to pour into the lakes of Gao and Bao, then the upper river's calamity will cease;
translations.idiomatic: open the Natural Dam into the Gao and Bao lakes and the upper river's trouble will cease;

sentences.zh: 開三壩以注興、鹽之澤，則高、寶之患息；

translations.literal: open the three dams to pour into the marshes of Xing and Yan, then Gao and Bao's calamity will cease;
translations.idiomatic: open the three dams into the Xing and Yan marshes and the Gao-Bao trouble will cease;

sentences.zh: 開范公堤以注之海，則興、鹽、泰諸州、縣之患息。」

translations.literal: open the Dike of Fan Gong to pour into the sea, then the calamity of the prefectures and counties of Xing, Yan, and Tai will cease.
translations.idiomatic: open the Dike of Fan Gong to the sea and the troubles of Xing, Yan, and Tai will cease.

sentences.zh: 當路者頗韙其言，而未能用。

translations.literal: Those in power largely approved his words but were unable to implement them.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power largely approved his plan but could not implement it.

sentences.zh: 京察，大臣當自陳。

translations.literal: At the capital evaluation, grand ministers were to report on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital evaluation grand ministers were to report on themselves.

sentences.zh: 高宗命自陳者各舉一人自代。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor ordered each self-reporting official to recommend one man to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor ordered each reporting official to recommend one successor.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士李清植舉亨陽，時論以為允。

translations.literal: Cabinet Academician Li Qingzhi recommended Hengyang, and public opinion deemed it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Cabinet Academician Li Qingzhi recommended Hengyang, and opinion judged the choice apt.

sentences.zh: 勘淮海災過勞，以羸疾卒。

translations.literal: Surveying the Huai-Hai calamity he overworked himself and died of emaciating illness.
translations.idiomatic: He overworked surveying the Huai-Hai disaster and died of exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，淮海諸氓罷巿奔走，樹幟哭而投賻。

translations.literal: On the day he died the common people of Huai and Hai closed their markets and ran about, raising banners, weeping, and offering funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died the people of Huai and Hai closed their markets, ran through the streets weeping, and offered funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 訥親巡江南，監司皆鞾袴跪迎，亨陽獨長揖，訥責問，曰：「非敢惜此膝於公，其如會典所無何？」

translations.literal: When Neqin inspected Jiangnan, surveillance commissioners all knelt in boots and trousers to welcome him; Hengyang alone made a long bow. Neqin rebuked and questioned him; he said: "It is not that I begrudge this knee to you, but what of the fact that the statutes do not provide for it?
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin inspected Jiangnan, surveillance commissioners knelt in boots to welcome him; Hengyang alone bowed from the waist. Neqin rebuked him; he replied: "I do not begrudge my knee to you, but the statutes provide no such ceremony.

sentences.zh: 訥默然。

translations.literal: Neqin was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin fell silent.

sentences.zh: 亨陽出巡，屬吏循故事餽殽，然一切勿拒，曰：「物以烹飪，卻之是暴天物而違人情也。」

translations.literal: When Hengyang went on inspection, subordinates according to custom offered dishes, yet he refused nothing, saying: "Things are meant to be cooked; to refuse them is to waste Heaven's goods and violate human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: On tour, subordinates offered dishes by custom; he refused nothing, saying: "Food is meant to be eaten; refusal wastes Heaven's bounty and offends human feeling.

sentences.zh: 所從僕皆自飲其馬，或犒之，跽而辭曰：「公視奴輩為兒子，不告而受，於心不安。

translations.literal: The servants who followed all watered their own horses; if rewarded they knelt and declined, saying: "The master treats us servants as sons; to accept without telling him unsettles the heart.
translations.idiomatic: His servants watered their own horses; if rewarded they knelt and declined: "You treat us as sons; to accept without telling you would trouble our hearts.

sentences.zh: 告公，公必命辭，是仍虛君惠也。」

translations.literal: If we tell the master, the master will surely order us to decline—that is still to make the gentleman's gift empty.
translations.idiomatic: If we tell you, you will only order us to refuse—making the gift empty anyway.

sentences.zh: 強之，皆伏地，誓指其心。

translations.literal: When pressed they all prostrated themselves, swearing by pointing to their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When pressed they prostrated themselves and swore by their hearts.

sentences.zh: 其感人如此。

translations.literal: Such was his power to move people.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his power to move people.

sentences.zh: 官獻瑤，字瑜卿，安溪人。

translations.literal: Guan Xianyao, courtesy name Yuqing, was a native of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Xianyao, styled Yuqing, came from Anxi.

sentences.zh: 執業於漳浦蔡世遠、桐城方苞，稱高足弟子。

translations.literal: He studied under Cai Shiyuan of Zhangpu and Fang Bao of Tongcheng and was called their foremost disciple.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Cai Shiyuan of Zhangpu and Fang Bao of Tongcheng and was counted their foremost disciple.

sentences.zh: 亦以楊名時薦，補助教。

translations.literal: Also through Yang Mingshi's recommendation he was appointed assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Through Yang Mingshi's recommendation he was appointed assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 甫入學，上事宜六條於其長。

translations.literal: As soon as he entered the college he submitted six items of policy to his superior.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he entered the college he submitted six policy proposals to his superior.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，選庶吉士，充三禮館纂修，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, he served on the compilation staff of the Three Rites Institute and was appointed editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, he entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, served on the Three Rites Institute, and was appointed editor.

sentences.zh: 九年，典試浙江。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as chief examiner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as chief examiner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋提督廣西、陝甘學政，遷洗馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to educational commissioner of Guangxi and Shaanxi-Gansu, then transferred to groom of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to educational commissioner of Guangxi and Shaanxi-Gansu, then transferred to groom of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 在關中求得宋張載二十餘代孫，囑其邑學官教之。

translations.literal: In the examination hall he found a twenty-some-generation descendant of Song Zhang Zai and ordered the county school official to teach him.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination hall he found a descendant of Zhang Zai twenty-odd generations removed and ordered the county school to educate him.

sentences.zh: 識韓城王杰於諸生，以為大器，果如其言。

translations.literal: He recognized Wang Jie of Hancheng among the students as a great vessel, and it proved as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Among the students he recognized Wang Jie of Hancheng as a great vessel, and events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 獻瑤少孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: Xianyao was orphaned young and served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Xianyao served his mother with deep filial piety.

sentences.zh: 自陝甘任滿歸，乞侍養。

translations.literal: When his term in Shaanxi-Gansu ended he returned and asked to serve her in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When his Shaanxi-Gansu term ended he returned and asked to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 奉母二十餘載，母年九十乃終。

translations.literal: He attended his mother for more than twenty years; she died at ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for his mother for more than twenty years until she died at ninety.

sentences.zh: 撫愛諸子弟，脩大小宗祠，增祭器，考禮經，遵時制以定儀式，立鄉規以教宗人，置義租以卹親族之貧者。

translations.literal: He lovingly raised the various younger relatives, repaired the large and small ancestral halls, increased sacrificial vessels, examined the ritual classics, followed current regulations to fix ceremonies, established village rules to instruct the clan, and set up charity rents to relieve poor kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He lovingly raised younger kinsmen, repaired the ancestral halls, increased sacrificial vessels, studied the ritual classics, fixed ceremonies according to current regulations, established village rules to instruct the clan, and set up charity rents for poor relatives.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 著讀易偶記三卷，尚書偶記三卷，尚書講藁，思問錄一卷，讀詩偶記二卷，周官偶記二卷，儀禮讀三卷，喪服私鈔並雜記一卷，春秋傳習錄五卷，孝經刊誤一卷，文集十六卷，詩集二卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Casual Notes on Reading the Changes in three juan, Casual Notes on the Documents in three juan, Draft Lectures on the Documents, Record of Reflective Inquiry in one juan, Casual Notes on Reading the Odes in two juan, Casual Notes on the Rites of Zhou in two juan, Reading the Rituals in three juan, Private Copy of Mourning Garments with Miscellaneous Notes in one juan, Record of Studying the Spring and Autumn Annals in five juan, Corrections to Errors in the Classic of Filial Piety in one juan, Collected Writings in sixteen juan, and Collected Poems in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Casual Notes on Reading the Changes (3 juan), Casual Notes on the Documents (3 juan), Draft Lectures on the Documents, Record of Reflective Inquiry (1 juan), Casual Notes on Reading the Odes (2 juan), Casual Notes on the Rites of Zhou (2 juan), Reading the Rituals (3 juan), Private Copy of Mourning Garments with Miscellaneous Notes (1 juan), Record of Studying the Spring and Autumn Annals (5 juan), Corrections to Errors in the Classic of Filial Piety (1 juan), Collected Writings (16 juan), and Collected Poems (2 juan).

sentences.zh: 王懋竑，字子中，寶應人。

translations.literal: Wang Maohong, courtesy name Zizhong, was a native of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maohong, styled Zizhong, came from Baoying.

sentences.zh: 少從叔父式丹學，刻勵篤志，精研朱子之學，身體力行。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under his uncle Shidan, exerting himself with steadfast resolve, deeply investigating Zhu Xi's learning and putting it into practice in his own life.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under his uncle Shidan, applying himself with tireless resolve, mastering Zhu Xi's learning and living it out in practice.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十七年成進士，年已五十一。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, he passed the jinshi examination when he was already fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year of Kangxi, he became a jinshi at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 乞就教職，補安慶府學教授，

translations.literal: He requested a teaching appointment and was appointed professor at the Anqing Prefectural School.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a teaching post and was appointed professor at the Anqing Prefectural School.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，以薦被召引見，授翰林院編修，在上書房行走。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, through recommendation he was summoned for an audience, appointed Hanlin compiler, and assigned to serve in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, on recommendation he was summoned for an audience, appointed Hanlin compiler, and assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 二年，以母憂去官，特賜內府白金為喪葬費。

translations.literal: In the second year he left office on account of mourning for his mother; the court specially granted inner-palace silver for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he left office to mourn his mother; the court specially granted silver from the inner palace for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 懋竑素善病，居喪毀瘠，服闋就職。

translations.literal: Maohong had always been prone to illness; during mourning he wasted away with grief, and when the mourning period ended he returned to office.
translations.idiomatic: Maohong had long been frail; during mourning he wasted away with grief, and when the mourning period ended he resumed his post.

sentences.zh: 旋以老病乞歸，越十六年卒。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on account of old age and illness and returned home; sixteen years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon begged leave on account of old age and illness and returned home; he died sixteen years later.

sentences.zh: 懋竑性恬淡，少嘗謂友人曰：「老屋三間，破書萬卷，平生志原足矣。」

translations.literal: Maohong was by nature quiet and content; in youth he once told a friend: "Three old rooms and ten thousand worn volumes—my life's wish is already fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Maohong was by nature quiet and content; in youth he once told a friend: "Three old rooms and ten thousand worn volumes—that is all my life's wish requires.

sentences.zh: 歸里後，杜門著書。

translations.literal: After returning home he shut his door and wrote books.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he shut his door and devoted himself to writing.

sentences.zh: 校定朱子年譜，大旨在辨為學次序，以攻姚江之說。

translations.literal: He revised Zhu Xi's chronological biography, his main aim being to clarify the order of learning so as to refute the Yangming school.
translations.idiomatic: He revised Zhu Xi's chronological biography, chiefly to clarify the proper sequence of learning and refute the Yangming school.

sentences.zh: 又所著白田雜著八卷，於朱子文集、語類考訂尤詳。

translations.literal: In his Miscellaneous Writings from Baitian in eight juan, his textual verification of Zhu Xi's collected writings and classified conversations is especially detailed.
translations.idiomatic: His Miscellaneous Writings from Baitian in eight juan contains especially detailed textual verification of Zhu Xi's collected writings and classified conversations.

sentences.zh: 謂易本義前九圖、筮儀皆後人依託，非朱子所作，其略云：「朱子於易，有本義，有啟蒙，與門人講論甚詳，而此九圖曾無一語及之。

translations.literal: He held that the nine diagrams and the divination protocol preceding Zhu Xi's Original Meaning of the Changes were later forgeries and not Zhu Xi's work; in summary he said: "Zhu Xi on the Changes had the Original Meaning and the Introduction to the Study of the Changes, and discussed them at length with his disciples, yet these nine diagrams are never mentioned in a single word.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the nine diagrams and the divination protocol prefixed to Zhu Xi's Original Meaning of the Changes were later forgeries, not Zhu Xi's own work; in summary he wrote: "Zhu Xi on the Changes had the Original Meaning and the Introduction to the Study of the Changes, and discussed them exhaustively with his disciples, yet not one word ever touches these nine diagrams.

sentences.zh: 九圖之不合本義、啟蒙者多矣，門人何以絕不致疑也？

translations.literal: The nine diagrams conflict with the Original Meaning and the Introduction in many places—why did the disciples never raise a doubt?
translations.idiomatic: The nine diagrams conflict with the Original Meaning and the Introduction in many places—why did his disciples never once raise a doubt?

sentences.zh: 本義之敘畫卦云：『自下而上，再倍而三，以成八卦。

translations.literal: The preface to the Original Meaning on forming the hexagrams says: 'From below upward, doubling twice and thrice to form the eight trigrams.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the Original Meaning on forming the hexagrams says: 'From below upward, doubling twice and thrice to form the eight trigrams.

sentences.zh: 八卦之上，各加八卦，以成六十四卦。』

translations.literal: Upon the eight trigrams, each trigram is added to form the sixty-four hexagrams.'
translations.idiomatic: Upon the eight trigrams, each trigram is added to form the sixty-four hexagrams.'

sentences.zh: 初不參邵子說。

translations.literal: At first it does not invoke Master Shao's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: At first it does not invoke Master Shao's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 至啟蒙，則一本邵子。

translations.literal: In the Introduction, however, it follows Master Shao entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the Introduction, however, it follows Master Shao throughout.

sentences.zh: 而邵子所傳，止有先天方圓圖。

translations.literal: What Master Shao transmitted was only the Prior Heaven square-and-circle diagram.
translations.idiomatic: What Master Shao transmitted was only the Prior Heaven square-and-circle diagram.

sentences.zh: 其伏羲八卦圖、文王八卦圖，則以經世演易圖推而得之。

translations.literal: The Fuxi Eight Trigrams Diagram and the King Wen Eight Trigrams Diagram were derived by inference from the Diagram for Expounding the Changes in the Classic of World Governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuxi Eight Trigrams Diagram and the King Wen Eight Trigrams Diagram were derived by inference from the Diagram for Expounding the Changes in the Classic of World Governance.

sentences.zh: 同州王氏、漢上朱氏易，皆有此二圖，啟蒙因之。

translations.literal: The Changes works of the Wang family of Tongzhou and the Zhu family of Han River both contain these two diagrams; the Introduction followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes works of the Wang family of Tongzhou and the Zhu family of Han River both contain these two diagrams; the Introduction followed them.

sentences.zh: 至朱子所自作橫圖六，則注大傳及邵子語於下，而不敢題曰伏羲六十四卦圖，其慎如此。

translations.literal: As for the six horizontal diagrams Zhu Xi made himself, he annotated passages from the Great Commentary and Master Shao's words below, yet did not dare title them the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Diagram—such was his caution.
translations.idiomatic: The six horizontal diagrams Zhu Xi composed himself bear annotations from the Great Commentary and Master Shao's words below, yet he did not dare title them the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Diagram—such was his caution.

sentences.zh: 今直云伏羲八卦次序圖、伏羲八卦方位圖、伏羲六十四卦次序圖，伏羲六十四卦方位圖，是孰受而孰傳之耶？

translations.literal: Now they are simply called the Fuxi Eight Trigrams Sequence Diagram, the Fuxi Eight Trigrams Position Diagram, the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Sequence Diagram, and the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Position Diagram—who received and transmitted them?
translations.idiomatic: Now they are simply called the Fuxi Eight Trigrams Sequence Diagram, the Fuxi Eight Trigrams Position Diagram, the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Sequence Diagram, and the Fuxi Sixty-Four Hexagrams Position Diagram—who received and transmitted them?

sentences.zh: 乃云伏羲四圖，其說皆出邵氏，邵氏止有先天一圖，其八卦圖後來所推，六橫圖朱子所作。

translations.literal: Yet it is said that the four Fuxi diagrams all derive from the Shao school; Master Shao had only the one Prior Heaven diagram—the Eight Trigrams diagrams were later inferences, and the six horizontal diagrams were Zhu Xi's own work.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is said that the four Fuxi diagrams all derive from the Shao school; Master Shao had only the one Prior Heaven diagram—the Eight Trigrams diagrams were later inferences, and the six horizontal diagrams were Zhu Xi's own work.

sentences.zh: 以為皆出邵氏，是誣邵氏也。」

translations.literal: To claim they all came from Master Shao is to slander Master Shao."
translations.idiomatic: To claim they all came from Master Shao is to slander Master Shao."

sentences.zh: 又云：「邵氏得之李之才，李之才得之穆修，穆修得之希夷先生，此明道敘康節學問源流如此。

translations.literal: He also said: "Master Shao received it from Li Zhicai, Li Zhicai from Mu Xiu, Mu Xiu from Master Xiyi—this is how Mingdao narrated the lineage of Master Kangjie's learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Master Shao received it from Li Zhicai, Li Zhicai from Mu Xiu, Mu Xiu from Master Xiyi—this is how Mingdao narrated the lineage of Master Kangjie's learning.

sentences.zh: 漢上朱氏以先天圖屬之，已無所據。

translations.literal: The Zhu family of Han River already lacked grounds for attributing the Prior Heaven diagram to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhu family of Han River already lacked grounds for attributing the Prior Heaven diagram to him.

sentences.zh: 乃今移之四圖，若希夷已有此四圖也，是並誣希夷也。

translations.literal: Now to transfer all four diagrams to him, as if Master Xiyi already had these four diagrams, is to slander Master Xiyi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Now to transfer all four diagrams to him, as if Master Xiyi already possessed these four diagrams, is to slander Master Xiyi as well.

sentences.zh: 文王八卦，說卦明言之。

translations.literal: King Wen's eight trigrams are stated plainly in the Explanation of the Trigrams.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's eight trigrams are stated plainly in the Explanation of the Trigrams.

sentences.zh: 本義以為未詳，啟蒙別為之說，而不以入於本義。

translations.literal: The Original Meaning considers this unclear; the Introduction offers a separate account and does not incorporate it into the Original Meaning.
translations.idiomatic: The Original Meaning considers this unclear; the Introduction offers a separate account and does not incorporate it into the Original Meaning.

sentences.zh: 至於『乾，天也，故稱乎父』一節，本義以為揲蓍以求爻，啟蒙以為『乾求於坤，坤求於乾』與『乾為首』兩節，皆文王觀於已成之卦，而推其未明之象，與本義不同。

translations.literal: As for the passage 'Qian is Heaven, therefore called the father,' the Original Meaning takes it as about casting stalks to obtain lines; the Introduction takes it, together with the passages 'Qian seeks from Kun, Kun seeks from Qian' and 'Qian is the head,' as King Wen observing already-formed hexagrams and inferring images not yet made clear—differing from the Original Meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As for the passage 'Qian is Heaven, therefore called the father,' the Original Meaning takes it as about casting stalks to obtain lines; the Introduction takes it, together with the passages 'Qian seeks from Kun, Kun seeks from Qian' and 'Qian is the head,' as King Wen observing already-formed hexagrams and inferring images not yet made clear—differing from the Original Meaning.

sentences.zh: 今乃以為文王八卦次序圖，又孰受而孰傳之耶？

translations.literal: Now it is taken as the King Wen Eight Trigrams Sequence Diagram—again, who received and transmitted it?
translations.idiomatic: Now it is taken as the King Wen Eight Trigrams Sequence Diagram—again, who received and transmitted it?

sentences.zh: 卦變圖啟蒙詳之，蓋一卦可變為六十四卦，彖傳卦變，偶舉十九卦以說爾。

translations.literal: The Hexagram Transformation Diagram is treated in detail in the Introduction; generally one hexagram can transform into sixty-four hexagrams; the hexagram transformations in the Tuan commentary merely cite nineteen hexagrams as examples.
translations.idiomatic: The Hexagram Transformation Diagram is treated in detail in the Introduction; generally one hexagram can transform into sixty-four hexagrams; the hexagram transformations in the Tuan commentary merely cite nineteen hexagrams as examples.

sentences.zh: 今圖、卦皆不合，其非朱子之書明矣。」

translations.literal: Now the diagrams and hexagrams do not match—it is clear this is not Zhu Xi's book."
translations.idiomatic: Now the diagrams and hexagrams do not match—it is clear this is not Zhu Xi's book."

sentences.zh: 其說為宋、元儒者所未發。

translations.literal: This argument was something Song and Yuan Confucians had not developed.
translations.idiomatic: This was an argument Song and Yuan Confucians had not developed.

sentences.zh: 又考證諸史，謂：「孟子七篇，所言齊王皆湣王，非宣王。

translations.literal: He also verified various histories, saying: "In the seven chapters of Mencius, every reference to the Qi ruler is to King Min, not King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He also verified various histories, writing: "In the seven chapters of Mencius, every reference to the Qi ruler is to King Min, not King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 孟子去齊，當在湣王十三四年。

translations.literal: Mencius left Qi around the thirteenth or fourteenth year of King Min.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius left Qi around the thirteenth or fourteenth year of King Min.

sentences.zh: 下距湣王之歿，更二十五六年，孟子必不及見。

translations.literal: Down to King Min's death was another twenty-five or twenty-six years—Mencius could not have lived to see it.
translations.idiomatic: Down to King Min's death was another twenty-five or twenty-six years—Mencius could not have lived to see it.

sentences.zh: 公孫醜兩篇，稱王不稱諡，乃其元本，而梁惠王兩篇稱宣王，為後人所增。

translations.literal: The two chapters of Gongsun Chou call the ruler 'king' without posthumous title—that is the original text; the two chapters of King Hui of Liang call him King Xuan, added by later men.
translations.idiomatic: The two chapters of Gongsun Chou call the ruler 'king' without posthumous title—that is the original text; the two chapters of King Hui of Liang call him King Xuan, added by later men.

sentences.zh: 通鑑上增威王十年，下減湣王十年，蓋遷就伐燕之歲也。」

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror adds ten years to King Wei's reign above and subtracts ten years from King Min's below—adjusting to fit the year of the attack on Yan."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror adds ten years to King Wei's reign above and subtracts ten years from King Min's below—adjusting to fit the year of the attack on Yan."

sentences.zh: 可謂實事求是矣。

translations.literal: One may call this seeking truth from facts.
translations.idiomatic: One may call this seeking truth from facts.

sentences.zh: 同邑與懋竑學朱子學者，有朱澤澐、喬僅。

translations.literal: Fellow townsmen who studied Zhu Xi's learning with Maohong included Zhu Zeyun and Qiao Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsmen who studied Zhu Xi's learning with Maohong included Zhu Zeyun and Qiao Jin.

sentences.zh: 澤澐，字湘陶。

translations.literal: Zeyun, courtesy name Xiangtao.
translations.idiomatic: Zeyun, styled Xiangtao.

sentences.zh: 少勤學，得程氏讀書分年日程，尋序誦習。

translations.literal: In youth he studied diligently; obtaining the Cheng family's Schedule for Reading by Year, he followed it in order, reciting and practicing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied diligently; obtaining the Cheng family's Schedule for Reading by Year, he followed it in order, reciting and practicing.

sentences.zh: 更學天文於泰州陳厚耀，能得其意，久之，有志於聖人之道。

translations.literal: He further studied astronomy under Chen Houyao of Taizhou and grasped its principles; after long effort he aspired to the Way of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: He further studied astronomy under Chen Houyao of Taizhou and grasped its principles; after long effort he aspired to the Way of the sages.

sentences.zh: 念朱子之學，實繼周、程，紹顏、孟，以上溯孔子。

translations.literal: Reflecting that Zhu Xi's learning truly continued Zhou and Cheng, linked Yan and Mencius, and traced upward to Confucius,
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that Zhu Xi's learning truly continued Zhou and Cheng, linked Yan and Mencius, and traced upward to Confucius,

sentences.zh: 有謂朱子為道問學，陸、王為尊德性者，復取朱子文集、語類讀之，一字一句，無不精心研窮，反身體認，質之懋竑，懋竑屢答之。

translations.literal: when some said Zhu Xi stood for investigating things to extend knowledge while Lu and Wang stood for honoring moral nature, he again read Zhu Xi's collected writings and classified conversations, studying every word and phrase with utmost care, applying them to self-examination, and questioning Maohong, who answered repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: when some said Zhu Xi stood for investigating things to extend knowledge while Lu and Wang stood for honoring moral nature, he again read Zhu Xi's collected writings and classified conversations, studying every word and phrase with utmost care, applying them to self-examination, and questioning Maohong, who answered repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 深信朱子居敬、窮理之學，為孔子以來相傳的緒，窮即窮其所存之心，存即存其所窮之理，止是一事，喟然歎曰：「尊德性者，莫如朱子，道問學者，亦莫如朱子矣。」

translations.literal: He deeply trusted Zhu Xi's learning of reverent attentiveness and exhaustive investigation of principle as the transmitted thread since Confucius—investigation is investigating the mind as it is preserved, preservation is preserving the principle being investigated; they are one matter. He sighed and said: "For honoring moral nature, none surpasses Zhu Xi; for investigating things to extend knowledge, none surpasses Zhu Xi either."
translations.idiomatic: He deeply trusted Zhu Xi's learning of reverent attentiveness and exhaustive investigation of principle as the transmitted thread since Confucius—investigation is investigating the mind as it is preserved, preservation is preserving the principle being investigated; they are one matter. He sighed and said: "For honoring moral nature, none surpasses Zhu Xi; for investigating things to extend knowledge, none surpasses Zhu Xi either."

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，詔大臣各舉所知。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, an edict ordered the high ministers each to recommend men they knew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, an edict ordered the high ministers each to recommend men they knew.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督劉師恕欲薦於朝，使其弟造廬請，弗應。

translations.literal: Zhili governor-general Liu Shishu wished to recommend him to the court and sent his younger brother to his cottage to ask, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili governor-general Liu Shishu wished to recommend him to the court and sent his younger brother to his cottage to ask, but he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 晚年得髀疾，然猶五更起，盥沐，觀書至夜分不倦。

translations.literal: In his later years he suffered from a thigh ailment, yet he still rose at the fifth watch, washed, and read until midnight without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he suffered from a thigh ailment, yet he still rose at the fifth watch, washed, and read until midnight without tiring.

sentences.zh: 誡其子光進曰：「聖賢工夫，正於困苦時驗之。」

translations.literal: He admonished his son Guangjin, saying: “The work of sages and worthies is tested precisely in times of hardship.”
translations.idiomatic: He admonished his son Guangjin, saying: “The work of sages and worthies is tested precisely in times of hardship.”

sentences.zh: 疾甚，謂門人喬僅曰：「死生平常事，時至則行，無所戀也。」

translations.literal: When his illness became severe, he told his disciple Qiao Jin: “Death and life are ordinary matters. When the time arrives, one goes; there is nothing to cling to.”
translations.idiomatic: When his illness became severe, he told his disciple Qiao Jin: “Death and life are ordinary matters. When the time arrives, one goes; there is nothing to cling to.”

sentences.zh: 吟邵雍詩，怡然而逝，年六十有七。

translations.literal: He chanted a poem by Shao Yong and passed away peacefully, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He chanted a poem by Shao Yong and passed away peacefully, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 所著止泉文集八卷，朱子聖賢考略十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included Zhixuan Collected Writings in eight juan and Concise Studies of Zhu Xi, Sages, and Worthies in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Zhixuan Collected Writings in eight juan and Concise Studies of Zhu Xi, Sages, and Worthies in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 僅，字星渚。

translations.literal: Jin, courtesy name Xingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin, styled Xingzhu.

sentences.zh: 少有氣節。

translations.literal: In youth he had strong moral fiber.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had strong moral fiber.

sentences.zh: 水決子嬰堤，眾走避，僅倡議捍塞，十日堤成。

translations.literal: When the Ziying embankment burst, the crowd fled; Jin alone proposed blocking and repairing it, and in ten days the dike was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ziying embankment burst, the crowd fled; Jin alone proposed blocking and repairing it, and in ten days the dike was complete.

sentences.zh: 從澤澐受學，恪遵朱子教人讀書次第。

translations.literal: He received instruction from Zeyun and strictly followed Zhu Xi's prescribed order for reading.
translations.idiomatic: He received instruction from Zeyun and strictly followed Zhu Xi's prescribed order for reading.

sentences.zh: 取朱子書切己體察，有疑輒質澤澐，時年五十矣。

translations.literal: He took Zhu Xi's books and applied them to self-examination; whenever he had doubts he questioned Zeyun—he was already fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhu Xi's books and applied them to self-examination; whenever he had doubts he questioned Zeyun—he was already fifty.

sentences.zh: 澤澐稱之曰：「從吾遊者眾矣，惟喬君剛甚。」

translations.literal: Zeyun praised him: "Of those who have studied with me, many—but only Master Qiao is truly resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Zeyun praised him: "Of those who have studied with me, many—but only Master Qiao is truly resolute.

sentences.zh: 因舉或問過時後學、語類訓石洪慶語告之，僅益奮，

translations.literal: He therefore cited passages from the Classified Conversations on late learners and Shih Hongqing's instruction to tell him; Jin was all the more inspired.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore cited passages from the Classified Conversations on late learners and Shih Hongqing's instruction to tell him; Jin was all the more inspired.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉孝廉方正，辭不就。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt and Rectified, but declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt and Rectified, but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 與懋竑書，論學問之道凡再三。

translations.literal: He exchanged letters with Maohong on the Way of learning, altogether several times.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged letters with Maohong on the Way of learning, altogether several times.

sentences.zh: 自謂向道晚，須用己百之功。

translations.literal: He said himself that he came to the Way late and must apply the effort of one who corrects a hundred failures.
translations.idiomatic: He said himself that he came to the Way late and must apply the effort of one who corrects a hundred failures.

sentences.zh: 聞弟卒江陵任，即日冒雪行數千里扶櫬歸。

translations.literal: When he heard his younger brother had died in office at Jiangling, that very day he traveled several thousand li through the snow to bring the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard his younger brother had died in office at Jiangling, that very day he traveled several thousand li through the snow to bring the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 有潘某貸金不能償，以券與之。

translations.literal: A certain Pan owed him gold and could not repay; he gave him the bond.
translations.idiomatic: A certain Pan owed him gold and could not repay; he gave him the bond.

sentences.zh: 疾革，曰：「吾自頂至踵，無一處不痛。

translations.literal: As his illness worsened he said: "From crown to heel, not one place is free of pain.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he said: "From crown to heel, not one place is free of pain.

sentences.zh: 惟此心凝然不亂耳！」

translations.literal: Only this heart remains concentrated and unconfused!"
translations.idiomatic: Only this heart remains concentrated and unconfused!"

sentences.zh: 命沐浴正衣冠而逝，年六十五。

translations.literal: He ordered bathing, straightened his robes and cap, and passed away, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered bathing, straightened his robes and cap, and passed away, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 著日省錄、訓子要言、困學堂遺稿，湯金釗序而行之。

translations.literal: He wrote Daily Self-Examination Record, Essential Words for Instructing Sons, and Posthumous Drafts from the Studio of Struggling to Learn; Tang Jinzhai preface and published them.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Daily Self-Examination Record, Essential Words for Instructing Sons, and Posthumous Drafts from the Studio of Struggling to Learn; Tang Jinzhai preface and published them.

sentences.zh: 謂其「學術剛健篤實，發為輝光，粹然有德之言」。

translations.literal: Tang said his "learning was vigorous, solid, and sincere, issuing in radiant brilliance—pure words of virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Tang said his "learning was vigorous, solid, and sincere, issuing in radiant brilliance—pure words of virtue."

sentences.zh: 李夢箕，字季豹，連城人。

translations.literal: Li Mengji, courtesy name Jibao, was a native of Liancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mengji, styled Jibao, came from Liancheng.

sentences.zh: 年十五而孤。

translations.literal: At fifteen he was orphaned.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was orphaned.

sentences.zh: 精進學業，崇向朱子，以孝友著稱。

translations.literal: He advanced in his studies, revered Zhu Xi, and was renowned for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced in his studies, revered Zhu Xi, and was renowned for filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 其教人輒言為善最樂，人易而忽之。

translations.literal: In teaching others he always said that doing good is the greatest joy; people took it lightly and neglected it.
translations.idiomatic: In teaching others he always said that doing good is the greatest joy; people took it lightly and neglected it.

sentences.zh: 夢箕曰：「為之難，汝為之否乎？」

translations.literal: Mengji said: "It is hard to do—will you not do it?
translations.idiomatic: Mengji said: "It is hard to do—will you not do it?

sentences.zh: 人問之曰：「其樂何如？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: "What is that joy like?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "What is that joy like?

sentences.zh: 曰：「不愧不怍，」「孰與孔、顏之樂？」

translations.literal: He said: "Without shame, without inner distress," "How does it compare with the joy of Confucius and Yan?
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Without shame, without inner distress." "How does it compare with the joy of Confucius and Yan?

sentences.zh: 曰：「熟之而已矣！」

translations.literal: He said: "One need only become thoroughly familiar with it!"
