translations.idiomatic: He said: "One need only become thoroughly familiar with it!"

sentences.zh: 事兄如嚴父，撫猶子如子。

translations.literal: He served his elder brother as a strict father and raised his nephew as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He served his elder brother as a strict father and raised his nephew as a son.

sentences.zh: 每語諸子以氣質之偏，使知變化。

translations.literal: He always told his sons about biases in temperament so they would know how to transform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He always told his sons about biases in temperament so they would know how to transform themselves.

sentences.zh: 疾亟，謂所親曰：「吾生平竭力檢身，將毋有不及省者？

translations.literal: As his illness became urgent he told those close to him: "All my life I have exerted myself to examine my person—are there things I have failed to reflect on?
translations.idiomatic: As his illness became urgent he told those close to him: "All my life I have exerted myself to examine my person—are there things I have failed to reflect on?

sentences.zh: 第言之，得聞過而終，亦云幸矣。」

translations.literal: Just speak of them; to hear my faults and die would also be fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Just speak of them; to hear my faults and die would also be fortunate.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子圖南，字開士。

translations.literal: His son Tunan, courtesy name Kaishi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tunan, styled Kaishi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十一年舉人。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi, a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi, a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 能世其學。

translations.literal: He could inherit his father's learning.
translations.idiomatic: He could inherit his father's learning.

sentences.zh: 初工詩古文，既而歎曰：「吾學自有身心性命所宜急者，可以虛名騖乎？」

translations.literal: At first he excelled at poetry and ancient prose, then sighed and said: "My learning has matters of body, heart, and life-and-death that should be urgent—can I chase empty reputation?
translations.idiomatic: At first he excelled at poetry and ancient prose, then sighed and said: "My learning has matters of body, heart, and life-and-death that should be urgent—can I chase empty reputation?

sentences.zh: 於是究心濂、洛、關、閩書，以反躬切己為務。

translations.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself to the books of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, making introspection and self-application his task.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he devoted himself to the books of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, making introspection and self-application his task.

sentences.zh: 居連峰、點石諸山中者久之。

translations.literal: He dwelt long in the mountains at Lianfeng, Dianshi, and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt long in the mountains at Lianfeng, Dianshi, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「學者唯利名之念為害最大。

translations.literal: He once said: "For scholars, the thought of profit and fame does the greatest harm.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "For scholars, the thought of profit and fame does the greatest harm.

sentences.zh: 越此庶可與共學。」

translations.literal: Pass beyond this and one may study together.
translations.idiomatic: Pass beyond this and one may study together.

sentences.zh: 與蔡世遠講明修身窮理之要，世遠重之，

translations.literal: He and Cai Shiyuan expounded the essentials of self-cultivation and exhaustive investigation of principle; Shiyuan held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: He and Cai Shiyuan expounded the essentials of self-cultivation and exhaustive investigation of principle; Shiyuan held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年，吏部檄天下舉人需次縣令者先赴京學習政事，圖南至，觀政戶部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongzheng, the Board of Personnel ordered provincial graduates awaiting appointment as county magistrates to come first to the capital to study administration; Tunan arrived and observed affairs at the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongzheng, the Board of Personnel ordered provincial graduates awaiting appointment as county magistrates to come first to the capital to study administration; Tunan arrived and observed affairs at the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以母病亟歸，歸先母卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: His mother's illness became urgent and he returned; he arrived home just before his mother died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's illness became urgent and he returned; he arrived home just before his mother died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 雷鋐謂：「學聖人必自狷者始，圖南庶足當之。」

translations.literal: Lei Hong said: "To learn from the sages one must begin with the resolute—Tunan may well suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Lei Hong said: "To learn from the sages one must begin with the resolute—Tunan may well suffice."

sentences.zh: 時邑人張鵬翼、童能靈皆以學行稱。

translations.literal: At the time fellow townsmen Zhang Pengyi and Tong Nengling were also renowned for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time fellow townsmen Zhang Pengyi and Tong Nengling were also renowned for learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 鵬翼，字蜚子。

translations.literal: Pengyi, courtesy name Feizi.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyi, styled Feizi.

sentences.zh: 歲貢生。

translations.literal: A senior licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A senior licentiate.

sentences.zh: 八歲嗜學，十餘歲通諸經。

translations.literal: At eight he loved learning; by his teens he had mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he loved learning; by his teens he had mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 塾師教以作文取科第，心疑之。

translations.literal: When his schoolteacher taught essay-writing for the examinations he inwardly doubted it.
translations.idiomatic: When his schoolteacher taught essay-writing for the examinations he inwardly doubted it.

sentences.zh: 熟讀四書大全，忽悟曰：「心當在身內，身當在心內。」

translations.literal: Reading the Great Compendium of the Four Books thoroughly, he suddenly understood and said: "The heart should be within the body; the body should be within the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Great Compendium of the Four Books thoroughly, he suddenly understood and said: "The heart should be within the body; the body should be within the heart.

sentences.zh: 遂不仕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he declined office.

sentences.zh: 連城處萬山中，無師。

translations.literal: Liancheng lies deep among myriad mountains, with no teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Liancheng lay deep among ten thousand mountains, with no teachers to be found.

sentences.zh: 鵬翼年已四十，始見近思錄及朱子全書。

translations.literal: Pengyi was already forty before he first saw the Reflections on Things Near at Hand and Zhu Xi's Complete Works.
translations.idiomatic: Pengyi was already forty before he first saw the Reflections on Things Near at Hand and Zhu Xi's Complete Works.

sentences.zh: 更十年，始見薛文清讀書錄。

translations.literal: Ten years more passed before he first saw Xue Wenqing's Record of Reading.
translations.idiomatic: Another ten years passed before he first saw Xue Wenqing's Record of Reading.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「考亭易簀之時，乃我下帷之始。」

translations.literal: He once said: "When Master Kaoting changed his mat was when my study behind closed doors began.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "When Master Kaoting changed his mat—that was when my study behind closed doors began.

sentences.zh: 蓋俛焉日有孳孳，不知其老且耄也。

translations.literal: He bent himself to daily effort, unaware that he was growing old and aged.
translations.idiomatic: He bent himself to daily effort, unaware that he was growing old and frail.

sentences.zh: 所居鄉曰新泉，男女往來二橋，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: The village where he lived was called Xinquan; men and women crossing the two bridges lost nothing on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The village where he lived was called Xinquan; men and women crossing its two bridges lost nothing on the road.

sentences.zh: 巿中交易，先讓外客，皆服鵬翼教也。

translations.literal: In market transactions they yielded first to outside customers—all obeyed Pengyi's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In market transactions they yielded first to outside customers—all in obedience to Pengyi's teaching.

sentences.zh: 著有讀經說略、理學入門、孝子傳、歷代將相諫臣三譜、二十二史案、芝壇日讀小記。

translations.literal: He wrote Outline of Reading the Classics, Introduction to Neo-Confucian Learning, Biographies of Filial Sons, Three Genealogies of Generals, Ministers, and Remonstrating Officials through the Ages, Cases from the Twenty-Two Histories, and Daily Reading Notes from the Zhitan.
translations.idiomatic: His works included Outline of Reading the Classics, Introduction to Neo-Confucian Learning, Biographies of Filial Sons, Three Genealogies of Generals, Ministers, and Remonstrating Officials through the Ages, Cases from the Twenty-Two Histories, and Daily Reading Notes from the Zhitan.

sentences.zh: 能靈，字龍儔。

translations.literal: Nengling, courtesy name Longchou.
translations.idiomatic: Nengling, styled Longchou.

sentences.zh: 貢生。

translations.literal: A tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute student.

sentences.zh: 好學，守程、朱家法，不失尺寸，

translations.literal: He loved learning and kept the methods of the Cheng and Zhu schools without the slightest deviation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and kept the methods of the Cheng and Zhu schools without the slightest deviation.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，舉博學鴻詞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was nominated for the erudite examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong, he was nominated for the erudite examination.

sentences.zh: 累舉優行，皆以母老辭。

translations.literal: Repeatedly nominated for outstanding conduct, he always declined on account of his aged mother.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly nominated for outstanding conduct, he always declined on account of his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 年九十，兄弟白首同居。

translations.literal: At ninety he and his brothers lived together, all white-haired.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety he and his brothers lived together, all white-haired.

sentences.zh: 居喪以禮，化及鄉人。

translations.literal: He observed mourning according to ritual, and his example transformed the villagers.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning according to ritual, and his example transformed the villagers.

sentences.zh: 能靈嘗與雷鋐論易，主河圖以明像數之學。

translations.literal: Nengling once debated the Changes with Lei Hong, upholding the River Diagram to clarify the learning of images and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Nengling once debated the Changes with Lei Hong, upholding the River Diagram to clarify the learning of images and numbers.

sentences.zh: 其樂律古義，謂：「洛書為五音之本，河圖為洛書之源。

translations.literal: On the ancient meaning of pitch pipes he said: "The Luo Writing is the root of the five tones; the River Diagram is the source of the Luo Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On the ancient meaning of pitch pipes he said: "The Luo Writing is the root of the five tones; the River Diagram is the source of the Luo Writing.

sentences.zh: 河圖圓而為氣，洛書方而為體。

translations.literal: The River Diagram is round and is qi; the Luo Writing is square and is form.
translations.idiomatic: The River Diagram is round and is qi; the Luo Writing is square and is form.

sentences.zh: 五音者氣也，氣凝為體，體以聚氣，然後聲音出焉。

translations.literal: The five tones are qi; qi congeals into form, form gathers qi, and then sound emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The five tones are qi; qi congeals into form, form gathers qi, and then sound emerges.

sentences.zh: 蔡氏律呂新書沿《淮南子》、《漢書》之說，誤以亥為黃鍾之實。

translations.literal: Master Cai's New Book on Pitch Pipes followed the Huainanzi and the Book of Han, wrongly taking hai as the solid note of Yellow Bell.
translations.idiomatic: Master Cai's New Book on Pitch Pipes followed the Huainanzi and the Book of Han, wrongly taking hai as the solid note of Yellow Bell.

sentences.zh: 惟所約寸分釐絲忽之法，其數合於史記律書，因取其說為之推究源委以成書。」

translations.literal: Only his method of inch, fen, li, si, and hu matched the numbers in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes in the Records of the Grand Historian; taking his account, Nengling traced its sources and completed a book.
translations.idiomatic: Only his method of inch, fen, li, si, and hu matched the numbers in the Treatise on Pitch Pipes in the Records of the Grand Historian; taking his account, Nengling traced its sources and completed a book.

sentences.zh: 他著中天河洛五倫說、朱子為學考、理學疑問。

translations.literal: He also wrote On the Five Relationships in the Central River and Luo Writings, An Inquiry into Zhu Xi's Learning, and Questions on Neo-Confucian Learning.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote On the Five Relationships in the Central River and Luo Writings, An Inquiry into Zhu Xi's Learning, and Questions on Neo-Confucian Learning.

sentences.zh: 連城理學，始自宋之邱起潛、明之童東皋，而能靈、鵬翼繼之。

translations.literal: Neo-Confucian learning in Liancheng began with Qiu Qiqian of Song and Tong Donggao of Ming; Nengling and Pengyi continued it.
translations.idiomatic: Neo-Confucian learning in Liancheng began with Qiu Qiqian of Song and Tong Donggao of Ming; Nengling and Pengyi continued it.

sentences.zh: 力敦倫紀，嚴辨朱、陸異同。

translations.literal: They vigorously upheld ethical order and strictly distinguished Zhu and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: They vigorously upheld ethical order and strictly distinguished Zhu and Lu.

sentences.zh: 張伯行撫閩時，建文溪書院，祀起潛、東皋。

translations.literal: When Zhang Boxing governed Fujian he built the Wenxi Academy and sacrificed to Qiqian and Donggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Boxing governed Fujian he built the Wenxi Academy and sacrificed to Qiqian and Donggao.

sentences.zh: 後增建五賢書院，中祀宋五子，而以能靈、鵬翼配焉。

translations.literal: Later the Five Worthies Academy was added; the Five Masters of Song were worshipped at the center, with Nengling and Pengyi as associated sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Five Worthies Academy was added; the Five Masters of Song were worshipped at the center, with Nengling and Pengyi as associated sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 胡方，字大靈，新會人。

translations.literal: Hu Fang, courtesy name Daling, was a native of Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang, styled Daling, came from Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 歲貢生。

translations.literal: A senior licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A senior licentiate.

sentences.zh: 方敦崇實行，處道學風氣之末，獨守堅確。

translations.literal: Fang deeply honored practical conduct; at the end of the Neo-Confucian trend he alone held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Fang deeply honored practical conduct; at the end of the Neo-Confucian trend he alone held firm.

sentences.zh: 總督吳興祚聞其名，使招之，方走匿，不能得也。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wu Xingzuo heard his name and sent to summon him; Fang fled and hid, and could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wu Xingzuo heard his name and sent to summon him; Fang fled and hid, and could not be found.

sentences.zh: 事父母，色養靡不周，而心常如不及。

translations.literal: In serving his parents his attentive care was thorough, yet his heart always felt as if it fell short.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his parents his attentive care was thorough, yet his heart always felt as if it fell short.

sentences.zh: 遇有病，憂形於色，藥必嘗而後進。

translations.literal: When they fell ill, worry showed on his face; he always tasted medicine before presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: When they fell ill, worry showed on his face; he always tasted medicine before presenting it.

sentences.zh: 夜必衣冠侍，未嘗就寢。

translations.literal: At night he always waited in full dress and never went to bed.
translations.idiomatic: At night he always waited in full dress and never went to bed.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，藉草宿柩旁，三年不入內。

translations.literal: During mourning he slept on straw beside the coffin and did not enter the inner quarters for three years.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he slept on straw beside the coffin and did not enter the inner quarters for three years.

sentences.zh: 先人田廬，悉以與弟，授徒自給。

translations.literal: He gave all his forefathers' fields and houses to his younger brother and supported himself by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all his forefathers' fields and houses to his younger brother and supported himself by teaching.

sentences.zh: 族姻不能自存者，竭力資之。

translations.literal: For clansmen and in-laws who could not support themselves, he exerted himself to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: For clansmen and in-laws who could not support themselves, he exerted himself to aid them.

sentences.zh: 有達官齎重金乞其文為壽，不應；

translations.literal: A high official brought heavy gold begging his writing for a birthday celebration—he did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: A high official brought heavy gold begging his writing for a birthday celebration—he did not respond;

sentences.zh: 吏懾之，不應；

translations.literal: an attendant threatened him—he did not respond;
translations.idiomatic: an attendant threatened him—he did not respond;

sentences.zh: 家人告以絕糧，不應。

translations.literal: his family told him they had no grain—he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: his family told him they had no grain—he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 鄉曲子弟偶蹈不韙，有原就鞭撲，不原聞其事於方者。

translations.literal: When village youths occasionally transgressed, some would rather be whipped than have Fang hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: When village youths occasionally transgressed, some would rather be whipped than have Fang hear of it.

sentences.zh: 里中語曰：「可被他人笞，勿使胡君知。

translations.literal: A village saying ran: "Better be beaten by others than let Master Hu know.
translations.idiomatic: A village saying ran: "Better be beaten by others than let Master Hu know.

sentences.zh: 他人笞猶可，胡君愧煞我。」

translations.literal: Beaten by others is still bearable; Master Hu would shame me to death.
translations.idiomatic: Beaten by others is still bearable; Master Hu would shame me to death.

sentences.zh: 其從學者，仕與未仕，白首猶懍懍奉其教。

translations.literal: Those who followed his learning, whether in office or not, white-haired still reverently obeyed his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Those who followed his learning, whether in office or not, white-haired still reverently obeyed his teaching.

sentences.zh: 雖困甚，終不入公庭。

translations.literal: However hard pressed, they never entered the yamen.
translations.idiomatic: However hard pressed, they never entered the yamen.

sentences.zh: 聞聲向慕，以得見為喜，曰：「教我矣！」

translations.literal: Hearing his reputation they yearned toward him; to meet him was joy, and they said: "He has taught me!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing his reputation they yearned toward him; to meet him was joy, and they said: "He has taught me!

sentences.zh: 有以廕得官，則大慚曰：「吾未能信，得無辱我夫子。」

translations.literal: When one obtained office through yin privilege he was deeply ashamed and said: "I am not yet confident—would this not disgrace our master?
translations.idiomatic: When one obtained office through yin privilege he was deeply ashamed and said: "I am not yet confident—would this not disgrace our master?

sentences.zh: 方告之曰：「為官能不愛錢，致力於官守，有何不可？」

translations.literal: Fang told him: "If in office you can refrain from loving money and devote yourself to your duties, what is impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Fang told him: "If in office you can refrain from loving money and devote yourself to your duties, what is impossible?

sentences.zh: 其人卒不負其言。

translations.literal: That man in the end did not betray his words.
translations.idiomatic: That man in the end did not betray his words.

sentences.zh: 四十後杜門著述，所居曰鹽步。

translations.literal: After forty he shut his door and wrote; his dwelling was called Yanbu.
translations.idiomatic: After forty he shut his door and wrote; his dwelling was called Yanbu.

sentences.zh: 元和惠士奇督學粵東，聞方名，艤舟村外，遣吳生至其家求一見，急揮手曰：「學政未蕆事，不可見！

translations.literal: Hui Shiqi of Yuanhe, as educational commissioner of Guangdong, heard Fang's name, moored his boat outside the village, and sent a student Wu to his home requesting an audience; Fang hurriedly waved his hand: "The commissioner has not finished his duties—no audience!
translations.idiomatic: Hui Shiqi of Yuanhe, as educational commissioner of Guangdong, heard Fang's name, moored his boat outside the village, and sent a student Wu to his home requesting an audience; Fang hurriedly waved his hand: "The commissioner has not finished his duties—no audience!

sentences.zh: 不可見！」

translations.literal: No audience!
translations.idiomatic: No audience!

sentences.zh: 出吳而扃其門。

translations.literal: He sent Wu out and barred his door.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu out and barred his door.

sentences.zh: 士奇乃索所著書而去。

translations.literal: Shiqi then asked for his writings and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi then asked for his writings and left.

sentences.zh: 試事畢，仍介吳生以請，則假一冠投刺，至，長揖曰：「今日齋沐謝知己。

translations.literal: When the examinations were finished he again sent Wu to request an audience; Fang borrowed a cap, sent his card, and when he arrived bowed with hands clasped: "Today, bathed and purified, I thank my knowing friend.
translations.idiomatic: When the examinations were finished he again sent Wu to request an audience; Fang borrowed a cap, sent his card, and when he arrived bowed with hands clasped: "Today, bathed and purified, I thank my knowing friend.

sentences.zh: 方年邁，無受教地，不能執弟子禮。」

translations.literal: Fang is old and has no place to receive instruction; I cannot perform the disciple's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fang is old and has no place to receive instruction; I cannot perform the disciple's rites.

sentences.zh: 數語遂起。

translations.literal: A few words and he rose.
translations.idiomatic: A few words and he rose.

sentences.zh: 惠握其手曰：「縱不欲多語，敢問先生，鄉人誰能為文者？」

translations.literal: Hui grasped his hand and said: "Though you do not wish to say much, dare I ask, Master—who in your village can write?
translations.idiomatic: Hui grasped his hand and said: "Though you do not wish to say much, dare I ask, Master—who in your village can write?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「並世中無人。

translations.literal: He answered: "Among contemporaries there is no one.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Among contemporaries there is no one.

sentences.zh: 必求之，惟明季梁朝鐘耳！」

translations.literal: If one must seek, only Liang Chaozhong of the late Ming!
translations.idiomatic: If one must seek, only Liang Chaozhong of the late Ming!

sentences.zh: 士奇遂求梁文並各家文刻之，名曰嶺南文選。

translations.literal: Shiqi then sought Liang's writings and those of various masters and printed them under the title Selected Writings of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi then sought Liang's writings and those of various masters and printed them under the title Selected Writings of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 既而疏薦於朝。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized recommending him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he memorialized recommending him to the court.

sentences.zh: 士奇嘗語吳生曰：「胡君貌似顧炎武，豐厚端偉，必享大名。」

translations.literal: Shiqi once told the student Wu: "Master Hu resembles Gu Yanwu—full-bodied and dignified; he will surely enjoy great fame.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi once told the student Wu: "Master Hu resembles Gu Yanwu—full-bodied and dignified; he will surely enjoy great fame.

sentences.zh: 蓋當時知方者，士奇一人而已。

translations.literal: At the time Shiqi alone knew Fang's worth.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shiqi alone knew Fang's worth.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 著有周易本義註六卷，四子書註十卷，莊子註四卷，鴻桷堂詩文集六卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Commentary on the Original Meaning of the Book of Changes in six juan, Commentary on the Four Books in ten juan, Commentary on Zhuangzi in four juan, and Collected Poetry and Prose from the Hongjue Hall in six juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Commentary on the Original Meaning of the Book of Changes in six juan, Commentary on the Four Books in ten juan, Commentary on Zhuangzi in four juan, and Collected Poetry and Prose from the Hongjue Hall in six juan.

sentences.zh: 集中謁白沙祠諸作及白沙子論，具見淵源所自。

translations.literal: In the collection, works visiting the Baisha Shrine and the Treatise on Master Baisha fully reveal the source of his lineage.
translations.idiomatic: In the collection, works visiting the Baisha Shrine and the Treatise on Master Baisha fully reveal the source of his lineage.

sentences.zh: 粵中勵志篤行者，方後有馮成修、勞潼。

translations.literal: Among those in Guangdong who resolved their will and practiced steadfastly, after Fang came Feng Chengxiu and Lao Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Among those in Guangdong who resolved their will and practiced steadfastly, after Fang came Feng Chengxiu and Lao Tong.

sentences.zh: 成修，字達夫，南海人。

translations.literal: Chengxiu, courtesy name Dafu, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxiu, styled Dafu, came from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 父遠出不歸，成修生有至性，語及其父，輒涕泗交頤。

translations.literal: His father went far away and did not return; Chengxiu was born with utmost sincerity, and whenever he spoke of his father tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: His father went far away and did not return; Chengxiu was born with utmost sincerity, and whenever he spoke of his father tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，選庶吉士，散館改吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, after leaving the Hanlin he was changed to a principal clerk in the Board of Civil Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, after leaving the Hanlin he was changed to a principal clerk in the Board of Civil Officials.

sentences.zh: 晉禮部祠祭司郎中，典試福建、四川，督學貴州，揭條約十四則以訓士。

translations.literal: Promoted to director in the Sacrificial Ceremonies Bureau of the Board of Rites, he served as chief examiner of Fujian and Sichuan, educational commissioner of Guizhou, and posted fourteen articles of covenant to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director in the Sacrificial Ceremonies Bureau of the Board of Rites, he served as chief examiner of Fujian and Sichuan, educational commissioner of Guizhou, and posted fourteen articles of covenant to instruct scholars.

sentences.zh: 成修初計偕，即遍訪其父蹤跡。

translations.literal: When Chengxiu first went to the capital for the examinations, he already searched everywhere for traces of his father.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengxiu first went to the capital for the examinations, he already searched everywhere for traces of his father.

sentences.zh: 得官後，兩次乞假尋親，卒無所遇，不復出。

translations.literal: After obtaining office he twice begged leave to seek his parent, found nothing, and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: After obtaining office he twice begged leave to seek his parent, found nothing, and never went out again.

sentences.zh: 授經里中，粹然師範。

translations.literal: He taught the classics in his village—a pure model as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the classics in his village—a pure model as teacher.

sentences.zh: 年八十，計其父已百有一齡。

translations.literal: At eighty he calculated that his father would already be one hundred and one.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he calculated that his father would already be one hundred and one.

sentences.zh: 乃持服三年，終身衣布。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wore mourning for three years and wore cloth all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wore mourning for three years and wore cloth all his life.

sentences.zh: 乙卯重宴鹿鳴，逾年卒，年九十有五。

translations.literal: At the yimao repeat banquet for senior licentiates, a year later he died, aged ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the yimao repeat banquet for senior licentiates, a year later he died, aged ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 潼，字潤芝，亦南海人。

translations.literal: Tong, courtesy name Runzhi, was also from Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, styled Runzhi, was also from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十年舉人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 髫齡時，母常於榻上授毛詩，長遂習焉。

translations.literal: In childhood his mother often taught him the Book of Odes on her couch; when grown he continued the practice.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood his mother often taught him the Book of Odes on her couch; when grown he continued the practice.

sentences.zh: 盧文弨視學湖南，召之往。

translations.literal: Lu Wenchao, as educational commissioner of Hunan, summoned him to come.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenchao, as educational commissioner of Hunan, summoned him to come.

sentences.zh: 至冬乃歸，母思念殊切。

translations.literal: He returned only in winter; his mother missed him intensely.
translations.idiomatic: He returned only in winter; his mother missed him intensely.

sentences.zh: 抵家時漏三下，跪母榻前，母且泣且撫之曰：「其夢也耶？」

translations.literal: When he reached home it was the third watch; kneeling before his mother's couch, she wept and stroked him, saying: "Is this a dream?
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home it was the third watch; kneeling before his mother's couch, she wept and stroked him, saying: "Is this a dream?

sentences.zh: 潼悲不自勝，自是絕意進取，侍養十有六年而母卒。

translations.literal: Tong grieved beyond bearing; from then on he abandoned all ambition for advancement and served his mother for sixteen years until she died.
translations.idiomatic: Tong grieved beyond bearing; from then on he abandoned all ambition for advancement and served his mother for sixteen years until she died.

sentences.zh: 潼哀毀骨立，杖而後起。

translations.literal: Tong mourned until he was wasted to the bone and could rise only with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Tong mourned until he was wasted to the bone and could rise only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 家人或失潼所在，即於殯所覓之，則已慟哭失聲矣。

translations.literal: When the family could not find Tong, they looked at the mourning hall and there he was, already wailing aloud.
translations.idiomatic: When the family could not find Tong, they looked at the mourning hall and there he was, already wailing aloud.

sentences.zh: 又痛早孤，故以莪野為號。

translations.literal: Grieving also for early orphanhood, he took E'ye as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving also for early orphanhood, he took E'ye as his sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「讀孔子書，得一言，曰『務民之義』；

translations.literal: He once said: "Reading Confucius's books, I gained one saying: 'Devote yourself to the duties proper to the people';
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Reading Confucius's books, I gained one saying: 'Devote yourself to the duties proper to the people';

sentences.zh: 讀孟子書，得一言，曰『強為善而已矣』；

translations.literal: reading Mencius's books, one saying: 'Just strive to do good';
translations.idiomatic: reading Mencius's books, one saying: 'Just strive to do good';

sentences.zh: 讀朱子書，得一言，曰『切己體察』。」

translations.literal: reading Zhu Xi's books, one saying: 'Apply it to yourself and examine it closely.'
translations.idiomatic: reading Zhu Xi's books, one saying: 'Apply it to yourself and examine it closely.'

sentences.zh: 著有《四書擇粹》十二卷，《孝經考異選註》二卷，《救荒備覽》四卷，《荷經堂古文詩稿》四卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Selected Essentials of the Four Books in twelve juan, Selected Commentary on Textual Variants in the Classic of Filial Piety in two juan, Comprehensive Guide to Famine Relief in four juan, and Ancient Prose and Poetry Drafts from the Hejing Hall in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Selected Essentials of the Four Books in twelve juan, Selected Commentary on Textual Variants in the Classic of Filial Piety in two juan, Comprehensive Guide to Famine Relief in four juan, and Ancient Prose and Poetry Drafts from the Hejing Hall in four juan.

sentences.zh: 勞史，字麟書，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Lao Shi, courtesy name Linshu, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Lao Shi, styled Linshu, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 世為農。

translations.literal: His family were farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family were farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 少就傅讀書，長躬耕養父母，夜則披卷莊誦。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with a teacher; grown, he plowed the fields to support his parents, and at night spread his books and read aloud with solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied with a teacher; grown, he plowed the fields to support his parents, and at night spread his books and read aloud with solemnity.

sentences.zh: 讀朱子小學、中庸序，慨然發憤，以道自任，舉動必依於禮。

translations.literal: Reading Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning and the Preface to the Doctrine of the Mean, he sighed and resolved in indignation to take the Way upon himself; in every action he adhered to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Zhu Xi's Elementary Learning and the Preface to the Doctrine of the Mean, he sighed and resolved in indignation to take the Way upon himself; in every action he adhered to ritual.

sentences.zh: 繼讀朱子近思錄，立起設香案，北面稽首曰：「吾師在是矣！」

translations.literal: Then reading Zhu Xi's Reflections on Things Near at Hand, he immediately rose, set out an incense table, bowed facing north, and said: "My teacher is here!
translations.idiomatic: Then reading Zhu Xi's Reflections on Things Near at Hand, he immediately rose, set out an incense table, bowed facing north, and said: "My teacher is here!

sentences.zh: 常自刻責，謂：「天之命我者，若君之詔臣，父之詔子。

translations.literal: He constantly reproached himself, saying: "Heaven's charge to me is like a lord's command to a minister, a father's command to a son.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly reproached himself, saying: "Heaven's charge to me is like a lord's command to a minister, a father's command to a son.

sentences.zh: 一廢職，即膺嚴譴，一墜家業，即窮無所歸，可不慎哉！」

translations.literal: One dereliction of duty brings severe reproof; one ruin of the family estate leaves one with nowhere to return—can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: One dereliction of duty brings severe reproof; one ruin of the family estate leaves one with nowhere to return—can one not be cautious!

sentences.zh: 其論學以為始於不妄語，不妄動，即極諸至誠無息。

translations.literal: His teaching held that it begins with not speaking falsely and not acting rashly—that is the utmost of utmost sincerity without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching held that it begins with not speaking falsely and not acting rashly—that is the utmost of utmost sincerity without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 接後學，委曲進誠，雖傭工下隸皆引之鄉道，曰：「盡爾職分，務實做去，終身不懈，即聖賢矣。

translations.literal: In receiving later students he tactfully led them with sincerity; even hired laborers and low servants he guided toward the Way, saying: "Fulfill your duties, earnestly act them out, never slacken all your life—that is to be a sage.
translations.idiomatic: In receiving later students he tactfully led them with sincerity; even hired laborers and low servants he guided toward the Way, saying: "Fulfill your duties, earnestly act them out, never slacken all your life—that is to be a sage.

sentences.zh: 勿過自薄也。」

translations.literal: Do not undervalue yourself too much.
translations.idiomatic: Do not undervalue yourself too much.

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不爽然。

translations.literal: Those who heard were all refreshed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard were all refreshed.

sentences.zh: 里中負販者近史居，不敢貨偽物。

translations.literal: Peddlers in the village near Shi's dwelling dared not sell counterfeit goods.
translations.idiomatic: Peddlers in the village near Shi's dwelling dared not sell counterfeit goods.

sentences.zh: 芻兒牧童或折棄矰繳，毀機穽。

translations.literal: Herdboys and shepherd boys sometimes broke and discarded crossbow strings and destroyed snares.
translations.idiomatic: Herdboys and shepherd boys sometimes broke and discarded crossbow strings and destroyed snares.

sentences.zh: 有鬥爭，就史質，往往置酒求解。

translations.literal: When there were quarrels they went to Shi for judgment; often he set out wine to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: When there were quarrels they went to Shi for judgment; often he set out wine to reconcile them.

sentences.zh: 門人桑調元自錢塘來謁，論學數日。

translations.literal: His disciple Sang Diaoyuan came from Qiantang to visit him; they discussed learning for several days.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Sang Diaoyuan came from Qiantang to visit him; they discussed learning for several days.

sentences.zh: 將別，送之曰：「吾壽不過三年，恐不復相見。

translations.literal: When about to part, he saw him off saying: "My life will not exceed three years; I fear we shall not meet again.
translations.idiomatic: When about to part, he saw him off saying: "My life will not exceed three years; I fear we shall not meet again.

sentences.zh: 行矣勉之！」

translations.literal: Go, and exert yourself!
translations.idiomatic: Go, and exert yourself!

sentences.zh: 後三年九月，謂門人汪鑑曰：「不過今月，吾將去矣！」

translations.literal: Three years later, in the ninth month, he told his disciple Wang Jian: "Before this month is out, I shall depart!
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, in the ninth month, he told his disciple Wang Jian: "Before this month is out, I shall depart!

sentences.zh: 遂遍詣親友家，與老者言所以教，少者言所以學，令家人治木飭後事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he visited every friend and kinsman's home, telling the old what to teach and the young what to learn, and ordered his family to prepare wood and arrange funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he visited every friend and kinsman's home, telling the old what to teach and the young what to learn, and ordered his family to prepare wood and arrange funeral affairs.

sentences.zh: 晦前一夕，沐浴更衣，移榻正寢，炳燭晏坐如平時，旋就寢。

translations.literal: On the eve of the last day of the month he bathed, changed clothes, moved his couch to the main bedchamber, lit candles and sat at ease as in ordinary times, then went to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the last day of the month he bathed, changed clothes, moved his couch to the main bedchamber, lit candles and sat at ease as in ordinary times, then went to sleep.

sentences.zh: 明晨，撫之冰矣。

translations.literal: At dawn next morning, when touched he was cold as ice.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn next morning, when touched he was cold as ice.

sentences.zh: 調元為刻其遺書十卷，其書謂易之為道，細無不該，遠無不屆，故多本易理以推人物之性。

translations.literal: Diaoyuan printed his posthumous writings in ten juan; the book holds that the Way of the Changes embraces the minute without omission and reaches afar without limit, so he often based himself on Changes principles to infer human nature.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoyuan printed his posthumous writings in ten juan; the book holds that the Way of the Changes embraces the minute without omission and reaches afar without limit, so he often based himself on Changes principles to infer human nature.

sentences.zh: 調元，字弢甫，錢塘人，為孝子天顯之子。

translations.literal: Diaoyuan, courtesy name Taofu, was a native of Qiantang and the son of the filial son Tianxian.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoyuan, styled Taofu, came from Qiantang and was the son of the filial son Tianxian.

sentences.zh: 天顯親病革，合羊脂和粥以進。

translations.literal: When Tianxian's parent was critically ill, he mixed mutton fat into gruel and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxian's parent was critically ill, he mixed mutton fat into gruel and presented it.

sentences.zh: 親死，抱鐺而哭，人為繪抱鐺圖。

translations.literal: When the parent died he embraced the cauldron and wept; people painted the picture Embracing the Cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: When the parent died he embraced the cauldron and wept; people painted the picture Embracing the Cauldron.

sentences.zh: 調元受業於史，得聞性理之學，

translations.literal: Diaoyuan received instruction from Shi and heard the learning of human nature and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoyuan received instruction from Shi and heard the learning of human nature and principle.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，召試通知性理，欽賜進士，授工部主事，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, he was summoned to examination on Neo-Confucian principle, granted jinshi by imperial favor, appointed principal clerk in the Board of Works, and returned on plea of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, he was summoned to examination on Neo-Confucian principle, granted jinshi by imperial favor, appointed principal clerk in the Board of Works, and returned on plea of illness.

sentences.zh: 調元主九江濂溪書院，構須友堂，祠餘山先生，以著淵源有自，餘山，史自號也。

translations.literal: Diaoyuan headed the Lianxi Academy at Jiujiang, built the Hall of Needing Friends, and sacrificed to Master Yushan to show lineage with clear source—Yushan was Shi's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: Diaoyuan headed the Lianxi Academy at Jiujiang, built the Hall of Needing Friends, and sacrificed to Master Yushan to show lineage with clear source—Yushan was Shi's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 調元東皋別業又辟餘山書屋，以友教四方之士。

translations.literal: At his Donggao country estate Diaoyuan also opened the Yushan Book Hall to befriend and teach scholars from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At his Donggao country estate Diaoyuan also opened the Yushan Book Hall to befriend and teach scholars from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 為人清鯁絕俗，足跡遍五嶽。

translations.literal: As a man he was pure, upright, and aloof from the vulgar; his footsteps reached all Five Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he was pure, upright, and aloof from the vulgar; his footsteps reached all Five Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 晚主灤源書院，益暢師說。

translations.literal: In later years he headed the Luanyuan Academy and further expounded his master's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he headed the Luanyuan Academy and further expounded his master's teaching.

sentences.zh: 鑒，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Jian was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 父死於雲南，鑒護喪歸至漢川，遇大風，舟且覆，抱棺大哭，誓以身殉。

translations.literal: His father died in Yunnan; Jian escorted the coffin home to Hanchuan, met a great wind, the boat nearly capsized; he embraced the coffin and wept aloud, vowing to die with it.
translations.idiomatic: His father died in Yunnan; Jian escorted the coffin home to Hanchuan, met a great wind, the boat nearly capsized; he embraced the coffin and wept aloud, vowing to die with it.

sentences.zh: 忽風回得泊沙渚，眾呼為孝子。

translations.literal: Suddenly the wind turned and they moored on a sandbar; the crowd called him a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the wind turned and they moored on a sandbar; the crowd called him a filial son.

sentences.zh: 為人尚氣節，史戒之曰：「英氣，客氣也。

translations.literal: As a man he valued moral fiber; Shi admonished him: "Heroic spirit is guest spirit.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he valued moral fiber; Shi admonished him: "Heroic spirit is guest spirit.

sentences.zh: 其以問學融化之。」

translations.literal: Use learning to melt it away.
translations.idiomatic: Use learning to melt it away.

sentences.zh: 史之歿也，鑒實左右焉。

translations.literal: When Shi died, Jian was truly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, Jian was truly at his side.

sentences.zh: 顧棟高，字震滄，無錫人。

translations.literal: Gu Donggao, courtesy name Zhencang, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Donggao, styled Zhencang, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: In the 60 year of Kangxi, a jinshi, appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the 60 year of Kangxi, a jinshi, appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 雍正間，引見，以奏對越次罷職，

translations.literal: During the Yongzheng reign he was presented to the throne; because his memorial replies overstepped protocol he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign he was presented to the throne; because his memorial replies overstepped protocol he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十五年，特詔內外大臣薦舉經明行修之士，所舉四十餘人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Qianlong, an special edict ordered inner and outer ministers to recommend scholars clear in the classics and upright in conduct; more than forty were recommended.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Qianlong, a special edict ordered inner and outer ministers to recommend scholars clear in the classics and upright in conduct; more than forty were recommended.

sentences.zh: 惟大學士張廷玉、尚書王安國、侍郎歸宣光舉江南舉人陳祖範，尚書汪由敦舉江南舉人吳鼎，侍郎錢陳群舉山西舉人梁錫璵，大理寺卿鄒一桂舉棟高，此四人，論者謂名實允孚焉。

translations.literal: Only Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu, Minister Wang Anguo, and Vice Minister Gui Xuanguang recommended the Jiangnan provincial graduate Chen Zufan; Minister Wang Youdun recommended the Jiangnan provincial graduate Wu Ding; Vice Minister Qian Chenqun recommended the Shanxi provincial graduate Liang Xiyu; and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zou Yigui recommended Donggao—these four, commentators said, matched name and reality.
translations.idiomatic: Only Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu, Minister Wang Anguo, and Vice Minister Gui Xuanguang recommended the Jiangnan provincial graduate Chen Zufan; Minister Wang Youdun recommended the Jiangnan provincial graduate Wu Ding; Vice Minister Qian Chenqun recommended the Shanxi provincial graduate Liang Xiyu; and Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Zou Yigui recommended Donggao—these four, commentators said, matched name and reality.

sentences.zh: 尋皆授國子監司業。

translations.literal: Soon all were appointed vice directors of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were appointed vice directors of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 棟高以年老不任職，賜司業銜。

translations.literal: Donggao, on account of old age, could not take office and was granted the rank of vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Donggao, on account of old age, could not take office and was granted the rank of vice director.

sentences.zh: 皇太后萬壽，棟高入京祝嘏，召見，拜起令內侍扶掖。

translations.literal: On the empress dowager's birthday Donggao entered the capital to offer congratulations, was summoned for audience, and when bowing and rising was supported by inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's birthday Donggao entered the capital to offer congratulations, was summoned for audience, and when bowing and rising was supported by inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 棟高奏對，首及吳敝俗，請以節儉風示海內，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In his memorial reply Donggao first spoke of the vulgar customs of Wu and asked that frugality be displayed to the empire; the emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial reply Donggao first spoke of the vulgar customs of Wu and asked that frugality be displayed to the empire; the emperor commended this.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，賜七言律詩二章。

translations.literal: On taking leave from audience he was granted two regulated poems in seven characters.
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave from audience he was granted two regulated poems in seven characters.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，南巡，召見行在，加祭酒銜，賜御書「傳經耆碩」四字。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, during the southern tour, he was summoned to audience at the temporary palace, given the additional rank of libationer, and granted the imperial inscription "Venerable Master Who Transmits the Classics" in four characters.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, during the southern tour, he was summoned to audience at the temporary palace, given the additional rank of libationer, and granted the imperial inscription "Venerable Master Who Transmits the Classics" in four characters.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒於家，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died at home, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he died at home, aged eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 所學合宋、元、明諸儒門徑而一之，援新安以合金谿，為調停之說。

translations.literal: His learning united the paths of Song, Yuan, and Ming Confucians into one, using Xin'an to harmonize with Jinxi—a mediating doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: His learning united the paths of Song, Yuan, and Ming Confucians into one, using Xin'an to harmonize with Jinxi—a mediating doctrine.

sentences.zh: 著大儒粹語二十八卷，又著春秋大事表百三十一篇，條理詳明，議論精覈，多發前人所未發。

translations.literal: He wrote Pure Sayings of Great Confucians in twenty-eight juan, and also Major Events Tables for the Spring and Autumn Annals in 131 sections—detailed in arrangement, precise in argument, often developing what predecessors had not.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Pure Sayings of Great Confucians in twenty-eight juan, and also Major Events Tables for the Spring and Autumn Annals in 131 sections—detailed in arrangement, precise in argument, often developing what predecessors had not.

sentences.zh: 毛詩類釋二十一卷，續編三卷，採錄舊說，發明經義，頗為謹嚴。

translations.literal: Classified Explanations of the Mao Odes in twenty-one juan with a continuation in three juan collected old interpretations and clarified the classics, and was quite rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Classified Explanations of the Mao Odes in twenty-one juan with a continuation in three juan collected old interpretations and clarified the classics, and was quite rigorous.

sentences.zh: 其尚書質疑二卷，多據臆斷，不足以言心得。

translations.literal: His Doubts on the Documents in two juan relied mostly on conjecture and is insufficient to speak of genuine insight.
translations.idiomatic: His Doubts on the Documents in two juan relied mostly on conjecture and is insufficient to speak of genuine insight.

sentences.zh: 大抵棟高窮經之功，春秋為最，而書則用力少也。

translations.literal: Generally Donggao's effort in exhausting the classics was greatest in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and least in the Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Generally Donggao's effort in exhausting the classics was greatest in the Spring and Autumn Annals, and least in the Documents.

sentences.zh: 陳祖範，字亦韓，常熟人。

translations.literal: Chen Zufan, courtesy name Yihan, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zufan, styled Yihan, came from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年舉人，其秋禮部中式，以病不與殿試。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, a provincial graduate; that autumn he passed the Ministry of Rites examination but, owing to illness, did not attend the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng, a provincial graduate; that autumn he passed the Ministry of Rites examination but, owing to illness, did not attend the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 歸，僦廛華匯之濱，楗戶讀書。

translations.literal: Returning home, he rented a shop on the bank of Huahui, barred his door, and read.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he rented a shop on the bank of Huahui, barred his door, and read.

sentences.zh: 居數年，詔天下設書院以教士，大吏爭延為師，訓課有法。

translations.literal: After several years an edict ordered academies established throughout the empire to teach scholars; great officials competed to invite him as teacher, and his instruction had method.
translations.idiomatic: After several years an edict ordered academies established throughout the empire to teach scholars; great officials competed to invite him as teacher, and his instruction had method.

sentences.zh: 或一二年輒辭去，曰：「士習難醇，師道難立。

translations.literal: After a year or two he always resigned, saying: "Scholarly habits are hard to refine; the teacher's Way is hard to establish.
translations.idiomatic: After a year or two he always resigned, saying: "Scholarly habits are hard to refine; the teacher's Way is hard to establish.

sentences.zh: 且此席似宋時祠祿，仕而不遂者處焉。

translations.literal: Moreover this chair resembles the stipends of Song times—a place for those who sought office but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover this chair resembles the stipends of Song times—a place for those who sought office but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 吾不求仕，而久與其列為汗顏耳。」

translations.literal: I do not seek office, yet to long remain in their ranks shames me.
translations.idiomatic: I do not seek office, yet to long remain in their ranks shames me.

sentences.zh: 薦舉經學，祖範褒然居首。

translations.literal: When classics learning was recommended, Zufan stood foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When classics learning was recommended, Zufan stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 以年老不任職，賜司業銜，

translations.literal: On account of old age he could not take office and was granted the rank of vice director.
translations.idiomatic: On account of old age he could not take office and was granted the rank of vice director.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十八年，卒於家，年七十有九。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong, he died at home, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Qianlong, he died at home, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 所撰述有經咫一卷，膺薦時錄呈御覽。

translations.literal: His writings include A Span of the Classics in one juan, recorded and presented for imperial viewing when he was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include A Span of the Classics in one juan, recorded and presented for imperial viewing when he was recommended.

sentences.zh: 文集四卷，詩集四卷，掌錄二卷。

translations.literal: Collected Writings in four juan, Collected Poems in four juan, and Recorded Discourses in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Writings in four juan, Collected Poems in four juan, and Recorded Discourses in two juan.

sentences.zh: 祖範於學務求心得，論易不取先天之學，論書不取梅賾，論詩不廢​​小序，論春秋不取義例，論禮不以古制違人情，皆通達之論。

translations.literal: In learning Zufan sought genuine insight; on the Changes he rejected Prior Heaven learning, on the Documents he rejected Mei Ze, on the Odes he did not discard the small prefaces, on the Spring and Autumn Annals he rejected principle-categories, on the Rituals he did not let ancient institutions violate human feeling—all penetrating views.
translations.idiomatic: In learning Zufan sought genuine insight; on the Changes he rejected Prior Heaven learning, on the Documents he rejected Mei Ze, on the Odes he did not discard the small prefaces, on the Spring and Autumn Annals he rejected principle-categories, on the Rituals he did not let ancient institutions violate human feeling—all penetrating views.

sentences.zh: 同縣顧主事鎮傳其學。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Gu Zhen of the Secretariat transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Gu Zhen of the Secretariat transmitted his learning.

sentences.zh: 吳鼎，字尊彝，金匱人。

translations.literal: Wu Ding, courtesy name Zunyi, was a native of Jingui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ding, styled Zunyi, came from Jingui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆九年舉人，授司業。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate, appointed vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Qianlong, a provincial graduate, appointed vice director.

sentences.zh: 洊擢翰林院侍講學士，轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting, then transferred to expositor-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly promoted to Hanlin reader-in-waiting, then transferred to expositor-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 大考降左春坊左贊善，遷翰林院侍講，旋休致。

translations.literal: In the grand evaluation demoted to left assistant in the Eastern Palace, transferred to Hanlin reader, and soon retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the grand evaluation demoted to left assistant in the Eastern Palace, transferred to Hanlin reader, and soon retired.

sentences.zh: 所撰有易例舉要二卷，十家易象集說九十卷。

translations.literal: His writings include Essential Examples of the Changes in two juan and Collected Explanations of the Images from Ten Masters of the Changes in ninety juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include Essential Examples of the Changes in two juan and Collected Explanations of the Images from Ten Masters of the Changes in ninety juan.

sentences.zh: 裒宋俞琰、元龍仁夫、明來知德等十家易說，以繼李鼎祚、董楷之後。

translations.literal: He gathered the Changes interpretations of ten masters—Song Yu Yan, Yuan Long Renfu, Ming Lai Zhide, and others—to continue after Li Dingzuo and Dong Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the Changes interpretations of ten masters—Song Yu Yan, Yuan Long Renfu, Ming Lai Zhide, and others—to continue after Li Dingzuo and Dong Kai.

sentences.zh: 其東莞學案，則專攻陳建學蔀通辨作也。

translations.literal: His Case Study of Dongguan was written specifically to attack Chen Jian's Learning Ramparts and Comprehensive Discrimination.
translations.idiomatic: His Case Study of Dongguan was written specifically to attack Chen Jian's Learning Ramparts and Comprehensive Discrimination.

sentences.zh: 兄鼐，亦通經，深於易、三禮。

translations.literal: His elder brother Nai also mastered the classics and was deep in the Changes and the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Nai also mastered the classics and was deep in the Changes and the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 梁錫璵，字確軒，介休人。

translations.literal: Liang Xiyu, courtesy name Quexuan, was a native of Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xiyu, styled Quexuan, came from Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年舉人，亦授司業，與吳鼎同食俸辦事，不為定員。

translations.literal: In Yongzheng year two he became a provincial graduate; he too was appointed director of studies and served on salary together with Wu Ding, without being made a regular appointee.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year two he became a provincial graduate; he too was appointed director of studies and served on salary together with Wu Ding, without being made a regular appointee.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，命直上書房，累遷詹事府少詹事。

translations.literal: In Qianlong year seventeen, he was ordered to serve directly in the Upper Study and rose successively to junior supervisor in the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year seventeen, he was ordered to serve directly in the Upper Study and rose successively to junior supervisor in the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大考降左庶子，擢祭酒，坐遺失書籍鐫級。

translations.literal: In the grand evaluation demoted to left assistant tutor, promoted to libationer, then reduced in rank for losing books.
translations.idiomatic: In the grand evaluation demoted to left assistant tutor, promoted to libationer, then reduced in rank for losing books.

sentences.zh: 膺薦時，以所撰易經揆一呈御覽。

translations.literal: When recommended he presented his Harmonizing Unity of the Classic of Changes for imperial viewing.
translations.idiomatic: When recommended he presented his Harmonizing Unity of the Classic of Changes for imperial viewing.

sentences.zh: 鼎、錫璵並蒙召對，面諭曰：「汝等以是大學士、九卿公保經學，朕所以用汝等去教人。

translations.literal: Ding and Xiyu were both summoned for audience and personally instructed: "You were recommended for classics learning by grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers—that is why I employ you to teach others.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and Xiyu were both summoned for audience and personally instructed: "You were recommended for classics learning by grand secretaries and the Nine Ministers—that is why I employ you to teach others.

sentences.zh: 是汝等積學所致，不是他途幸進。」

translations.literal: This comes from your accumulated learning, not advancement by other paths.
translations.idiomatic: This comes from your accumulated learning, not advancement by other paths.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「窮經為讀書根本。

translations.literal: He also said: "Exhausting the classics is the root of reading.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Exhausting the classics is the root of reading.

sentences.zh: 但窮經不徒在口耳，須要躬行實踐。

translations.literal: But exhausting the classics is not merely in ear and mouth—you must personally practice it.
translations.idiomatic: But exhausting the classics is not merely in ear and mouth—you must personally practice it.

sentences.zh: 汝等自己躬行實踐，方能教人躬行實踐。」

translations.literal: Only when you yourselves personally practice can you teach others to personally practice.
translations.idiomatic: Only when you yourselves personally practice can you teach others to personally practice.

sentences.zh: 鼎、錫璵頓首祇謝。

translations.literal: Ding and Xiyu bowed their heads in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and Xiyu bowed their heads in thanks.

sentences.zh: 又奉諭：「吳鼎、梁錫璵所著經學，著派翰林二十員、中書二十員，在武英殿各謄寫一部進呈。

translations.literal: They also received instruction: "The classics learning written by Wu Ding and Liang Xiyu—assign twenty Hanlin members and twenty secretaries each to copy one set in the Hall of Military Glory and present it.
translations.idiomatic: They also received instruction: "The classics learning written by Wu Ding and Liang Xiyu—assign twenty Hanlin members and twenty secretaries each to copy one set in the Hall of Military Glory and present it.

sentences.zh: 原書給還本人。

translations.literal: Return the original books to the authors.
translations.idiomatic: Return the original books to the authors.

sentences.zh: 所有紙札、飯食皆給於官。

translations.literal: All paper and meals are supplied by the government.
translations.idiomatic: All paper and meals are supplied by the government.

sentences.zh: 著梁詩正、劉統勳董理其事。」

translations.literal: Assign Liang Shizheng and Liu Tongxun to supervise the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Assign Liang Shizheng and Liu Tongxun to supervise the matter.

sentences.zh: 稽古之榮，海內所未有也。

translations.literal: Such honor for revering antiquity was unprecedented within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Such honor for revering antiquity was unprecedented within the seas.

sentences.zh: 孟超然，字朝舉，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Meng Chaoran, courtesy name Chaoju, was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chaoran, styled Chaoju, came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年進士，選庶吉士，改兵部主事，累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, changed to principal clerk in the Board of War, and repeatedly promoted to director in the Board of Civil Officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong, a jinshi, selected as Hanlin bachelor, changed to principal clerk in the Board of War, and repeatedly promoted to director in the Board of Civil Officials.

sentences.zh: 三十年，典廣西試，尋督學四川，廉正不阿，遇士有禮。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he served as chief examiner of Guangxi, then as educational commissioner of Sichuan—incorrupt and unyielding, treating scholars with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he served as chief examiner of Guangxi, then as educational commissioner of Sichuan—incorrupt and unyielding, treating scholars with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 以蜀民父子兄弟異居者眾，作厚俗論以箴其失。

translations.literal: Because many Shu people lived separately as fathers, sons, and brothers, he wrote On Thickening Custom to admonish the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Because many Shu people lived separately as fathers, sons, and brothers, he wrote On Thickening Custom to admonish the fault.

sentences.zh: 旋以親老，請急歸，年甫四十二，遂不出。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of aged parents, he requested urgent leave to return; he was only forty-two and never went out again.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of aged parents, he requested urgent leave to return; he was only forty-two and never went out again.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，侍父疾，躬執廁牏。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; when serving his father's illness he personally attended the privy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; when serving his father's illness he personally attended the privy.

sentences.zh: 戚族喪娶，雖空乏必應。

translations.literal: For kinsmen's funerals and weddings, however empty his means he always responded.
translations.idiomatic: For kinsmen's funerals and weddings, however empty his means he always responded.

sentences.zh: 嘗嘆服徐陵「我輩猶有車可賣」之言。

translations.literal: He once sighed in admiration at Xu Ling's words: "We still have a carriage to sell."
translations.idiomatic: He once sighed in admiration at Xu Ling's words: "We still have a carriage to sell."

sentences.zh: 其學以懲忿、窒慾、改過、遷善為主。

translations.literal: His learning took restraining anger, checking desire, correcting faults, and moving toward good as its main themes.
translations.idiomatic: His learning took restraining anger, checking desire, correcting faults, and moving toward good as its main themes.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「變化氣質，當學呂成公；

translations.literal: He once said: "To transform temperament, one should study Master Lu Chenggong;
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "To transform temperament, one should study Master Lu Chenggong;

sentences.zh: 刻意自責，當學吳聘君。」

translations.literal: to reproach oneself deliberately, one should study Master Wu Pingjun.
translations.idiomatic: to reproach oneself deliberately, one should study Master Wu Pingjun.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「談性命，則先儒之書已詳，不如歸諸實踐；

translations.literal: He also said: "On human nature and Heaven's mandate, the books of earlier Confucians are already detailed—better to return to practical conduct;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "On human nature and Heaven's mandate, the books of earlier Confucians are already detailed—better to return to practical conduct;

sentences.zh: 博見聞，則將衰之年無及，不如反諸身心。」

translations.literal: for broad learning, the declining years have no time—better to turn back to body and heart.
translations.idiomatic: for broad learning, the declining years have no time—better to turn back to body and heart.

sentences.zh: 其讀商子云：「論至德者，不和於俗；

translations.literal: Reading the Book of Lord Shang he noted: "Those who discuss supreme virtue do not harmonize with custom;
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Book of Lord Shang he noted: "Those who discuss supreme virtue do not harmonize with custom;

sentences.zh: 成大功者，不謀於眾。

translations.literal: those who achieve great merit do not consult the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: those who achieve great merit do not consult the multitude.

sentences.zh: 聖人苟可以強國，不法其故，苟可以利民，不循其禮，以為此王介甫之先驅也。

translations.literal: If a sage can strengthen the state, he need not follow old ways; if he can benefit the people, he need not observe old ritual—he took this as the forerunner of Wang Jiepu.
translations.idiomatic: If a sage can strengthen the state, he need not follow old ways; if he can benefit the people, he need not observe old ritual—he took this as the forerunner of Wang Jiepu.

sentences.zh: 然鞅猶明於帝王霸之說，介甫乃以言利為堯、舜、周公之道，又鞅之不如矣。」

translations.literal: Yet Shang Yang still understood the doctrines of emperors, kings, and hegemons; Jiepu took speaking of profit as the Way of Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou—he fell even below Shang Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shang Yang still understood the doctrines of emperors, kings, and hegemons; Jiepu took speaking of profit as the Way of Yao, Shun, and the Duke of Zhou—he fell even below Shang Yang.

sentences.zh: 其論楊時云：「龜山得伊、洛之正傳，開道南之先聲。

translations.literal: On Yang Shi he wrote: "Guishan received the orthodox transmission of Cheng and Luo and opened the first voice of the Southern Way.
translations.idiomatic: On Yang Shi he wrote: "Guishan received the orthodox transmission of Cheng and Luo and opened the first voice of the Southern Way.

sentences.zh: 然為人身後文，如溫州陳君、李子約、許德佔、張進、孫龍圖諸墓誌，往往述及釋氏之學，而讚之曰『安』、曰『定』、曰『靜』，毋惑乎後之學者，援儒入墨，紛紛不已也。」

translations.literal: Yet in posthumous writings for others, such as the tomb inscriptions for Master Chen of Wenzhou, Li Ziyue, Xu Dezhan, Zhang Jin, and Sun Longtu, he often described Buddhist learning and praised it as 'peace,' 'stillness,' and 'quiet'—no wonder later scholars endlessly drew Confucianism toward Mohism."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in posthumous writings for others, such as the tomb inscriptions for Master Chen of Wenzhou, Li Ziyue, Xu Dezhan, Zhang Jin, and Sun Longtu, he often described Buddhist learning and praised it as 'peace,' 'stillness,' and 'quiet'—no wonder later scholars endlessly drew Confucianism toward Mohism."

sentences.zh: 超然性靜，家居杜門卻掃。

translations.literal: Chaoran was quiet by nature; at home he shut his door and swept away visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoran was quiet by nature; at home he shut his door and swept away visitors.

sentences.zh: 久之，巡撫徐嗣曾請主鼇峰書院，倡明正學。

translations.literal: After long time Governor Xu Sizeng asked him to head the Aofeng Academy and advocate orthodox learning.
translations.idiomatic: After long time Governor Xu Sizeng asked him to head the Aofeng Academy and advocate orthodox learning.

sentences.zh: 閩之學者，以安溪李光地、寧化雷鋐為最。

translations.literal: Among Fujian scholars, Li Guangdi of Anxi and Lei Hong of Ninghua were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among Fujian scholars, Li Guangdi of Anxi and Lei Hong of Ninghua were foremost.

sentences.zh: 超然輩行稍後，而讀書有識，不為俗學所牽，則後先一揆也。

translations.literal: Chaoran's generation came slightly later, but in reading he had discernment and was not pulled by vulgar learning—in earlier and later they were of one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoran's generation came slightly later, but in reading he had discernment and was not pulled by vulgar learning—in earlier and later they were of one measure.

sentences.zh: 居喪時，考士喪禮、荀子及宋司馬光、程子、朱子說，並採近代諸儒言論，以正閩俗喪葬之失，著喪禮輯略二卷。

translations.literal: During mourning he studied the Scholar's Mourning Rites, Xunzi, and the accounts of Song Sima Guang, Master Cheng, and Master Zhu, and gathered recent Confucians' words to correct Fujian customs in funerals and burial, writing Abridged Mourning Rites in two juan.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he studied the Scholar's Mourning Rites, Xunzi, and the accounts of Song Sima Guang, Master Cheng, and Master Zhu, and gathered recent Confucians' words to correct Fujian customs in funerals and burial, writing Abridged Mourning Rites in two juan.

sentences.zh: 傷不葬其親者惑形家言以速禍，取孟子「掩之誠是」之語，作誠是錄一卷。

translations.literal: Grieved that those who did not bury their parents were misled by geomancers' words to hasten disaster, he took Mencius's phrase 'to cover them is truly right' and wrote Record of True Rightness in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: Grieved that those who did not bury their parents were misled by geomancers' words to hasten disaster, he took Mencius's phrase 'to cover them is truly right' and wrote Record of True Rightness in one juan.

sentences.zh: 他著有焚香錄、觀復錄、晚聞錄。

translations.literal: His other works include Record of Burning Incense, Record of Returning to the Origin, and Record of Late Hearings.
translations.idiomatic: His other works include Record of Burning Incense, Record of Returning to the Origin, and Record of Late Hearings.

sentences.zh: 汪紱，初名烜，字燦人，婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Fu, original name Xuan, courtesy name Canren, was a native of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, original name Xuan, styled Canren, came from Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate.

sentences.zh: 少禀母教，八歲，四子書、五經悉成誦。

translations.literal: In youth he received his mother's teaching; at eight he could recite the Four Books and Five Classics entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he received his mother's teaching; at eight he could recite the Four Books and Five Classics entirely.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父淹滯江寧，侍母疾累年，十日未嘗一飽。

translations.literal: The family was poor; his father lingered in Jiangning; he attended his mother's illness for years and went ten days without a full meal.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; his father lingered in Jiangning; he attended his mother's illness for years and went ten days without a full meal.

sentences.zh: 母歿，紱走詣父，勸之歸。

translations.literal: When his mother died Fu ran to his father and urged him to return.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died Fu ran to his father and urged him to return.

sentences.zh: 父曰：「昔人言家徒四壁，吾壁亦屬人。

translations.literal: His father said: "People say 'only four bare walls'—my walls too belong to others.
translations.idiomatic: His father said: "People say 'only four bare walls'—my walls too belong to others.

sentences.zh: 若持吾安歸？」

translations.literal: If you take me, where can I return?
translations.idiomatic: If you take me, where can I return?

sentences.zh: 叱之去。

translations.literal: He scolded him away.
translations.idiomatic: He scolded him away.

sentences.zh: 紱乃之江西景德鎮，畫碗，傭其間。

translations.literal: Fu then went to Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, painted bowls, and worked as a hired laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu then went to Jingdezhen in Jiangxi, painted bowls, and worked as a hired laborer.

sentences.zh: 然稱母喪，不御酒肉。

translations.literal: Yet he observed mourning for his mother and did not partake of wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he observed mourning for his mother and did not partake of wine or meat.

sentences.zh: 後飄泊至閩中，為童子師。

translations.literal: Later he drifted to Fujian and became a schoolteacher for boys.
translations.idiomatic: Later he drifted to Fujian and became a schoolteacher for boys.

sentences.zh: 及授學浦城，從者日進。

translations.literal: When he taught at Pucheng, followers increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: When he taught at Pucheng, followers increased daily.

sentences.zh: 聞父歿，一慟幾殆，即日奔喪，迎櫬歸。

translations.literal: When he heard his father had died he grieved nearly to death; that very day he rushed to mourning and brought the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard his father had died he grieved nearly to death; that very day he rushed to mourning and brought the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 紱自二十後，務博覽，著書十餘萬言，三十後儘燒之。

translations.literal: From twenty on Fu sought broad reading and wrote more than a hundred thousand words; after thirty he burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: From twenty on Fu sought broad reading and wrote more than a hundred thousand words; after thirty he burned them all.

sentences.zh: 自是凡有述作，凝神直書。

translations.literal: Thereafter whenever he wrote he concentrated his spirit and wrote straight through.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter whenever he wrote he concentrated his spirit and wrote straight through.

sentences.zh: 自六經下逮樂律、天文、地輿、陣法、術數無不究暢，而一以宋五子之學為歸。

translations.literal: From the Six Classics down to pitch pipes, astronomy, geography, battle formations, and numerology—nothing he did not exhaust—and all returned to the learning of the Five Masters of Song.
translations.idiomatic: From the Six Classics down to pitch pipes, astronomy, geography, battle formations, and numerology—nothing he did not exhaust—and all returned to the learning of the Five Masters of Song.

sentences.zh: 著有易經詮義十五卷，尚書詮義十二卷，詩經詮義十五卷，四書詮義十五卷，詩韻析六卷，春秋集傳十六卷，禮記章句十卷、或問四卷，參讀禮志疑二卷，樂經律呂通解五卷，樂經或問三卷，孝經章句一卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Explanatory Meaning of the Classic of Changes in fifteen juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Documents in twelve juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Classic of Poetry in fifteen juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Four Books in fifteen juan, Analysis of Poetic Rhymes in six juan, Collected Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals in sixteen juan, Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Record of Rituals in ten juan with Questions in four juan, Doubts on Reading the Rituals in two juan, Comprehensive Explanation of Pitch Pipes in the Classic of Music in five juan, Questions on the Classic of Music in three juan, and Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Explanatory Meaning of the Classic of Changes in fifteen juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Documents in twelve juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Classic of Poetry in fifteen juan, Explanatory Meaning of the Four Books in fifteen juan, Analysis of Poetic Rhymes in six juan, Collected Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals in sixteen juan, Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Record of Rituals in ten juan with Questions in four juan, Doubts on Reading the Rituals in two juan, Comprehensive Explanation of Pitch Pipes in the Classic of Music in five juan, Questions on the Classic of Music in three juan, and Chapter and Sentence Commentary on the Classic of Filial Piety in one juan.

sentences.zh: 其參讀禮志疑多得經意，可與陸隴其書並存。

translations.literal: His Doubts on Reading the Rituals often grasped the classics' intent and can stand alongside Lu Longqi's book.
translations.idiomatic: His Doubts on Reading the Rituals often grasped the classics' intent and can stand alongside Lu Longqi's book.

sentences.zh: 紱之論學，謂學不可不知要。

translations.literal: In Fu's teaching on learning, he said one cannot fail to know essentials.
translations.idiomatic: In Fu's teaching on learning, he said one cannot fail to know essentials.

sentences.zh: 然所以得要，正須從學得多後，乃能揀擇出緊要處。

translations.literal: Yet to obtain essentials one must first learn much, then one can select what is crucial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to obtain essentials one must first learn much, then one can select what is crucial.

sentences.zh: 謂易理全在像、數上乘載而來。

translations.literal: He held that Changes principle is entirely borne on images and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Changes principle is entirely borne on images and numbers.

sentences.zh: 謂書歷象、禹貢、洪範須著力去考，都是經濟。

translations.literal: He held that in the Documents the calendar, stars, Yu's Tribute, and Great Plan must be studied with effort—all are statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: He held that in the Documents the calendar, stars, Yu's Tribute, and Great Plan must be studied with effort—all are statecraft.

sentences.zh: 謂詩只依字句吟詠，意味自出。

translations.literal: He held that in the Odes one need only chant by word and line and meaning emerges of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He held that in the Odes one need only chant by word and line and meaning emerges of itself.

sentences.zh: 謂看周禮，須得周公之心，乃於宏大處見治體之大，於瑣屑處見法度之詳。

translations.literal: He held that in reading the Rites of Zhou one must grasp the Duke of Zhou's heart—then in the grand one sees the greatness of governance, in the minute the detail of law.
translations.idiomatic: He held that in reading the Rites of Zhou one must grasp the Duke of Zhou's heart—then in the grand one sees the greatness of governance, in the minute the detail of law.

sentences.zh: 謂春秋非理明義精，殆未可學。

translations.literal: He held that the Spring and Autumn Annals cannot be studied unless principle is clear and meaning refined.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the Spring and Autumn Annals cannot be studied unless principle is clear and meaning refined.

sentences.zh: 謂「格物」之「格」訓「至」，如書言「格於上下」、「格於皇天」，皆「至到」之義。

translations.literal: He held that 'ge' in 'ge wu' is glossed as 'reach,' as the Documents says 'reach above and below' and 'reach to August Heaven'—all mean 'arrive at.'
translations.idiomatic: He held that 'ge' in 'ge wu' is glossed as 'reach,' as the Documents says 'reach above and below' and 'reach to August Heaven'—all mean 'arrive at.'

sentences.zh: 上文「致知」字為「推致」，則「格物」為「窮至物理」甚明。

translations.literal: Since 'extend knowledge' above means 'extend and reach,' then 'ge wu' as 'exhaustively reach physical principle' is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Since 'extend knowledge' above means 'extend and reach,' then 'ge wu' as 'exhaustively reach physical principle' is very clear.

sentences.zh: 謂「性與天道不可得聞」，直是不可得聞，陸、王家因早聞性天，而未嘗了悟，又果於自信，遺害後人也。

translations.literal: He held that 'human nature and Heaven's Way cannot be heard' means simply that they cannot be heard; the Lu and Wang schools because they heard nature and Heaven early yet never truly understood, and were firm in self-confidence, harmed later people.
translations.idiomatic: He held that 'human nature and Heaven's Way cannot be heard' means simply that they cannot be heard; the Lu and Wang schools because they heard nature and Heaven early yet never truly understood, and were firm in self-confidence, harmed later people.

sentences.zh: 謂周子言「一」，言「無欲」，程子言「主一」，言「無適」，微有不同。

translations.literal: He held that Master Zhou spoke of 'one' and 'without desire,' Master Cheng of 'holding to one' and 'without deviation'—slightly different.
translations.idiomatic: He held that Master Zhou spoke of 'one' and 'without desire,' Master Cheng of 'holding to one' and 'without deviation'—slightly different.

sentences.zh: 周子所謂「一」者天也，所謂「欲」者人也。

translations.literal: What Master Zhou called 'one' is Heaven; what he called 'desire' is human.
translations.idiomatic: What Master Zhou called 'one' is Heaven; what he called 'desire' is human.

sentences.zh: 純乎天，不參以人，一者即無欲也。

translations.literal: Pure Heaven without human admixture—one is without desire.
translations.idiomatic: Pure Heaven without human admixture—one is without desire.
